That separation is the\nwhole point: the README says chronicles can be PDF or DOCX, codex can be\nPDF or DOCX, and ephemera is \"mixed formats, including scanned pages\" -- so\n\"what folder is this file in\" and \"how do I read this file\" are two\ndifferent questions with two different answers, and conflating them (like\nthe first draft of this code did) breaks the moment a codex entry happens\nto be a PDF instead of a DOCX.\n\nEvery reader returns the same shape: (raw_text, tables, image_refs)\n  raw_text    : str            -- full extracted text, markdown-ish where possible\n  tables      : list[dict]     -- any field/value tables found, e.g. infoboxes,\n                                   codex registers\n  image_refs  : list[str]      -- paths/refs to embedded or linked images (kept\n                                   for 1A-style needs later; harmless for 1C)\n\nread_any() is the single entry point everything else should call --\nit looks at the file extension and dispatches to the right reader.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\ntry:\n    import pdfplumber\nexcept ImportError:\n    pdfplumber = None\n\ntry:\n    import pytesseract\n    from PIL import Image\nexcept ImportError:\n    pytesseract = None\n\n\nIMAGE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"!\\[([^\\]]*)\\]\\(([^)]+)\\)\")\n\n\ndef read_markdown(path: Path) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\".md files: plain read, no conversion needed. Wikilinks/infobox parsing\n    happen one layer up (entity_extraction.py) since that's markdown-specific\n    syntax, not something every format has.\"\"\"\n    text = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    image_refs = [m.group(2) for m in IMAGE_PATTERN.finditer(text)]\n    return text, [], image_refs\n\n\ndef read_docx(path: Path) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"\n    .docx files: read directly with python-docx, walking paragraphs and\n    tables IN DOCUMENT ORDER (python-docx doesn't do this by default --\n    .paragraphs and .tables are separate lists with position info lost,\n    so we walk the underlying XML body ourselves).\n\n    Originally this shelled out to `pandoc`, but pandoc is an extra system\n    install most people (especially on Windows) don't have on PATH. Doing\n    it natively in python-docx means one less thing anyone on the team\n    needs to install.\n\n    Headings (Word styles \"Heading 1/2/3\") are converted to markdown\n    '#'/'##'/'###' so the rest of the pipeline (split.py) doesn't need to\n    know or care that this text originally came from a .docx.\n\n    2-column tables (the \"Field | Value\" register pattern seen in every\n    codex sample) are converted to markdown pipe-table lines, inserted\n    into the text AT THE POSITION they appeared -- this keeps a table tied\n    to the correct entry after splitting, the same way it naturally would\n    be for a markdown source file.\n    \"\"\"\n    from docx import Document as DocxDocument\n    from docx.table import Table as DocxTable\n    from docx.text.paragraph import Paragraph as DocxParagraph\n    from docx.oxml.ns import qn\n\n    def iter_block_items(doc):\n        \"\"\"Yield paragraphs and tables in the order they appear in the body.\n        Standard python-docx recipe -- .paragraphs/.tables alone lose order.\"\"\"\n        for child in doc.element.body.iterchildren():\n            if child.tag == qn(\"w:p\"):\n                yield DocxParagraph(child, doc)\n            elif child.tag == qn(\"w:tbl\"):\n                yield DocxTable(child, doc)\n\n    doc = DocxDocument(str(path))\n    lines = []\n\n    for block in iter_block_items(doc):\n        if isinstance(block, DocxParagraph):\n            text = block.text\n            style_name = block.style.name if block.style else \"\"\n            heading_match = re.match(r\"Heading (\\d)\", style_name)\n            if heading_match and text.strip():\n                level = min(int(heading_match.group(1)), 3)\n                lines.append(\"#\" * level + \" \" + text.strip())\n            else:\n                lines.append(text)\n        elif isinstance(block, DocxTable):\n            for i, row in enumerate(block.rows):\n                if i == 0:\n                    continue  # first row is a label row (e.g. \"Classification | Record\"), not data\n                cells = [c.text.strip() for c in row.cells]\n                if len(cells) == 2 and cells[0]:\n                    lines.append(f\"| {cells[0]} | {cells[1]} |\")\n\n    text = \"\\n\".join(lines)\n    # Image extraction from .docx is out of scope for 1C (no image embedding\n    # needed in answers) -- worth revisiting if the team ever tackles 1A.\n    return text, [], []\n\n\ndef read_pdf(path: Path) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"\n    .pdf files: try normal text extraction first (pdfplumber). If a page\n    yields almost no text, it's very likely a \"simulated scan\" -- an image\n    of a page rather than real embedded text -- so we fall back to OCR via\n    pdftoppm (render page -> image) + pytesseract (image -> text).\n\n    This dual-path handles BOTH real text PDFs (ephemera prose, or a codex/\n    chronicle that happens to be PDF) AND scanned-page ephemera without\n    needing to know in advance which kind a given file is.\n    \"\"\"\n    if pdfplumber is None:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"pdfplumber not installed\")\n\n    text_parts = []\n    tables = []\n    needs_ocr_pages = []\n\n    with pdfplumber.open(str(path)) as pdf:\n        for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n            page_text = page.extract_text() or \"\"\n            if len(page_text.strip()) < 20:\n                # Almost no extractable text -> likely a scanned/image page.\n                needs_ocr_pages.append(i)\n            else:\n                text_parts.append(page_text)\n\n            for table in page.extract_tables():\n                # Turn a raw pdfplumber table (list of rows) into a field/value\n                # dict IF it looks like a 2-column register (matches the codex\n                # \"Field | Value\" pattern seen in the real samples).\n                if table and all(len(row) == 2 for row in table if row):\n                    tables.append({row[0]: row[1] for row in table if row and row[0]})\n\n    if needs_ocr_pages:\n        text_parts.append(_ocr_pdf_pages(path, needs_ocr_pages))\n\n    return \"\\n\\n\".join(text_parts), tables, []\n\n\ndef _ocr_pdf_pages(path: Path, page_indices: list[int]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Render specific PDF pages to images and OCR them with pytesseract.\n\n    Uses pymupdf (fitz) for the page->image rendering step -- a pip package,\n    no separate system install needed (this replaced an earlier version that\n    shelled out to pdftoppm/poppler, which meant a second manual installer\n    on top of tesseract for no real benefit).\n\n    tesseract itself still has no pip-only substitute -- it's a genuine\n    external OCR engine, pytesseract is just a thin wrapper around it.\n    \"\"\"\n    if pytesseract is None:\n        return \"[OCR SKIPPED: pytesseract not available]\"\n\n    import fitz  # pymupdf\n    from io import BytesIO\n\n    ocr_text = []\n    doc = fitz.open(str(path))\n    for i in page_indices:\n        page = doc[i]\n        # 200 DPI-ish render -- higher than default 72 DPI so small text stays legible\n        pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=fitz.Matrix(200 / 72, 200 / 72))\n        img = Image.open(BytesIO(pix.tobytes(\"png\")))\n        ocr_text.append(pytesseract.image_to_string(img))\n    doc.close()\n    return \"\\n\\n\".join(ocr_text)\n\n\ndef read_txt(path: Path) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    return path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"), [], []\n\n\ndef read_image(path: Path) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Standalone image files (images/ folder, or figure plates). OCR any\n    text baked into the image (captions, labels on a figure plate).\"\"\"\n    if pytesseract is None:\n        return \"[OCR SKIPPED: pytesseract not available]\", [], [str(path)]\n    text = pytesseract.image_to_string(Image.open(path))\n    return text, [], [str(path)]\n\n\nREADERS = {\n    \".md\": read_markdown,\n    \".markdown\": read_markdown,\n    \".docx\": read_docx,\n    \".pdf\": read_pdf,\n    \".txt\": read_txt,\n    \".png\": read_image,\n    \".jpg\": read_image,\n    \".jpeg\": read_image,\n}\n\n\ndef read_any(file_path: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Single entry point: look at the extension, dispatch, done.\n    Callers should NEVER need to know or care about the file's topic folder\n    to read it correctly -- that's the whole fix.\"\"\"\n    path = Path(file_path)\n    ext = path.suffix.lower()\n    reader = READERS.get(ext)\n    if reader is None:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"No reader registered for extension '{ext}' ({file_path}). \"\n            f\"Known extensions: {list(READERS.keys())}\"\n        )\n    return reader(path)\n", "filename": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/ingest/readers.py"}, "hidden_in_chat": null, "tool_origin": "first_party"}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-08-29T15:51:42.334900Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-29T15:51:52.823291Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "Copy the whole block above into `src/ingest/readers.py` (delete the old contents first). But\nchronicle chapters are long narrative prose (tens of thousands of chars) --\ntoo big for a single embedding to represent well, and too big to usefully\ncite in an answer. So long documents get split further, on paragraph\nboundaries, with a bit of overlap so we don't cut a sentence in half at a\nchunk edge and lose the fact it contained.\n\nEVERY CHUNK CARRIES ITS PARENT'S METADATA (source_type, reliability_prior,\ntitle, doc_id) -- this is what lets the agent's conflict-check step later\nsay \"this chunk is from a codex (0.9 reliability), that one's from ephemera\n(0.3 reliability)\" without re-looking anything up.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom src.models.document import SourceDocument\n\n\nCHUNK_TARGET_CHARS = 1000   # roughly 200-250 tokens -- small enough to embed\n                             # precisely, big enough to hold a full fact\nCHUNK_OVERLAP_CHARS = 150    # keeps a sentence from being orphaned at a chunk edge\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Chunk:\n    chunk_id: str\n    doc_id: str\n    text: str\n    source_type: str\n    title: str\n    reliability_prior: float\n    file_path: str\n    needs_review: bool = False\n    chunk_index: int = 0\n\n\ndef chunk_document(doc: SourceDocument) -> list[Chunk]:\n    \"\"\"One SourceDocument -> one or more Chunks.\"\"\"\n    text = doc.raw_text.strip()\n\n    if len(text) <= CHUNK_TARGET_CHARS * 1.5:\n        # Short enough already (typical wiki/codex entry) -- keep as one chunk.\n        return [Chunk(\n            chunk_id=f\"{doc.doc_id}_c0\",\n            doc_id=doc.doc_id,\n            text=text,\n            source_type=doc.source_type.value,\n            title=doc.title,\n            reliability_prior=doc.reliability_prior,\n            file_path=doc.file_path,\n            needs_review=doc.metadata.get(\"needs_review\", False),\n            chunk_index=0,\n        ))\n\n    # Long document (typical chronicle chapter) -- split on paragraph breaks,\n    # packing paragraphs together up to ~CHUNK_TARGET_CHARS, with the last\n    # bit of one chunk repeated at the start of the next (overlap) so a fact\n    # split across the boundary isn't lost from both sides.\n    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in text.split(\"\\n\\n\") if p.strip()]\n    chunks = []\n    current = \"\"\n    for para in paragraphs:\n        if len(current) + len(para) > CHUNK_TARGET_CHARS and current:\n            chunks.append(current.strip())\n            # start next chunk with the tail of this one, for overlap\n            current = current[-CHUNK_OVERLAP_CHARS:] + \"\\n\\n\" + para\n        else:\n            current = current + \"\\n\\n\" + para if current else para\n    if current.strip():\n        chunks.append(current.strip())\n\n    return [\n        Chunk(\n            chunk_id=f\"{doc.doc_id}_c{i}\",\n            doc_id=doc.doc_id,\n            text=chunk_text,\n            source_type=doc.source_type.value,\n            title=doc.title,\n            reliability_prior=doc.reliability_prior,\n            file_path=doc.file_path,\n            needs_review=doc.metadata.get(\"needs_review\", False),\n            chunk_index=i,\n        )\n        for i, chunk_text in enumerate(chunks)\n    ]\n\n\ndef chunk_all(documents: list[SourceDocument]) -> list[Chunk]:\n    all_chunks = []\n    for doc in documents:\n        all_chunks.extend(chunk_document(doc))\n    return all_chunks\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    from src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n    chunks = chunk_all(docs)\n    print(f\"{len(docs)} documents -> {len(chunks)} chunks\")\n    lengths = [len(c.text) for c in chunks]\n    print(f\"avg chunk length: {sum(lengths)//max(len(lengths),1)} chars, \"\n          f\"max: {max(lengths) if lengths else 0}, min: {min(lengths) if lengths else 0}\")\n", "path": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/chunk/chunker.py"}, "message": "Splits already-ingested SourceDocuments into embedding-sized chunks", "integration_name": "File Creation", the embedding + local vector store \u2014 using Voyage AI (your 200M free tokens) + ChromaDB (free, local, no server to run):", "citations": []}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-08-30T09:55:51.917876Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-30T09:56:05.291288Z", "flags": null, "type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_018gaGtnAq6Nq3RhKXGakh2E", "name": "create_file", "input": {"description": "Embeds chunks with Voyage AI and stores them in a local ChromaDB vector store", "file_text": "\"\"\"\nEmbeds every chunk with Voyage AI and stores it in ChromaDB (a free, local\nvector database -- no server to run, no cost beyond the embedding API calls).\n\nWHY VOYAGE AI: 200M free tokens on signup, one of the best embedding\nquality tiers available for free (see docs/decisions.md for the comparison\nwe did against OpenRouter-only and Grok).\n\nWHY CHUNK IN BATCHES: Voyage's API accepts many texts per call. Batching\nmeans 552+ chunks costs ~a few API calls instead of 552 separate round\ntrips -- much faster, and matters if you're rate-limited.\n\nCOST AWARENESS: embedding the full corpus once should use a tiny fraction\nof the 200M free token allowance. Still, this script prints exactly how\nmany tokens it's about to use, and supports a --limit flag so you can test\non a handful of chunks first before running the whole corpus.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nimport voyageai\nimport chromadb\n\nfrom src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\nfrom src.chunk.chunker import chunk_all\n\n\nVOYAGE_MODEL = \"voyage-4-large\"     # for documents (highest quality)\nBATCH_SIZE = 100                     # chunks per API call\nCHROMA_DB_PATH = \"data/processed/chroma_db\"\nCOLLECTION_NAME = \"ashen_era_corpus\"\n\n\ndef embed_and_store(limit: int | None = None):\n    api_key = os.environ.get(\"VOYAGE_API_KEY\")\n    if not api_key:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"VOYAGE_API_KEY not set. Create a .env file (see .env.example) \"\n            \"or set it directly: $env:VOYAGE_API_KEY='your-key-here' (PowerShell)\"\n        )\n\n    print(\"Ingesting corpus...\")\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n    print(f\"  {report['parsed_files']} files -> {len(docs)} documents \"\n          f\"({len(report['failed'])} failed)\")\n\n    print(\"Chunking...\")\n    chunks = chunk_all(docs)\n    if limit:\n        chunks = chunks[:limit]\n        print(f\"  LIMITED to first {limit} chunks for testing\")\n    print(f\"  {len(chunks)} chunks ready to embed\")\n\n    client = voyageai.Client(api_key=api_key)\n    chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)\n    # Fresh collection each run -- simplest way to avoid stale/duplicate\n    # entries while we're still iterating. Swap to upsert-based updates\n    # later once the corpus is stable and re-embedding everything every\n    # time gets wasteful.\n    try:\n        chroma_client.delete_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    collection = chroma_client.create_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n\n    total_tokens = 0\n    for i in range(0, len(chunks), BATCH_SIZE):\n        batch = chunks[i:i + BATCH_SIZE]\n        texts = [c.text for c in batch]\n\n        result = client.embed(texts, model=VOYAGE_MODEL, input_type=\"document\")\n        total_tokens += result.total_tokens\n\n        collection.add(\n            ids=[c.chunk_id for c in batch],\n            embeddings=result.embeddings,\n            documents=texts,\n            metadatas=[{\n                \"doc_id\": c.doc_id,\n                \"title\": c.title,\n                \"source_type\": c.source_type,\n                \"reliability_prior\": c.reliability_prior,\n                \"file_path\": c.file_path,\n                \"needs_review\": c.needs_review,\n            } for c in batch],\n        )\n        print(f\"  embedded {min(i + BATCH_SIZE, len(chunks))}/{len(chunks)} chunks \"\n              f\"({total_tokens} tokens so far)\")\n\n    print(f\"\\nDone. {len(chunks)} chunks stored in ChromaDB at {CHROMA_DB_PATH}\")\n    print(f\"Total tokens used: {total_tokens} (of your 200M free allowance)\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(\"--limit\", type=int, default=None,\n                         help=\"Only embed the first N chunks, for a cheap test run\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    embed_and_store(limit=args.limit)\n", "path": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/embed/embed_and_store.py"}, "message": "Embeds Embeddings transform text into high-dimensional vectors where semantically similar texts are positioned closer together in vector space.\n\nEmbeddings are numerical representations of text that capture semantic meaning. They convert text into vectors (arrays of numbers) that can be used for various machine learning tasks. OpenRouter provides a unified API to access embedding models from multiple providers. Embeddings transform text into high-dimensional vectors where semantically similar texts are positioned closer together in vector space. For example, \u201ccat\u201d and \u201ckitten\u201d would have similar embeddings, while \u201ccat\u201d and \u201cairplane\u201d would be far apart. These vector representations enable machines to understand relationships between pieces of text, making them essential for many AI applications. \n\nOpenRouter provides access to various embedding models from different providers.\n\nBatch your requests: When processing multiple texts, send them in a single request rather than making individual API calls. This reduces latency and costs. Cache embeddings: Embeddings for the same text are deterministic (they don\u2019t change). Store embeddings in a database or vector store to avoid regenerating them repeatedly. Normalize for comparison: When comparing embeddings, use cosine similarity rather than Euclidean distance. Cosine similarity is scale-invariant and works better for high-dimensional vectors. Consider Context Length: Each model has a maximum input length (context window). Longer texts may need to be chunked or truncated. Check the model\u2019s specifications before processing long documents. chunk using OpenRouter's free embedding model, stores in\nChromaDB (free, local, no server to run).\n\nWHY OPENROUTER INSTEAD OF VOYAGE: no card required at all (Voyage needs one\nfor identity verification, even though the tokens are free). OpenRouter's\nfree tier is genuinely zero-friction -- sign up, get a key, go. Model used\nhere (nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free) is explicitly free-tier,\nconfirmed no cost per call.\n\nOpenRouter is OpenAI-API-compatible, so we just point the standard `openai`\npython package at OpenRouter's base URL instead of OpenAI's -- no special\nSDK needed.\n\nRATE LIMITS TO KNOW: free-tier OpenRouter accounts get ~50 requests/day\nwithout adding any credit. We batch up to 100 chunks per API call, so the\nfull ~550-chunk corpus costs ~6 calls total -- comfortably under the limit.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nfrom openai import OpenAI\nimport chromadb\n\nfrom src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\nfrom src.chunk.chunker import chunk_all\n\n\nEMBEDDING_MODEL = \"nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free\"\nOPENROUTER_BASE_URL = \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\"\nBATCH_SIZE = 100\nCHROMA_DB_PATH = \"data/processed/chroma_db\"\nCOLLECTION_NAME = \"ashen_era_corpus\"\n\n\ndef get_client() -> OpenAI:\n    api_key = os.environ.get(\"OPENROUTER_API_KEY\")\n    if not api_key:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set. In PowerShell: \"\n            '$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\"your-key-here\"'\n        )\n    return OpenAI(base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, api_key=api_key)\n\n\ndef embed_and_store(limit: int | None = None):\n    client = get_client()\n\n    print(\"Ingesting corpus...\")\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n    print(f\"  {report['parsed_files']} files -> {len(docs)} documents \"\n OpenRouter's\nfree tier is genuinely zero-friction -- sign up, get a key, go. Model used\nhere (nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free) is explicitly free-tier,\nconfirmed no cost per call.\n\nOpenRouter is OpenAI-API-compatible, so we just point the standard `openai`\npython package at OpenRouter's base URL instead of OpenAI's -- no special\nSDK needed.\n\nRATE LIMITS TO KNOW: free-tier OpenRouter accounts get ~50 requests/day\nwithout adding any credit. We batch up to 100 chunks per API call, so the\nfull ~550-chunk corpus costs ~6 calls total -- comfortably under the limit.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nfrom openai import OpenAI\nimport chromadb\n\nfrom src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\nfrom src.chunk.chunker import chunk_all\n\n\nEMBEDDING_MODEL = \"nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free\"\nOPENROUTER_BASE_URL = \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\"\nBATCH_SIZE = 100\nCHROMA_DB_PATH = \"data/processed/chroma_db\"\nCOLLECTION_NAME = \"ashen_era_corpus\"\n\n\ndef get_client() -> OpenAI:\n    api_key = os.environ.get(\"OPENROUTER_API_KEY\")\n    if not api_key:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set. In PowerShell: \"\n            '$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\"your-key-here\"'\n        )\n    return OpenAI(base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, api_key=api_key)\n\n\ndef embed_and_store(limit: int | None = print(f\"  embedded {min(i + BATCH_SIZE, len(chunks))}/{len(chunks)} chunks \"\n              f\"({total_calls} API calls so far)\")\n\n    print(f\"\\nDone. {len(chunks)} chunks stored in ChromaDB at chunk_index=0,\n        )]\n\n    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in text.split(\"\\n\\n\") if p.strip()]\n    chunks = []\n    current = \"\"\n    for para in paragraphs:\n        if len(current) + current + \"\\n\\n\" + para if current else para\n    if current.strip():\n        chunks.append(current.strip())\n\n    return [\n        Chunk(\n            chunk_id=f\"{doc.doc_id}_c{i}\",\n            doc_id=doc.doc_id,\n            text=chunk_text,\n            source_type=doc.source_type.value,\n            title=doc.title,\n            reliability_prior=doc.reliability_prior,\n            file_path=doc.file_path,\n            needs_review=doc.metadata.get(\"needs_review\", False),\n            chunk_index=i,\n        )\n        for i, chunk_text in enumerate(chunks)\n    ]\n\n\ndef chunk_all(documents: list[SourceDocument]) -> list[Chunk]:\n    all_chunks = []\n    for doc in documents:\n        all_chunks.extend(chunk_document(doc))\n    return all_chunks\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    from src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n    chunks = chunk_all(docs)\n    print(f\"{len(docs)} documents -> {len(chunks)} chunks\")\n run).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nfrom openai import OpenAI\nimport chromadb\n\nfrom src.ingest.parse_corpus import ingest_corpus\nfrom src.chunk.chunker import chunk_all\n\n\nEMBEDDING_MODEL = \"nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free\"\nOPENROUTER_BASE_URL = \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\"\nBATCH_SIZE = 100\nCHROMA_DB_PATH = RuntimeError(\n            \"OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set. In PowerShell: \"\n            '$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\"your-key-here\"'\n        )\n    return OpenAI(base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, api_key=api_key)\n\n\ndef embed_and_store(limit: int | None = None):\n    client = get_client()\n\n    print(\"Ingesting corpus...\")\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n    print(f\"  {report['parsed_files']} files -> {len(docs)} documents \"\n          f\"({len(report['failed'])} failed, skipped -- not embedded)\")\n\n    print(\"Chunking...\")\n    chunks = chunk_all(docs)\n    if limit:\n        chunks = chunks[:limit]\n        print(f\"  LIMITED to first {limit} chunks for testing\")\n    print(f\"  {len(chunks)} chunks ready to embed\")\n\n    chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)\n    try:\n        chroma_client.delete_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    collection = chroma_client.create_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n\n    total_calls = 0\n    for i in range(0, len(chunks), BATCH_SIZE):\n        batch = chunks[i:i + BATCH_SIZE]\n        texts = [c.text for c in batch]\n\n        response = client.embeddings.create(model=EMBEDDING_MODEL, input=texts)\n        embeddings = [item.embedding for item in response.data]\n        total_calls += 1\n\n        collection.add(\n            ids=[c.chunk_id for c in batch],\n            embeddings=embeddings,\n            documents=texts,\n            metadatas=[{\n                \"doc_id\": c.doc_id,\n                \"title\": c.title,\n                \"source_type\": c.source_type,\n                \"reliability_prior\": c.reliability_prior,\n                \"file_path\": c.file_path,\n                \"needs_review\": c.needs_review,\n            } for c in batch],\n        )\n        print(f\"  embedded {min(i + BATCH_SIZE, len(chunks))}/{len(chunks)} chunks \"\n              f\"({total_calls} API calls so far)\")\n\n    print(f\"\\nDone. {len(chunks)} chunks stored in ChromaDB at {CHROMA_DB_PATH}\")\n    print(f\"Total API calls used: {total_calls} (free tier: ~50/day without credits)\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(\"--limit\", type=int, default=None)\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    embed_and_store(limit=args.limit)\n```\n\n**`src\\embed\\test_search.py`:**\n\n```python\n\"\"\"\nQuick SourceType.EPHEMERA,\n}\nif not SKIP_OCR:\n    TOPIC_FOLDERS[\"images\"] = SourceType.IMAGE\n\n\ndef _is_ocr_file(file_path: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Standalone images always need OCR. .scan.pdf files are explicitly\n    named as scans in this corpus, so we can skip them by filename without\n    even opening them (faster than letting read_pdf discover it needs OCR\n    after already attempting text extraction).\"\"\"\n    if file_path.suffix.lower() in (\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\"):\n        return True\n    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(\".scan.pdf\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef ingest_corpus(raw_data_dir: str = \"data/raw\"):\n    all_documents = []\n    report = {\"parsed_files\": 0, \"documents_created\": 0, \"needs_review\": [],\n               \"failed\": [], \"skipped_ocr\": []}\n\n    for folder_name, source_type in TOPIC_FOLDERS.items():\n        folder = Path(raw_data_dir) / folder_name\n        if not folder.exists():\n            continue\n\n        for file_path in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")):\n            if not file_path.is_file():\n                continue\n\n            if SKIP_OCR and _is_ocr_file(file_path):\n                report[\"skipped_ocr\"].append(str(file_path))\n                continue\n\n            try:\n                print(f\"  parsing: {file_path.name}\", flush=True)\n                docs = ingest_file(str(file_path), source_type)\n                all_documents.extend(docs)\n                report[\"parsed_files\"] += 1\n                report[\"documents_created\"] += len(docs)\n                for d in docs:\n                    if d.metadata.get(\"needs_review\"):\n                        report[\"needs_review\"].append(d.doc_id)\n            except Exception as e:\n                report[\"failed\"].append({\"file\": str(file_path), \"error\": str(e)})\n\n    return all_documents, report\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n\n    print(f\"Files Reasoning: OCR is slow on typical dev\nhardware (each image/page takes several seconds), low-value for our 1C\ntrack specifically (most OCR-only content is portrait/heraldry art more\nrelevant to 1A, and facts on codex figure plates are usually also present\nin the register tables we already parse as text), and this is a one-time\nindexing step anyway -- doesn't affect live demo speed either way, so the\nreal cost was purely dev time, not final product quality. attempting text extraction).\"\"\"\n    if file_path.suffix.lower() in (\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\"):\n        return True\n    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(\".scan.pdf\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef ingest_corpus(raw_data_dir: str = \"data/raw\"):\n    all_documents = []\n    report = {\"parsed_files\": 0, \"documents_created\": 0, \"needs_review\": [],\n continue\n\n        for file_path in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")):\n            if not file_path.is_file():\n                continue\n\n            if SKIP_OCR and _is_ocr_file(file_path):\n         for d in docs:\n                    if d.metadata.get(\"needs_review\"):\n                        report[\"needs_review\"].append(d.doc_id)\n            except Exception as e:\n                report[\"failed\"].append({\"file\": str(file_path), \"error\": str(e)})\n\n    return all_documents, report\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n\n    print(f\"Files Embeds a query, searches ChromaDB,\nreturns chunks with their source metadata (title, source_type, reliability)\nattached -- the agent needs that metadata visible to reason about conflicts.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom src.embed.embed_and_store import get_client, EMBEDDING_MODEL, CHROMA_DB_PATH, COLLECTION_NAME\nimport chromadb\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SearchResult:\n    text: str\n    title: str\n    source_type: str\n    reliability_prior: float\n    doc_id: str\n\n\ndef search_corpus(query: str, n_results: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:\n    client = get_client()\n    query_embedding = client.embeddings.create(\n        model=EMBEDDING_MODEL, input=[query], encoding_format=\"float\"\n    ).data[0].embedding\n\n    chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)\n    collection = chroma_client.get_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n    results = collection.query(query_embeddings=[query_embedding], n_results=n_results)\n\n    out = []\n    for i in range(len(results[\"ids\"][0])):\n        meta = results[\"metadatas\"][0][i]\n        out.append(SearchResult(\n            text=results[\"documents\"][0][i],\n            title=meta[\"title\"],\n            source_type=meta[\"source_type\"],\n            reliability_prior=meta[\"reliability_prior\"],\n            doc_id=meta[\"doc_id\"],\n        ))\n    return out\n", "path": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/agent/search_tool.py"}, "message": "Search tool wrapping embedding + ChromaDB query, used by the agent loop", "integration_name": "File Creation", "integration_icon_url": null, "tool_identifier": null, "icon_name": "file", "context": null, "display_content": {"type": "code_block", "language": "python", "code": "\"\"\"\nThe agent's ONE tool: search the corpus. "2026-08-30T10:52:39.329191Z", "flags": null, "type": "thinking", "thinking": "I'm designing the main agent loop file that combines the LLM chat call with loop logic, planning to use OpenRouter's free auto-router model and prompt for strict JSON output as a robust fallback since not all free models support structured outputs reliably. Now I'm drafting the system prompt to establish the agent's role as a research assistant searching the Ashen Era Archive corpus.\n\nThe loop itself accumulates gathered chunks and a history log across iterations, calling the LLM each turn to decide whether to search further or answer, logging every step,\u2026", "summaries": [{"summary": "Architected agent loop integrating LLM routing and structured JSON fallbacks."}], "cut_off": false, "truncated": true, "hidden": false, "thinking_hidden": false, "alternative_display_type": null, "signature": null}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-08-30T10:52:39.330763Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-30T10:52:39.333365Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "Now the actual agent loop \u2014 the core of your 1C submission:", "citations": []}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-08-30T10:52:39.333388Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-30T10:53:04.055106Z", "flags": null, "type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01Xcy7LRUFhZi2ALbBdeQvVV", "name": "create_file", "input": {"description": "The core 1C agent: search, read, decide if enough info, repeat, then answer with reliability-aware reasoning", "file_text": "\"\"\"\nTHE AGENT LOOP -- this is the heart of the 1C submission.\n\nEach iteration, the LLM sees the question + everything gathered so far, and\ndecides ONE of two things:\n  - \"search\": it doesn't have enough yet, and proposes the next query\n  - \"answer\": it has enough, and gives a final answer\n\nWHY ONE COMBINED CALL (not a separate \"am I done?\" call + a separate\n\"what's next?\" call): cheaper, and it's the design decision we discussed\nearly on -- fold the self-critique into the same call by default. If we\never find this produces bad answers on conflicting-source questions\nspecifically, that's the trigger to add a SEPARATE double-check call just\nfor those cases, not for every question.\n\nCONFLICT HANDLING: the system prompt explicitly tells the model about the\nreliability tiers and instructs it to look for and flag disagreements\nbetween sources, preferring an explicit \"authoritative\" claim over a\ndefault reliability-tier ranking when one exists (this is the Ashreach\ncodex example: \"this is the authoritative record, popular accounts wrongly\nclaim otherwise\" should win over just trusting codex > wiki blindly, IF a\nwiki entry ever explicitly cited a correction the other way).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\n\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\nfrom src.agent.search_tool import search_corpus, SearchResult\n\n\nOPENROUTER_BASE_URL = \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\"\nAGENT_MODEL = \"openrouter/free\"   # auto-router across free models; swap to a\n                                    # specific model string if you want more\n                                    # control over which one answers\nMAX_ITERATIONS = 5\nRESULTS_PER_SEARCH = 5\n\n\nSYSTEM_PROMPT = \"\"\"You are a research agent answering questions about the Ashen \\\nEra Archive, a fictional fantasy corpus. You can only use facts from the search \\\nresults provided to you -- never use outside/general knowledge, since this world \\\nis entirely invented and nothing you already know about it is real.\n\nYou have ONE tool: search the corpus with a text query. Each result comes \\\ntagged with its source type and a reliability score (0.0-1.0):\n  codex (0.9)      = official record, most trustworthy by default\n  wiki (0.7)       = community-compiled, generally reliable\n  chronicle (0.5)  = in-story narrative, may reflect a character's bias\n  ephemera (0.3)   = in-world letters/ledgers/etc, least reliable by default\n\nIMPORTANT: these scores are a STARTING POINT, not the final word. If a source \\\nEXPLICITLY claims authority or corrects another account (e.g. \"this is the \\\nauthoritative record, popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise\"), that explicit \\\nclaim should outweigh the default score. Always check retrieved chunks for \\\ndisagreement before answering -- if two sources conflict, say so in your \\\nreasoning and explain which you trusted and why.\n\nEach turn, respond with ONLY a JSON object, no other text, in one of these two shapes:\n\nTo search for more information:\n{\"thought\": \"<your reasoning about what you have and what's missing>\", \"action\": \"search\", \"query\": \"<search text>\"}\n\nTo give a final answer (only once you have enough to answer confidently):\n{\"thought\": \"<your reasoning, including any source conflicts you found and how you resolved them>\", \"action\": \"answer\", \"answer\": \"<final answer>\", \"sources\": [\"<doc titles you relied on>\"]}\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _call_llm(messages: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    api_key = os.environ.get(\"OPENROUTER_API_KEY\")\n    if not api_key:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set.\")\n    client = OpenAI(base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, api_key=api_key)\n\n    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=AGENT_MODEL, messages=messages)\n    raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()\n\n    # Free models sometimes wrap JSON in ```json fences despite instructions -- strip those.\n    if raw.startswith(\"```\"):\n        raw = raw.strip(\"`\")\n        if raw.startswith(\"json\"):\n            raw = raw[4:]\n        raw = raw.strip()\n\n    try:\n        return json.loads(raw)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError:\n        # Model didn't follow the format -- surface the raw text so we can\n        # debug it, rather than crashing the whole loop silently.\n        return {\"thought\": \"PARSE_ERROR\", \"action\": \"answer\",\n                 \"answer\": f\"[Could not parse model output: {raw[:300]}]\", \"sources\": []}\n\n\ndef _format_evidence(results: list[SearchResult]) -> str:\n    if not results:\n        return \"(no evidence gathered yet)\"\n    lines = []\n    for r in results:\n        lines.append(\n            f\"[{r.source_type}, reliability={r.reliability_prior}] {r.title}:\\n{r.text}\\n\"\n        )\n    return \"\\n---\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef answer_question(question: str, verbose: bool = True) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Runs the full search -> read -> decide loop. Returns {\"answer\":, \"trace\":}.\"\"\"\n    gathered: list[SearchResult] = []\n    seen_doc_ids = set()\n    trace = []\n\n    for iteration in range(MAX_ITERATIONS):\n        user_message = (\n            f\"Question: {question}\\n\\n\"\n            f\"Evidence gathered so far:\\n{_format_evidence(gathered)}\"\n        )\n        messages = [\n            {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": SYSTEM_PROMPT},\n            {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": user_message},\n        ]\n\n        decision = _call_llm(messages)\n        trace.append({\"iteration\": iteration, \"decision\": decision})\n\n        if verbose:\n            print(f\"\\n--- Iteration {iteration} ---\")\n            print(f\"Thought: {decision.get('thought', '')}\")\n            print(f\"Action: {decision.get('action', '')}\")\n\n        if decision.get(\"action\") == \"answer\":\n            if verbose:\n                print(f\"ANSWER: {decision.get('answer', '')}\")\n            return {\"answer\": decision.get(\"answer\", \"\"), \"trace\": trace}\n\n        query = decision.get(\"query\", question)\n        if verbose:\n            print(f\"Searching: {query}\")\n        results = search_corpus(query, n_results=RESULTS_PER_SEARCH)\n\n        new_results = [r for r in results if r.doc_id not in seen_doc_ids]\n        for r in new_results:\n            seen_doc_ids.add(r.doc_id)\n        gathered.extend(new_results)\n\n    # Ran out of iterations without a confident answer -- force a final\n    # answer from whatever was gathered rather than failing silently.\n    if verbose:\n        print(\"\\n[Max iterations reached -- forcing final answer]\")\n    messages = [\n        {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": SYSTEM_PROMPT},\n        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": (\n            f\"Question: {question}\\n\\nEvidence gathered so far:\\n{_format_evidence(gathered)}\\n\\n\"\n            \"You must answer now with what you have, even if incomplete.\"\n        )},\n    ]\n    decision = _call_llm(messages)\n    trace.append({\"iteration\": MAX_ITERATIONS, \"decision\": decision, \"forced\": True})\n    return {\"answer\": decision.get(\"answer\", \"\"), \"trace\": trace}\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import sys\n    q = \" \".join(sys.argv[1:]) or \"In which year was the 'Gauntlet of Sorrowfell' actually forged?\"\n    result = answer_question(q)\n    print(f\"\\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\\n{result['answer']}\")\n", "path": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/agent/agent_loop.py"}, "message": "The core 1C agent: search, read, decide if enough info, repeat, then answer with reliability-aware reasoning", "integration_name": "File Creation", "integration_icon_url": null, "tool_identifier": null, "icon_name": "file", "context": null, "display_content": {"type": "code_block", "language": "python", "code": "\"\"\"\nTHE AGENT LOOP -- this is the heart of the 1C submission.\n\nEach iteration, the LLM sees the question + everything gathered so far, and\ndecides ONE of two things:\n  - \"search\": it doesn't have enough yet, and proposes the next query\n  - \"answer\": it has enough, and gives a final answer\n\nWHY ONE COMBINED CALL (not a separate \"am I done?\" call + a separate\n\"what's next?\" call): cheaper, and it's the design decision we discussed\nearly on -- fold the self-critique into the same call by default. Good luck with exams.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "2026-08-30T11:05:20.439528Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-30T11:05:20.439528Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a05258-4b6b-7a6d-af62-8620fbd05643"}, {"uuid": "01a052a2-dd7b-718c-91ad-f64e80e98d6a", "text": "came back siree\nwhats is our next step", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-08-30T12:26:42.527057Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-30T12:26:42.527057Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "came back siree\nwhats is our next step", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-08-30T12:26:42.527185Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-30T12:26:42.527185Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a05258-4b6c-78c4-b429-bd0639c03aa9"}, {"uuid": "01a052a2-dd7c-7e83-96cf-b024c0de8a8c", "text": "I'm digging into the duplicate ID bug in the codex file\u2014the doc_id format combines source type, filename, extension, and slugified title, but since multiple creature entries share identical heading names like \"Appearance\" or \"Threat Assessment\" within the same file, their generated IDs collide.\n\nThis suggests my split-level assumption for codex files is wrong: I assumed one level-3 header per entity, but this bestiary structures entity names at level-2 with their fields nested as level-3 subsections, unlike the gazetteer file where level-3 headers marked distinct entries. That's exactly the \"don't assume uniform structure across files\" trap I need to account for.\n\nThis creates doc_id collisions since generic field names like \"Appearance\" and \"Threat Assessment\" repeat across multiple creatures in the same file, and my splitter is treating each as a separate document with the same slugified title \u2014 producing duplicate IDs. I need to actually inspect the real heading structure to fix this properly.\n\nI don't have the armory file myself, only the gazetteer sample, so I should either ask them to paste some content or give them a debug script that prints the raw heading structure so we can see exact levels together. Given time constraints, I'll explain the bug clearly \u2014 the armory book nests entity names above sub-field headers unlike the gazetteer's flat list \u2014 and propose either getting a structure dump from them, or as a safety net, making doc_ids globally unique via a counter/hash regardless of title collisions.\n\nThe more robust fix is to detect the shallowest heading level that appears multiple times and split on that level, treating deeper headings as nested sub-content merged into the body rather than split into separate entries, falling back to a fixed level only if no shallower headings exist.\n\n\u2026Good \u2014 real bug, and I can see exactly what happened: `codex_vaeloria_ii_armory_of_relics_and_bestiary.docx` is structured differently than the gazetteer we sampled earlier. The gazetteer has one `###` heading per location (Ashreach, Blackford...). This bestiary apparently nests each creature's *name* at one heading level, with generic sub-sections like \"Appearance,\" \"Threat Assessment,\" \"Attunement\" at `###` **underneath** it. My splitter was treating those generic sub-section names as if they were entity names \u2014 so \"Appearance\" from 20 different creatures all collided into one ID.\n\nThis is the same lesson as the format-vs-topic bug, one level deeper: **structure varies file-to-file even within the same topic.** Fixing it properly \u2014 split on whichever heading level is actually being used to separate *entities*, not a fixed level per topic \u2014 plus a safety net so this can never crash the whole run again.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow widen the codex heading range so this new logic can see both possible levels (currently locked to level 3 only, which is why it never got the chance to prefer level 2):\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow let's add a safety net \u2014 even with this fixed, a future unknown file could still collide, and I'd rather it skip-and-warn than crash your whole embedding run again:\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nLet's verify this actually fixes the collision pattern, using a synthetic test that mimics the bestiary's nested structure, plus confirm no regression on your real 4 samples:\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nFixed and verified \u2014 2 entries, correctly split by creature name, sub-sections kept inside each body. Now confirming no regression on your real files:\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nClean, no regressions, gazetteer's 9 per-location entries still split correctly at `###`.\n\n## Files to update on your end\n\n**`src\\ingest\\split.py`** \u2014 replace the whole `split_into_entries` function with:\n\n```python\ndef split_into_entries(text: str, min_heading_level: int = 2, max_heading_level: int = 3):\n    \"\"\"\n    Returns a list of (title, body, needs_review) tuples.\n    Picks the SHALLOWEST heading level actually present in range, and splits\n    only on that level -- deeper headings stay embedded as body text. Fixes\n    a bug where nested structures (## Creature Name containing ### Appearance,\n    ### Threat Assessment sub-sections) caused every creature's \"Appearance\"\n    section to collide into one ID.\n    \"\"\"\n    headings = list(MD_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    usable_headings = [\n        h for h in headings if min_heading_level <= len(h.group(1)) <= max_heading_level\n    ]\n\n    if usable_headings:\n        levels_present = sorted(set(len(h.group(1)) for h in usable_headings))\n        split_level = levels_present[0]\n        split_headings = [h for h in usable_headings if len(h.group(1)) == split_level]\n\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(split_headings):\n            title = h.group(2).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = split_headings[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(split_headings) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, False))\n        return entries\n\n    heuristic_hits = list(HEURISTIC_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    if heuristic_hits:\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(heuristic_hits):\n            title = h.group(1).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = heuristic_hits[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(heuristic_hits) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, True))\n        return entries\n\n    return [(\"Untitled\", text.strip(), True)]\n```\n\n**`src\\ingest\\parse_document.py`** \u2014 find `TOPIC_SPLIT_LEVELS` and change the codex line to:\n```python\n    SourceType.CODEX: (2, 3),       # entity name can be at ## We check\n   the TEXT for the pattern, not the folder the file came from.\n\n2. split_into_entries: many raw files contain MULTIPLE logical documents\n   (e.g. the codex sample had Ashreach, Blackford, Cindermere Hold... all\n   in one .docx). This splits on heading-like breaks so each entity gets\n   its own SourceDocument and its own chunk for embedding, instead of one\n   giant blob where a question about \"Blackford\" also drags in irrelevant\n   text about \"Cindermere Hold\".\n\n   Two splitting strategies, tried in order:\n   (a) Markdown headings (## or ###) -- reliable, works whenever the source\n       came from read_markdown() or read_docx() (pandoc emits real headings).\n   (b) Heuristic fallback for plain-text/PDF-extracted text with NO markdown\n       headings -- looks for short, standalone title-like lines. Any document split this way is flagged in metadata\n       with needs_review=True so a human can sanity-check it -- better to\n       flag uncertainty than silently mis-split a document.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nWIKILINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\[\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\]\")\n\n# A markdown heading line: 1-3 '#' characters then a title.\nMD_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^(#{1,3})\\s+(.+)$\", re.MULTILINE)\n\n# Heuristic fallback for headless plain text (e.g. raw PDF extraction):\n# a short (<=8 words) standalone line, title-cased, with blank lines around\n# it, and NOT ending in sentence punctuation -- a rough proxy for \"this\n# looks like a heading, not a sentence.\"\nHEURISTIC_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"^\\n([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,'\\-]{2,50})\\n\\n(?!\\n)\", re.MULTILINE\n)\n\n\ndef extract_wikilinks(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    seen = []\n    for match in WIKILINK_PATTERN.finditer(text):\n        name = match.group(1).strip()\n        if name not in seen:\n            seen.append(name)\n    return seen\n\n\ndef split_into_entries(text: str, min_heading_level: int = 2, max_heading_level: int = 3):\n    \"\"\"\n    Returns a list of (title, body, needs_review) tuples.\n\n    min/max_heading_level lets a caller say \"split codex files on ### (level 3,\n    per-entity entries)\" vs \"split chronicles on ## (level 2, per-chapter)\" --\n    but this is a preference, not a hard requirement, since we can't always\n    predict which heading level a given source will use.\n    \"\"\"\n    headings = list(MD_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    usable_headings = [\n        h for h in headings if min_heading_level <= len(h.group(1)) <= max_heading_level\n    ]\n\n    if usable_headings:\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(usable_headings):\n            title = h.group(2).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = usable_headings[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(usable_headings) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, False))\n        return entries\n\n    # Fallback: no markdown headings found at all (likely PDF-extracted plain\n    # text). A\n    gazetteer might use ### once per location (flat). Reasoning: OCR is slow on typical dev\nhardware (each image/page takes several seconds), low-value for our 1C\ntrack specifically (most OCR-only content is portrait/heraldry art more\nrelevant to 1A, and facts on codex figure plates are usually also present\nin the register tables we already parse as text), and this is a one-time\nindexing step anyway -- doesn't affect live demo speed either way, so the\nreal cost was purely dev time, not final product quality. Flip SKIP_OCR to\nFalse any time to re-enable, e.g. on a faster machine later.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom src.models.document import SourceType\nfrom src.ingest.parse_document import ingest_file\n\n\nSKIP_OCR = True\n\nTOPIC_FOLDERS = {\n    \"wiki\": SourceType.WIKI,\n    \"codex\": SourceType.CODEX,\n    \"chronicles\": SourceType.CHRONICLE,\n    \"ephemera\": SourceType.EPHEMERA,\n}\nif not SKIP_OCR:\n    TOPIC_FOLDERS[\"images\"] = SourceType.IMAGE\n\n\ndef _is_ocr_file(file_path: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Standalone images always need OCR. .scan.pdf files are explicitly\n    named as scans in this corpus, so we can skip them by filename without\n    even opening them (faster than letting read_pdf discover it needs OCR\n    after already attempting text extraction).\"\"\"\n    if file_path.suffix.lower() in (\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\"):\n        return True\n    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(\".scan.pdf\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef ingest_corpus(raw_data_dir: str = \"data/raw\"):\n    all_documents = []\n    report = {\"parsed_files\": 0, \"documents_created\": 0, \"needs_review\": [],\n               \"failed\": [], \"skipped_ocr\": [], \"id_collisions\": []}\n    seen_doc_ids = set()\n\n    for folder_name, source_type in TOPIC_FOLDERS.items():\n        folder = Path(raw_data_dir) / folder_name\n        if not folder.exists():\n            continue\n\n        for file_path in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")):\n            if not file_path.is_file():\n                continue\n\n            if SKIP_OCR and _is_ocr_file(file_path):\n                report[\"skipped_ocr\"].append(str(file_path))\n                continue\n\n            try:\n                print(f\"  parsing: {file_path.name}\", flush=True)\n                docs = ingest_file(str(file_path), source_type)\n\n                # Safety net: guarantee doc_id uniqueness even if a future\n                # file's structure fools the splitter again. Better to\n                # rename-and-warn than crash the whole embedding run.\n                for d in docs:\n                    if d.doc_id in seen_doc_ids:\n                        original_id = d.doc_id\n                        counter = 2\n                        while f\"{original_id}_dup{counter}\" in seen_doc_ids:\n                            counter += 1\n                        d.doc_id = f\"{original_id}_dup{counter}\"\n                        report[\"id_collisions\"].append({\"original\": original_id, \"renamed_to\": d.doc_id})\n                    seen_doc_ids.add(d.doc_id)\n\n                all_documents.extend(docs)\n                report[\"parsed_files\"] += 1\n                report[\"documents_created\"] += len(docs)\n                for d in docs:\n                    if d.metadata.get(\"needs_review\"):\n                        report[\"needs_review\"].append(d.doc_id)\n            except Exception as e:\n                report[\"failed\"].append({\"file\": str(file_path), \"error\": str(e)})\n\n    return all_documents, report\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n\n    print(f\"Files parsed:      {report['parsed_files']}\")\n    print(f\"Documents created: {report['documents_created']}\")\n    print(f\"Skipped (OCR disabled): {len(report['skipped_ocr'])}\")\n    print(f\"ID collisions auto-renamed: {len(report['id_collisions'])}\")\n    for c in report[\"id_collisions\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {c['original']} -> {c['renamed_to']}\")\n    print(f\"Needs manual review (heuristic split, verify these): {len(report['needs_review'])}\")\n    for doc_id in report[\"needs_review\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {doc_id}\")\n    print(f\"Failed: {len(report['failed'])}\")\n    for f in report[\"failed\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {f['file']}: {f['error']}\")\n\n    print(\"\\n--- Sample of parsed documents ---\")\n    for d in docs[:8]:\n len(h.group(1)) == split_level]\n\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(split_headings):\n            title = h.group(2).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = split_headings[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(split_headings) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, False))\n        return entries\n\n    heuristic_hits = list(HEURISTIC_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    if heuristic_hits:\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(heuristic_hits):\n            title = h.group(1).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = heuristic_hits[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(heuristic_hits) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, True))\n        return entries\n\n    return [(\"Untitled\", text.strip(), True)]\n```\n\n**`src\\ingest\\parse_corpus.py`** \u2014 full file:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"\nWalks Flip to False\nto re-enable later on faster hardware.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom src.models.document import SourceType\nfrom src.ingest.parse_document import ingest_file\n\n\nSKIP_OCR = True\n\nTOPIC_FOLDERS = {\n    \"wiki\": SourceType.WIKI,\n    \"codex\": SourceType.CODEX,\n    \"chronicles\": SourceType.CHRONICLE,\n    \"ephemera\": SourceType.EPHEMERA,\n}\nif not SKIP_OCR:\n    TOPIC_FOLDERS[\"images\"] = SourceType.IMAGE\n\n\ndef _is_ocr_file(file_path: Path) -> bool:\n    if file_path.suffix.lower() in (\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\"):\n        return True\n    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(\".scan.pdf\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef ingest_corpus(raw_data_dir: str = \"data/raw\"):\n    all_documents = []\n    report = {\"parsed_files\": 0, \"documents_created\": 0, \"needs_review\": [],\n               \"failed\": [], \"skipped_ocr\": [], \"id_collisions\": []}\n    seen_doc_ids = set()\n\n    for folder_name, report[\"skipped_ocr\"].append(str(file_path))\n                continue\n\n            try:\n                print(f\"  parsing: {file_path.name}\", flush=True)\n                docs = Here it is in full to paste over `src\\ingest\\parse_document.py`:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"\nThe single function every other part of the system calls: ingest_file().\n\nTHE FIX THIS FILE REPRESENTS:\n  Before: \"this is in codex/, so read it as a .docx\"        <- wrong, breaks\n          the moment a codex entry is a .pdf instead.\n  Now:    \"this is in codex/, so source_type=CODEX (controls reliability\n          prior + how we'll route agent questions to it), AND separately,\n          this file ends in .pdf, so use read_pdf() (controls HOW we get\n          text out of it).\" Two independent lookups, combined at the end.\n\nPer-topic heading-split preferences are defaults, not hard assumptions --\nthey're just *parameters* passed to split_into_entries(), which itself\npicks the actual shallowest heading level present (see split.py).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom src.models.document import SourceDocument, SourceType, Entity\nfrom src.ingest.readers import read_any\nfrom src.ingest.split import extract_wikilinks, split_into_entries\nfrom src.ingest.tables import extract_markdown_tables\n\n\nTOPIC_SPLIT_LEVELS = {\n    SourceType.CODEX: (2, 3),       # entity name can be at ## or ###, sub-sections deeper\n    SourceType.CHRONICLE: (2, 2),   # \"## Chapter 1\" style\n    SourceType.WIKI: (1, 1),        # one wiki file = one entity, split on H1 only\n    SourceType.EPHEMERA: (2, 3),    # multiple entries per file, level varies\n}\n\n\ndef _slugify(text: str) -> str:\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"_\", text.lower()).strip(\"_\")\n\n\ndef ingest_file(file_path: str, source_type: SourceType) -> list[SourceDocument]:\n    path = Path(file_path)\n    raw_text, structured_tables, image_refs = read_any(file_path)\n\n    min_level, max_level = TOPIC_SPLIT_LEVELS.get(source_type, (2, 3))\n    entries = split_into_entries(raw_text, min_level, max_level)\n\n    documents = []\n    for title, body, needs_review in entries:\n        entities = [Entity(name=n) for n in extract_wikilinks(body)]\n        doc_id = f\"{source_type.value}_{path.stem}_{path.suffix.lstrip('.')}_{_slugify(title)}\"\n\n        entry_tables = extract_markdown_tables(body)\n        if structured_tables:\n            entry_tables = entry_tables + structured_tables\n            if len(entries) > 1:\n                needs_review = True\n\n        documents.append(SourceDocument(\n            doc_id=doc_id,\n            source_type=source_type,\n            title=title,\n            raw_text=body,\n            file_path=str(path),\n            entities=entities,\n            tables=entry_tables,\n            metadata={\n                \"source_file\": path.name,\n                \"file_extension\": path.suffix.lower(),\n                \"needs_review\": needs_review,\n                \"image_refs\": image_refs,\n            },\n        ))\n\n    return documents\n```\n\n**`src\\ingest\\split.py`** \u2014 full file:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"\nTwo format-agnostic helpers used AFTER a reader in readers.py has already\nturned a file into text:\n\n1. extract_wikilinks: pulls [[Entity]] mentions if the text happens to use\n   that syntax -- a markdown convention, checked on the TEXT, not tied to\n   the wiki folder specifically.\n\n2. split_into_entries: splits a file containing multiple logical documents\n   into separate entries. Picks the SHALLOWEST heading level actually\n   present in range and splits only on that level -- fixes a bug where a\n   nested structure (## Creature Name containing ### Appearance, ###\n   Threat Assessment sub-sections) caused every creature's \"Appearance\"\n   section to collide into one ID.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nWIKILINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\[\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\]\")\n\nMD_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^(#{1,3})\\s+(.+)$\", re.MULTILINE)\n\nHEURISTIC_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"^\\n([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,'\\-]{2,50})\\n\\n(?!\\n)\", re.MULTILINE\n)\n\n\ndef extract_wikilinks(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    seen = []\n    for match in WIKILINK_PATTERN.finditer(text):\n        name = match.group(1).strip()\n        if name not in seen:\n            seen.append(name)\n    return seen\n\n\ndef split_into_entries(text: str, min_heading_level: int = 2, max_heading_level: int = 3):\n    headings = list(MD_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    usable_headings = [\n        h for h in headings if min_heading_level <= len(h.group(1)) <= max_heading_level\n    ]\n\n    if usable_headings:\n        levels_present = sorted(set(len(h.group(1)) for h in usable_headings))\n        split_level = levels_present[0]\n        split_headings = [h for h in usable_headings if len(h.group(1)) == split_level]\n\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(split_headings):\n            title = h.group(2).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = split_headings[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(split_headings) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, False))\n        return entries\n\n    heuristic_hits = list(HEURISTIC_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(text))\n    if heuristic_hits:\n        entries = []\n        for i, h in enumerate(heuristic_hits):\n            title = h.group(1).strip()\n            start = h.end()\n            end = heuristic_hits[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(heuristic_hits) else len(text)\n            body = text[start:end].strip()\n            entries.append((title, body, True))\n        return entries\n\n    return [(\"Untitled\", text.strip(), True)]\n```\n\n**`src\\ingest\\parse_corpus.py`** \u2014 full file:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"\nWalks data/raw/{wiki,codex,chronicles,ephemera,[images]}/ and ingests every\nfile found, regardless of extension.\n\nSKIP_OCR: OCR disabled by default -- see docs/limitations.md. Flip to False\nto re-enable later on faster hardware.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom src.models.document import SourceType\nfrom src.ingest.parse_document import ingest_file\n\n\nSKIP_OCR = True\n\nTOPIC_FOLDERS = {\n    \"wiki\": SourceType.WIKI,\n    \"codex\": SourceType.CODEX,\n    \"chronicles\": SourceType.CHRONICLE,\n    \"ephemera\": SourceType.EPHEMERA,\n}\nif not SKIP_OCR:\n    TOPIC_FOLDERS[\"images\"] = SourceType.IMAGE\n\n\ndef _is_ocr_file(file_path: Path) -> bool:\n    if file_path.suffix.lower() in (\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\"):\n        return True\n    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(\".scan.pdf\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef ingest_corpus(raw_data_dir: str = \"data/raw\"):\n    all_documents = []\n    report = {\"parsed_files\": 0, \"documents_created\": 0, \"needs_review\": [],\n               \"failed\": [], \"skipped_ocr\": [], \"id_collisions\": []}\n    seen_doc_ids = set()\n\n    for folder_name, source_type in TOPIC_FOLDERS.items():\n        folder = Path(raw_data_dir) / folder_name\n        if not folder.exists():\n            continue\n\n        for file_path in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")):\n            if not file_path.is_file():\n                continue\n\n            if SKIP_OCR and _is_ocr_file(file_path):\n                report[\"skipped_ocr\"].append(str(file_path))\n                continue\n\n            try:\n                print(f\"  parsing: {file_path.name}\", flush=True)\n                docs = ingest_file(str(file_path), source_type)\n\n                for d in docs:\n                    if d.doc_id in seen_doc_ids:\n                        original_id = d.doc_id\n                        counter = 2\n                        while f\"{original_id}_dup{counter}\" in seen_doc_ids:\n                            counter += 1\n                        d.doc_id = f\"{original_id}_dup{counter}\"\n                        report[\"id_collisions\"].append({\"original\": original_id, \"renamed_to\": d.doc_id})\n                    seen_doc_ids.add(d.doc_id)\n\n                all_documents.extend(docs)\n                report[\"parsed_files\"] += 1\n                report[\"documents_created\"] += len(docs)\n                for d in docs:\n                    if d.metadata.get(\"needs_review\"):\n                        report[\"needs_review\"].append(d.doc_id)\n            except Exception as e:\n                report[\"failed\"].append({\"file\": str(file_path), \"error\": str(e)})\n\n    return all_documents, report\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    docs, report = ingest_corpus()\n\n    print(f\"Files parsed:      {report['parsed_files']}\")\n    print(f\"Documents created: {report['documents_created']}\")\n    print(f\"Skipped (OCR disabled): {len(report['skipped_ocr'])}\")\n    print(f\"ID collisions auto-renamed: {len(report['id_collisions'])}\")\n    for c in report[\"id_collisions\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {c['original']} -> {c['renamed_to']}\")\n    print(f\"Needs manual review (heuristic split, verify these): {len(report['needs_review'])}\")\n    for doc_id in report[\"needs_review\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {doc_id}\")\n    print(f\"Failed: {len(report['failed'])}\")\n    for f in report[\"failed\"]:\n        print(f\"  - {f['file']}: {f['error']}\")\n\n    print(\"\\n--- Sample of parsed documents ---\")\n    for d in docs[:8]:\n        print(f\"[{d.source_type.value:10s}] {d.doc_id:45s} reliability={d.reliability_prior} \"\n              f\"entities={len(d.entities)} tables={len(d.tables)} chars={len(d.raw_text)}\")\n```\n\nAll 3 saved \u2192 clear cache \u2192 quick On the deliverables side there's still architecture/decisions/limitations docs, diagrams, the AI usage disclosure and chat log export, the README, a git history cleanup check, demo video planning, and the final submission report.\n\nRounding out the list: final testing on tricky conflict questions, citation/source display in answers (partially done via the sources field), a requirements.txt/.env.example for reproducibility, and a configuration-example folder per the submission structure. I'm also flagging the open model-choice decision and whether to add wikilink-based entity search alongside vector search to better mimic human-style lookup.\u2026Good moment for this \u2014 here's the full remaining roadmap, split into \"just needs running\" vs. \"needs your actual input.\"\n\n## Just needs running (no decisions, whenever you're free)\n1. Check the `.docx`/`.pdf` duplicate-book issue we flagged (same file, two formats?)\n\n## Needs your actual input \u2014 this is where your feedback matters\n\n**1. Which chat model for the agent's reasoning?**\nRight now it's `openrouter/free`, an auto-router across whatever free models are up. Convenient, but unpredictable \u2014 different runs might get different quality/JSON-compliance. Alternative: pin one specific free model for consistency, at the cost of flexibility. Your call once you see how `openrouter/free` performs in the batch test.\n\n**2. Search strategy \u2014 pure semantic, or also entity-based?**\nRight now the agent only searches by meaning (vector similarity). But remember the wiki files have `[[wikilinks]]` \u2014 a clean entity graph we're not using yet. A human researcher, given \"who commands Fenspire,\" would likely search the literal term \"Fenspire\" and follow links, not just semantic vibes. Adding entity-exact-match as a second retrieval path (alongside vector search) might genuinely improve \"search like a human\" fidelity \u2014 and it's a nice thing to point to in your report as deliberate design, not default RAG. Worth building, or good enough as-is?\n\n**3. Should the agent be allowed to say \"I don't know\"?**\nCurrently if it hits 5 iterations without confidence, it's forced to answer anyway. "toolu_01Mo5mhk9QwtEELhvve3cvaM", "name": "create_file", "input": {"description": "Hybrid search: semantic vector search + exact-phrase entity matching, merged", "file_text": "\"\"\"\nThe agent's search tool -- now HYBRID, not pure semantic.\n\nWHY: a human researcher given \"who commands Fenspire?\" doesn't just search\nby vague meaning -- they search the literal name \"Fenspire\" too. Pure\nvector search can miss an exact-name hit if the surrounding phrasing\ndiffers enough. So every search now does TWO things and merges results:\n\n  1. SEMANTIC: embed the query, vector search (as before) -- good for\n     conceptual/paraphrased questions.\n  2. KEYWORD: pull out capitalized proper-noun-looking phrases from the\n     query (e.g. \"Fenspire\", \"Gauntlet of Sorrowfell\") and do an exact\n     substring match against chunk text via ChromaDB's $contains filter --\n     good for \"does this specific named thing appear here\" questions,\n     which is most of what this corpus's fact-lookup questions are.\n\nEach result is tagged with which method(s) found it -- useful for\ndebugging and for your report (\"our system uses hybrid retrieval, not\njust off-the-shelf vector search\" is a real, demonstrable design choice).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom src.embed.embed_and_store import get_client, EMBEDDING_MODEL, CHROMA_DB_PATH, COLLECTION_NAME\nimport chromadb\n\n\nPROPER_NOUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z']+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z']+){0,4}\\b\")\nQUESTION_STOPWORDS = {\n    \"What\", \"Which\", \"Who\", \"Where\", \"When\", \"How\", \"Why\", \"In\", \"On\", \"At\",\n    \"The\", \"Is\", \"Does\", \"Did\", \"According\", \"State\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SearchResult:\n    chunk_id: str\n    text: str\n    title: str\n    source_type: str\n    reliability_prior: float\n    doc_id: str\n    found_by: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # \"semantic\" and/or \"keyword\"\n\n\ndef _extract_entity_candidates(query: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Pull likely proper-noun phrases out of a question, dropping common\n    question-word false positives that get capitalized by sentence position.\"\"\"\n    candidates = PROPER_NOUN_PATTERN.findall(query)\n    return [c for c in candidates if c not in QUESTION_STOPWORDS and len(c) > 2]\n\n\ndef search_corpus(query: str, n_results: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:\n    chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)\n    collection = chroma_client.get_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n\n    merged: dict[str, SearchResult] = {}  # keyed by chunk_id, for clean dedup\n\n    # 1. Semantic search\n    client = get_client()\n    query_embedding = client.embeddings.create(\n        model=EMBEDDING_MODEL, input=[query], encoding_format=\"float\"\n    ).data[0].embedding\n    semantic = collection.query(query_embeddings=[query_embedding], n_results=n_results)\n\n    for i in range(len(semantic[\"ids\"][0])):\n        chunk_id = semantic[\"ids\"][0][i]\n        meta = semantic[\"metadatas\"][0][i]\n        merged[chunk_id] = SearchResult(\n            chunk_id=chunk_id,\n            text=semantic[\"documents\"][0][i],\n            title=meta[\"title\"],\n            source_type=meta[\"source_type\"],\n            reliability_prior=meta[\"reliability_prior\"],\n            doc_id=meta[\"doc_id\"],\n            found_by=[\"semantic\"],\n        )\n\n    # 2. Keyword/entity search -- exact substring match per candidate entity\n    for entity in _extract_entity_candidates(query):\n        try:\n            keyword_hits = collection.get(\n                where_document={\"$contains\": entity}, limit=n_results\n            )\n        except Exception:\n            continue  # ChromaDB version differences -- fail soft, semantic results still stand\n\n        for i, chunk_id in enumerate(keyword_hits[\"ids\"]):\n            meta = keyword_hits[\"metadatas\"][i]\n            if chunk_id in merged:\n                if \"keyword\" not in merged[chunk_id].found_by:\n                    merged[chunk_id].found_by.append(\"keyword\")\n            else:\n                merged[chunk_id] = SearchResult(\n                    chunk_id=chunk_id,\n                    text=keyword_hits[\"documents\"][i],\n                    title=meta[\"title\"],\n                    source_type=meta[\"source_type\"],\n                    reliability_prior=meta[\"reliability_prior\"],\n                    doc_id=meta[\"doc_id\"],\n                    found_by=[\"keyword\"],\n                )\n\n    return list(merged.values())\n", "path": "/home/claude/ashen-agent/src/agent/search_tool.py"}, "message": "Hybrid search: semantic vector search + exact-phrase entity matching, merged", "integration_name": "File Creation", "integration_icon_url": null, "tool_identifier": null, "icon_name": "file", "context": null, "display_content": {"type": "code_block", "language": "python", "code": "\"\"\"\nThe agent's search tool -- now HYBRID, not pure semantic.\n\nWHY: a human researcher given \"who commands Fenspire?\" doesn't just search\nby vague meaning -- they search the literal name \"Fenspire\" too. Pure\nvector search can miss an exact-name hit if the surrounding phrasing\ndiffers enough. So every search now does TWO things and merges results:\n\n  1. SEMANTIC: embed the query, vector search (as before) -- good for\n     conceptual/paraphrased questions.\n  2. KEYWORD: pull out capitalized proper-noun-looking phrases from the\n     query (e.g. \"Fenspire\", \"Gauntlet of Sorrowfell\") and do an exact\n     substring match against chunk text via ChromaDB's $contains filter --\n     good for \"does this specific named thing appear here\" questions,\n     which is most of what this corpus's fact-lookup questions are.\n\nEach result is tagged with which method(s) found it -- useful for\ndebugging and for your report (\"our system uses hybrid retrieval, not\njust off-the-shelf vector search\" is a real, demonstrable design choice).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom src.embed.embed_and_store import get_client, EMBEDDING_MODEL, CHROMA_DB_PATH, COLLECTION_NAME\nimport chromadb\n\n\nPROPER_NOUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z']+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z']+){0,4}\\b\")\nQUESTION_STOPWORDS = {\n    \"What\", \"Which\", \"Who\", \"Where\", \"When\", \"How\", \"Why\", \"In\", \"On\", \"At\",\n    \"The\", \"Is\", \"Does\", \"Did\", \"According\", \"State\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SearchResult:\n    chunk_id: str\n    text: str\n    title: str\n    source_type: str\n    reliability_prior: float\n    doc_id: str\n    found_by: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # \"semantic\" and/or \"keyword\"\n\n\ndef _extract_entity_candidates(query: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Pull likely proper-noun phrases out of a question, dropping common\n    question-word false positives that get capitalized by sentence position.\"\"\"\n    candidates = PROPER_NOUN_PATTERN.findall(query)\n    return [c for c in candidates if c not in QUESTION_STOPWORDS and len(c) > 2]\n\n\ndef search_corpus(query: str, n_results: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:\n    chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=CHROMA_DB_PATH)\n    collection = chroma_client.get_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)\n\n    merged: dict[str, SearchResult] = {}  # keyed by chunk_id, for clean dedup\n\n    # 1. Semantic search\n    client = get_client()\n    query_embedding = client.embeddings.create(\n        model=EMBEDDING_MODEL, input=[query], encoding_format=\"float\"\n    ).data[0].embedding\n    semantic = collection.query(query_embeddings=[query_embedding], n_results=n_results)\n\n    for i in range(len(semantic[\"ids\"][0])):\n        chunk_id = semantic[\"ids\"][0][i]\n        meta = semantic[\"metadatas\"][0][i]\n        merged[chunk_id] = SearchResult(\n            chunk_id=chunk_id,\n            text=semantic[\"documents\"][0][i],\n            title=meta[\"title\"],\n            source_type=meta[\"source_type\"],\n            reliability_prior=meta[\"reliability_prior\"],\n            doc_id=meta[\"doc_id\"],\n            found_by=[\"semantic\"],\n        )\n\n    # 2. Keyword/entity search -- exact substring match per candidate entity\n    for entity in _extract_entity_candidates(query):\n        try:\n            keyword_hits = collection.get(\n                where_document={\"$contains\": entity}, limit=n_results\n            )\n        except Exception:\n            continue  # ChromaDB version differences -- fail soft, semantic results still stand\n\n        for i, chunk_id in enumerate(keyword_hits[\"ids\"]):\n            meta = keyword_hits[\"metadatas\"][i]\n            if chunk_id in merged:\n                if \"keyword\" not in merged[chunk_id].found_by:\n                    merged[chunk_id].found_by.append(\"keyword\")\n            else:\n                merged[chunk_id] = SearchResult(\n                    chunk_id=chunk_id,\n                    text=keyword_hits[\"documents\"][i],\n                    title=meta[\"title\"],\n                    source_type=meta[\"source_type\"],\n                    reliability_prior=meta[\"reliability_prior\"],\n                    doc_id=meta[\"doc_id\"],\n                    found_by=[\"keyword\"],\n                )\n\n    return list(merged.values())\n",
