"/mnt/user-data/outputs/DWBI_Lecture5_ExamPrep.md", "file_text": "# IT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence\n## Lecture 05 Exam Prep: Data Integration, Extraction, Profiling & Quality\n\n---\n\n# SECTION 1: MCQs (25 Questions \u2014 Multiple Correct Answers)\n\n**Instructions:** Each question has 2\u20133 correct options. Select all that apply.\n\n---\n\n**Q1.** A retail chain wants a live dashboard that pulls current inventory counts directly from three regional warehouse databases, without storing a copy anywhere. Which statements justify choosing **Data Federation** here?\n\na) Data stays in the original source systems at all times\nb) A mediated/virtual schema presents a unified view to the dashboard\nc) Historical trend analysis over 5 years will be fast and efficient\nd) Query results are integrated and transformed dynamically at run-time\ne) Data is physically copied into a central repository nightly\n\n---\n\n**Q2.** A bank replicates every transaction from its core banking system to a fraud-detection system the instant it occurs. Which technique(s) and reasoning apply?\n\na) This is Data Propagation, since changes are copied to target systems\nb) This could be event-driven since the trigger is the transaction itself\nc) This is Data Federation because no physical copy occurs\nd) This could be implemented using Enterprise Data Replication (EDR)\ne) Full extraction must be used since propagation requires complete datasets\n\n---\n\n**Q3.** An organization builds a central repository combining 5 years of HR, sales, and finance data purely for BI reporting and trend analysis. Which are true of this approach?\n\na) This is Data Consolidation\nb) Data is physically moved and typically transformed before storage\nc) Updates always occur in true real-time with zero latency\nd) The repository can serve as a central source for downstream analytics\ne) No transformation or cleaning is ever required before loading\n\n---\n\n**Q4.** Referring to the university activity: the university wants a dashboard showing **current student information without copying data into another database**. Which reasons support the chosen technique?\n\na) Data Federation avoids physical duplication of data\nb) A virtual/mediated schema can serve real-time queries on demand\nc) Data Consolidation is better since it guarantees no latency\nd) Data Propagation is unnecessary since no data movement is required\ne) Batch loading is required to keep the dashboard updated\n\n---\n\n**Q5.** The university wants **student payment updates copied immediately** from the Finance System to the reporting database. Which justify using Data Propagation here?\n\na) Immediate copying suggests an event-driven or synchronous update\nb) EAI or EDR mechanisms could implement this transfer\nc) Data Federation is preferred since payments must never be duplicated\nd) This differs from consolidation because updates are continuous, not batch-delayed\ne) This requires full extraction of five years of payment history each time\n\n---\n\n**Q6.** The university wants **five years of student performance data for BI reports**. Which statements are correct?\n\na) Data Consolidation fits since a persistent, transformed dataset is needed\nb) Batch updates are acceptable since real-time freshness isn't required\nc) Data Federation is ideal because it avoids storing historical data\nd) The consolidated store becomes the analytical source of truth\ne) Propagation is mandatory since historical data must be event-driven\n\n---\n\n**Q7.** An ODS is being introduced between four operational systems and a data warehouse. Which of these are legitimate justifications for adding it?\n\na) It reduces query workload directly on operational/transactional systems\nb) It provides a near real-time, integrated view of current operational data\nc) It permanently replaces the need for a data warehouse\nd) It can clean and transform data before it reaches the DW\ne) It only stores historical data older than 10 years\n\n---\n\n**Q8.** A company extracts data from a mix of relational databases, flat files, JSON documents, and third-party REST APIs. Which ETL considerations are most relevant to this mixed-source scenario?\n\na) Data source connectivity and security differ across each source type\nb) Different sources may require different extraction frequencies\nc) All sources will always support real-time extraction equally well\nd) Legacy systems and APIs may need different extraction tooling/capabilities\ne) File-based sources eliminate the need to check data quality\n\n---\n\n**Q9.** A company can only extract from its production database during a narrow 2 AM\u20133 AM maintenance window. Which statements correctly reflect this constraint?\n\na) This is an extraction window limitation\nb) Scheduling extraction during off-peak hours minimizes operational impact\nc) This constraint disappears automatically once incremental extraction is used\nd) Near real-time requirements would be difficult to satisfy under this window\ne) The extraction window has no relation to source system load\n\n---\n\n**Q10.** A supermarket's sales database holds 500 million transactions with 100,000 new transactions added daily. For nightly ETL refreshes, which choices are best justified?\n\na) Incremental extraction, since only new/modified records need processing\nb) Incremental extraction reduces resource usage compared to reloading all 500M rows\nc) Full extraction, since it guarantees the freshest possible data every run\nd) Full extraction is preferable purely because it is simpler to implement, regardless of cost\ne) Incremental extraction is commonly used for large, regularly updated warehouses\n\n---\n\n**Q11.** The supermarket's sales system automatically exports a daily transaction file to the warehouse without the warehouse requesting it. Which statements correctly describe this?\n\na) This is Push extraction, since the source initiates the transfer\nb) This approach is commonly paired with offline/incremental extraction\nc) This is Pull extraction, since data eventually reaches the warehouse\nd) The source system controls when the data becomes available\ne) This requires the warehouse to query the source every night\n\n---\n\n**Q12.** A data warehouse connects nightly to a CRM database and issues queries to fetch newly updated customer records. Which are accurate about this method?\n\na) This is Pull extraction, as the target initiates the request\nb) This is commonly associated with online extraction\nc) It can support either full or incremental extraction\nd) This is inherently a Push-based mechanism\ne) The source system decides independently when to send data, without being asked\n\n---\n\n**Q13.** Which scenario(s) correctly describe **Online Extraction**?\n\na) SQL queries are run directly against the live operational database\nb) Data can be retrieved in real-time or near real-time\nc) Data is first dumped into flat files before being read\nd) No intermediate staging storage is required\ne) It is typically the only method used for batch dump-file processing\n\n---\n\n**Q14.** Which scenario(s) correctly describe **Offline Extraction**?\n\na) The source system pushes data into separate staging storage first\nb) Extraction reads from staged files/dumps rather than the live system\nc) It commonly uses formats like CSV, TXT, or database dump files\nd) It requires direct real-time querying of the operational database\ne) It is usually associated with batch-oriented data movement\n\n---\n\n**Q15.** A data profiling team examines a \"CustomerID\" column and finds it has no nulls, all unique values, and a consistent numeric pattern. Which profiling activities were most likely performed?\n\na) Column profiling (nulls, uniqueness, data type checks)\nb) Cross-column profiling to test primary key candidacy\nc) Pattern discovery to check consistent formatting\nd) Cross-table profiling to find orphaned foreign keys\ne) Statistical analysis to compute standard deviation only\n\n---\n\n**Q16.** A profiling exercise checks whether every \"CustomerID\" in the Orders table actually exists in the Customers table. Which statement(s) are correct?\n\na) This is Cross-Table Profiling\nb) It helps detect orphaned records or missing links\nc) This is Column Profiling, since only one column is involved\nd) Foreign key relationships are being validated across tables\ne) This activity replaces the need for any statistical analysis\n\n---\n\n**Q17.** A dataset requires every \"Email\" field to match a valid email format, and every \"Age\" field to fall between 0\u2013120. Which profiling activity best matches this check, and what does it verify?\n\na) Data Rule Validation\nb) Checks compliance with business rules/formats\nc) Cross-Table Profiling, since two fields are compared across tables\nd) It can catch invalid values like negative ages\ne) It always requires comparing two separate tables\n\n---\n\n**Q18.** Analysts notice recurring formats like \"071-1234567\" in a phone number column and flag entries that don't match. Which is the most accurate description?\n\na) This is Pattern Discovery\nb) It helps identify formatting errors or inconsistent entries\nc) This is Cross-Column Profiling, since two columns are compared\nd) It can be used to spot malformed phone numbers, dates, or postal codes\ne) It replaces the need for column profiling entirely\n\n---\n\n**Q19.** Consider this sample data:\n| ID | Name | Age | Country |\n|----|------|-----|---------|\n| 1 | John | 35 | Sri Lanka |\n| 2 | John | 35 | LK |\n| 3 | Sara | -5 | Sri Lanka |\n| 4 | NULL | 40 | NULL |\n\nWhich data quality issues are present?\n\na) Possible duplicate record (rows 1 and 2 may represent the same person)\nb) Inconsistent representation of the same value (\"Sri Lanka\" vs \"LK\")\nc) An invalid/implausible value in the Age column (-5)\nd) All four rows are fully complete and accurate\ne) Missing values (nulls) exist in the Name and Country fields\n\n---\n\n**Q20.** From the same sample table above, which data quality dimensions are being violated?\n\na) Accuracy \u2014 negative age is not a valid real-world value\nb) Consistency \u2014 the same country is represented in two different formats\nc) Completeness \u2014 some fields contain NULL values\nd) Timeliness \u2014 the data is outdated and no longer current\ne) Uniqueness \u2014 duplicate customer entries are possibly present\n\n---\n\n**Q21.** Which of the following are valid reasons an organization would prefer **Data Federation** over **Data Consolidation**?\n\na) Real-time access to source data is needed without duplication effort\nb) Data volumes are small enough that on-demand querying performs well\nc) Long-term historical analytics across years of data is the primary goal\nd) Sources should remain authoritative and are queried only when needed\ne) A permanent, transformed, cleaned copy of all data is required upfront\n\n---\n\n**Q22.** Which of the following are valid reasons an organization would prefer **Data Consolidation** over **Data Federation**?\n\na) Heavy, repeated analytical queries need to run without hitting live source systems\nb) A single persistent store is needed for downstream BI tools\nc) Sources must never be queried more than once at extraction time\nd) Historical data needs to be retained beyond what source systems keep\ne) Every query must always reflect the absolute latest source-system state\n\n---\n\n**Q23.** A company needs to support both a nightly batch load (large historical refresh) and an hourly incremental update job on the same fact table. Which combination of concepts applies?\n\na) The nightly job likely uses full extraction; the hourly job uses incremental\nb) Extraction frequency requirements can differ across the same source system\nc) Both jobs must use push-based extraction only\nd) The hourly job benefits from processing only new/modified records\ne) Full and incremental extraction can never coexist in one ETL pipeline\n\n---\n\n**Q24.** An enterprise wants to reduce the load on operational systems while still enabling operational reporting and near real-time data access for daily business decisions. Which solution(s) address this need?\n\na) Introducing an Operational Data Store (ODS) as an intermediate layer\nb) Using the ODS to clean and transform data before it reaches the DW\nc) Directly querying live operational systems for every report, bypassing ODS\nd) Allowing the ODS to integrate data from multiple source systems\ne) Removing all data quality checks to speed up reporting\n\n---\n\n**Q25.** A legacy mainframe system cannot support live queries and only allows nightly dump-file generation, which is then read by the ETL tool. Which statements correctly apply to this situation?\n\na) This is best modeled as Offline Extraction\nb) The dump file acts as staged data outside the original source system\nc) This is Online Extraction since data eventually reaches the warehouse\nd) This scenario is more compatible with Push-based, batch-oriented delivery\ne) No extraction window limitations apply since data is dumped nightly\n\n---\n---\n\n# SECTION 2: ANSWER KEY\n\n| Q# | Correct Options |\n|----|-----------------|\n| 1  | a, b, d |\n| 2  | a, b, d |\n| 3  | a, b, d |\n| 4  | a, b, d |\n| 5  | a, b, d |\n| 6  | a, b, d |\n| 7  | a, b, d |\n| 8  | a, b, d |\n| 9  | a, b, d |\n| 10 | a, b, e |\n| 11 | a, b, d |\n| 12 | a, b, c |\n| 13 | a, b, d |\n| 14 | a, b, c (e also valid \u2014 accept a, b, c, e) |\n| 15 | a, c |\n| 16 | a, b, d |\n| 17 | a, b, d |\n| 18 | a, b, d |\n| 19 | a, b, c, e (any 2-3 most defensible: a, b, c) |\n| 20 | a, b, c, e (core: a, b, c) |\n| 21 | a, b, d |\n| 22 | a, b, d |\n| 23 | a, b, d |\n| 24 | a, b, d |\n| 25 | a, b, d |\n\n*Note: For Q14, Q19, Q20 more than 3 options are defensible; examiners may accept the broader set or narrow to the 3 strongest.*\n\n---\n---\n\n# SECTION 3: SHORT NOTES (Quick Revision)\n\n## 1. Data Integration \u2014 Core Idea\n- Combines data from multiple, possibly differently-formatted sources into a **unified view**.\n- Goals: remove data silos, improve accessibility, support enterprise-wide analysis.\n\n## 2. Operational Data Store (ODS)\n- Sits **between operational systems and the DW**.\n- Purpose: near real-time integrated view, reduces load on operational systems, cleans/transforms data before DW load, supports operational reporting.\n- **Not a replacement** for the DW \u2014 it's a bridge/staging layer.\n\n## 3. Three Key Integration Techniques\n\n| Technique | How it works | Data movement? | Best for |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Data Federation** | Virtual/mediated schema; queries hit sources live | No physical copy | Real-time views, no duplication needed |\n| **Data Propagation** | Copies changes from source \u2192 target (event-driven, sync, or async) | Yes, continuous/change-based | Immediate updates (e.g., payments, fraud detection) via **EAI** or **EDR** |\n| **Data Consolidation** | Physically moves, transforms, and stores data in one repository | Yes, batch/near-real-time/real-time | Long-term BI reporting, historical analytics |\n\n**Exam tip:** \"No copying + on-demand\" \u2192 Federation. \"Immediate/continuous copy of changes\" \u2192 Propagation. \"Central historical store for reporting\" \u2192 Consolidation.\n\n## 4. ETL \u2014 Key Considerations\n- **Source variety:** databases, files (CSV/XLSX), documents (JSON/XML), legacy systems, APIs \u2014 each has different connectivity/security needs.\n- **Frequency:** near real-time, hourly, daily, weekly.\n- **Extraction window:** limited time slots (often off-peak) to pull data; tighter for near-real-time needs.\n- **Source realities:** data quality issues, tool limitations, poor real-time support in older ETL tools.\n\n## 5. Extraction Types\n\n**Full vs Incremental**\n- **Full Extraction:** entire dataset every run \u2192 simple but resource-heavy.\n- **Incremental Extraction:** only new/changed data \u2192 efficient, preferred for large, frequently-updated warehouses.\n\n**Online vs Offline**\n- **Online:** direct access to live source, real-time capable, no staging needed.\n- **Offline:** data staged first (flat files/dumps), then extracted \u2192 typical for batch processing.\n\n**Push vs Pull**\n- **Push:** source sends data unprompted (source controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with incremental + offline extraction.\n- **Pull:** target requests/retrieves data (target controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with online extraction; supports both full and incremental.\n\n**Exam tip:** \"System automatically sends/exports\" = Push. \"Warehouse queries/connects to fetch\" = Pull.\n\n## 6. Data Profiling \u2014 6 Core Activities\n1. **Column Profiling** \u2013 types, lengths, nulls, uniqueness, frequency per field.\n2. **Statistical Analysis** \u2013 min, max, mean, mode, median, std deviation.\n3. **Cross-Column Profiling** \u2013 dependencies within a table; testing primary key candidates.\n4. **Cross-Table Profiling** \u2013 relationships between tables via foreign keys; finds orphaned records.\n5. **Data Rule Validation** \u2013 checks against business rules/formats/regulations.\n6. **Pattern Discovery** \u2013 finds recurring formats (phone numbers, dates, postal codes) to catch format errors.\n\n**Exam tip:** Single column \u2192 Column Profiling/Statistical Analysis. Same table, multiple columns \u2192 Cross-Column. Multiple tables \u2192 Cross-Table. Format-based checks \u2192 Pattern Discovery. Rule/regulation-based checks \u2192 Data Rule Validation.\n\n## 7. Data Quality Dimensions (apply to sample data problems)\n- **Accuracy** \u2013 values reflect real-world truth (e.g., Age = -5 is inaccurate).\n- **Completeness** \u2013 no missing/NULL values.\n- **Consistency** \u2013 same fact represented the same way everywhere (e.g., \"Sri Lanka\" vs \"LK\").\n- **Uniqueness** \u2013 no unintended duplicate records.\n- **Timeliness** \u2013 data is current enough for use.\n- **Validity** \u2013 data conforms to defined formats/rules.\n\n## 8. Quick Decision Framework (for situational questions)\n- **No duplication + live access needed** \u2192 Federation\n- **Immediate/continuous sync of changes** \u2192 Propagation (EAI/EDR)\n- **Central historical repository for BI** \u2192 Consolidation\n- **Large volume + frequent updates** \u2192 Incremental extraction\n- **Source initiates transfer** \u2192 Push; **Target initiates transfer** \u2192 Pull\n- **Direct live query** \u2192 Online; **Staged file first** \u2192 Offline\n- **Checking one field** \u2192 Column Profiling; **checking across tables** \u2192 Cross-Table Profiling\n"}, "message": "Create exam prep document with MCQs, answer key, and short notes for Lecture 5", "integration_name": "File Creation", "integration_icon_url": null, "tool_identifier": null, "icon_name": "file", "context": null, "display_content": {"type": "code_block", "language": "markdown", "code": "# IT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence\n## Lecture 05 Exam Prep: Data Integration, Extraction, Profiling & Quality\n\n---\n\n# SECTION 1: MCQs (25 Questions \u2014 Multiple Correct Answers)\n\n**Instructions:** Each question has 2\u20133 correct options. Which technique(s) and reasoning apply?\n\na) This is Data Propagation, since changes are copied to target systems\nb) This could be event-driven since the trigger is the transaction itself\nc) This is Data Federation because no physical copy occurs\nd) This could be implemented using Enterprise Data Replication (EDR)\ne) Full extraction must be used since propagation requires complete datasets\n\n---\n\n**Q3.** An organization builds a central repository combining 5 years of HR, sales, and finance data purely for BI reporting and trend analysis. Which are true of this approach?\n\na) This is Data Consolidation\nb) Data is physically moved and typically transformed before storage\nc) Updates always occur in true real-time with zero latency\nd) The repository can serve as a central source for downstream analytics\ne) No transformation or cleaning is ever required before loading\n\n---\n\n**Q4.** Referring to the university activity: the university wants a dashboard showing **current student information without copying data into another database**. Which reasons support the chosen technique?\n\na) Data Federation avoids physical duplication of data\nb) A virtual/mediated schema can serve real-time queries on demand\nc) Data Consolidation is better since it guarantees no latency\nd) Data Propagation is unnecessary since no data movement is required\ne) Batch loading is required to keep the dashboard updated\n\n---\n\n**Q5.** The university wants **student payment updates copied immediately** from the Finance System to the reporting database. Which justify using Data Propagation here?\n\na) Immediate copying suggests an event-driven or synchronous update\nb) EAI or EDR mechanisms could implement this transfer\nc) Data Federation is preferred since payments must never be duplicated\nd) This differs from consolidation because updates are continuous, not batch-delayed\ne) This requires full extraction of five years of payment history each time\n\n---\n\n**Q6.** The university wants **five years of student performance data for BI reports**. Which statements are correct?\n\na) Data Consolidation fits since a persistent, transformed dataset is needed\nb) Batch updates are acceptable since real-time freshness isn't required\nc) Data Federation is ideal because it avoids storing historical data\nd) The consolidated store becomes the analytical source of truth\ne) Propagation is mandatory since historical data must be event-driven\n\n---\n\n**Q7.** An ODS is being introduced between four operational systems and a data warehouse. Which of these are legitimate justifications for adding it?\n\na) It reduces query workload directly on operational/transactional systems\nb) It provides a near real-time, integrated view of current operational data\nc) It permanently replaces the need for a data warehouse\nd) It can clean and transform data before it reaches the DW\ne) It only stores historical data older than 10 years\n\n---\n\n**Q8.** A company extracts data from a mix of relational databases, flat files, JSON documents, and third-party REST APIs. Which ETL considerations are most relevant to this mixed-source scenario?\n\na) Data source connectivity and security differ across each source type\nb) Different sources may require different extraction frequencies\nc) All sources will always support real-time extraction equally well\nd) Legacy systems and APIs may need different extraction tooling/capabilities\ne) File-based sources eliminate the need to check data quality\n\n---\n\n**Q9.** A company can only extract from its production database during a narrow 2 AM\u20133 AM maintenance window. Which statements correctly reflect this constraint?\n\na) This is an extraction window limitation\nb) Scheduling extraction during off-peak hours minimizes operational impact\nc) This constraint disappears automatically once incremental extraction is used\nd) Near real-time requirements would be difficult to satisfy under this window\ne) The extraction window has no relation to source system load\n\n---\n\n**Q10.** A supermarket's sales database holds 500 million transactions with 100,000 new transactions added daily. For nightly ETL refreshes, which choices are best justified?\n\na) Incremental extraction, since only new/modified records need processing\nb) Incremental extraction reduces resource usage compared to reloading all 500M rows\nc) Full extraction, since it guarantees the freshest possible data every run\nd) Full extraction is preferable purely because it is simpler to implement, regardless of cost\ne) Incremental extraction is commonly used for large, regularly updated warehouses\n\n---\n\n**Q11.** The supermarket's sales system automatically exports a daily transaction file to the warehouse without the warehouse requesting it. Which statements correctly describe this?\n\na) This is Push extraction, since the source initiates the transfer\nb) This approach is commonly paired with offline/incremental extraction\nc) This is Pull extraction, since data eventually reaches the warehouse\nd) The source system controls when the data becomes available\ne) This requires the warehouse to query the source every night\n\n---\n\n**Q12.** A data warehouse connects nightly to a CRM database and issues queries to fetch newly updated customer records. Which are accurate about this method?\n\na) This is Pull extraction, as the target initiates the request\nb) This is commonly associated with online extraction\nc) It can support either full or incremental extraction\nd) This is inherently a Push-based mechanism\ne) The source system decides independently when to send data, without being asked\n\n---\n\n**Q13.** Which scenario(s) correctly describe **Online Extraction**?\n\na) SQL queries are run directly against the live operational database\nb) Data can be retrieved in real-time or near real-time\nc) Data is first dumped into flat files before being read\nd) No intermediate staging storage is required\ne) It is typically the only method used for batch dump-file processing\n\n---\n\n**Q14.** Which scenario(s) correctly describe **Offline Extraction**?\n\na) The source system pushes data into separate staging storage first\nb) Extraction reads from staged files/dumps rather than the live system\nc) It commonly uses formats like CSV, TXT, or database dump files\nd) It requires direct real-time querying of the operational database\ne) It is usually associated with batch-oriented data movement\n\n---\n\n**Q15.** A data profiling team examines a \"CustomerID\" column and finds it has no nulls, all unique values, and a consistent numeric pattern. Which profiling activities were most likely performed?\n\na) Column profiling (nulls, uniqueness, data type checks)\nb) Cross-column profiling to test primary key candidacy\nc) Pattern discovery to check consistent formatting\nd) Cross-table profiling to find orphaned foreign keys\ne) Statistical analysis to compute standard deviation only\n\n---\n\n**Q16.** A profiling exercise checks whether every \"CustomerID\" in the Orders table actually exists in the Customers table. Which statement(s) are correct?\n\na) This is Cross-Table Profiling\nb) It helps detect orphaned records or missing links\nc) This is Column Profiling, since only one column is involved\nd) Foreign key relationships are being validated across tables\ne) This activity replaces the need for any statistical analysis\n\n---\n\n**Q17.** A dataset requires every \"Email\" field to match a valid email format, and every \"Age\" field to fall between 0\u2013120. Which profiling activity best matches this check, and what does it verify?\n\na) Data Rule Validation\nb) Checks compliance with business rules/formats\nc) Cross-Table Profiling, since two fields are compared across tables\nd) It can catch invalid values like negative ages\ne) It always requires comparing two separate tables\n\n---\n\n**Q18.** Analysts notice recurring formats like \"071-1234567\" in a phone number column and flag entries that don't match. Which is the most accurate description?\n\na) This is Pattern Discovery\nb) It helps identify formatting errors or inconsistent entries\nc) This is Cross-Column Profiling, since two columns are compared\nd) It can be used to spot malformed phone numbers, dates, or postal codes\ne) It replaces the need for column profiling entirely\n\n---\n\n**Q19.** Consider this sample data:\n| ID | Name | Age | Country |\n|----|------|-----|---------|\n| 1 | John | 35 | Sri Lanka |\n| 2 | John | 35 | LK |\n| 3 | Sara | -5 | Sri Lanka |\n| 4 | NULL | 40 | NULL |\n\nWhich data quality issues are present?\n\na) Possible duplicate record (rows 1 and 2 may represent the same person)\nb) Inconsistent representation of the same value (\"Sri Lanka\" vs \"LK\")\nc) An invalid/implausible value in the Age column (-5)\nd) All four rows are fully complete and accurate\ne) Missing values (nulls) exist in the Name and Country fields\n\n---\n\n**Q20.** From the same sample table above, which data quality dimensions are being violated?\n\na) Accuracy \u2014 negative age is not a valid real-world value\nb) Consistency \u2014 the same country is represented in two different formats\nc) Completeness \u2014 some fields contain NULL values\nd) Timeliness \u2014 the data is outdated and no longer current\ne) Uniqueness \u2014 duplicate customer entries are possibly present\n\n---\n\n**Q21.** Which of the following are valid reasons an organization would prefer **Data Federation** over **Data Consolidation**?\n\na) Real-time access to source data is needed without duplication effort\nb) Data volumes are small enough that on-demand querying performs well\nc) Long-term historical analytics across years of data is the primary goal\nd) Sources should remain authoritative and are queried only when needed\ne) A permanent, transformed, cleaned copy of all data is required upfront\n\n---\n\n**Q22.** Which of the following are valid reasons an organization would prefer **Data Consolidation** over **Data Federation**?\n\na) Heavy, repeated analytical queries need to run without hitting live source systems\nb) A single persistent store is needed for downstream BI tools\nc) Sources must never be queried more than once at extraction time\nd) Historical data needs to be retained beyond what source systems keep\ne) Every query must always reflect the absolute latest source-system state\n\n---\n\n**Q23.** A company needs to support both a nightly batch load (large historical refresh) and an hourly incremental update job on the same fact table. Which combination of concepts applies?\n\na) The nightly job likely uses full extraction; the hourly job uses incremental\nb) Extraction frequency requirements can differ across the same source system\nc) Both jobs must use push-based extraction only\nd) The hourly job benefits from processing only new/modified records\ne) Full and incremental extraction can never coexist in one ETL pipeline\n\n---\n\n**Q24.** An enterprise wants to reduce the load on operational systems while still enabling operational reporting and near real-time data access for daily business decisions. Which solution(s) address this need?\n\na) Introducing an Operational Data Store (ODS) as an intermediate layer\nb) Using the ODS to clean and transform data before it reaches the DW\nc) Directly querying live operational systems for every report, bypassing ODS\nd) Allowing the ODS to integrate data from multiple source systems\ne) Removing all data quality checks to speed up reporting\n\n---\n\n**Q25.** A legacy mainframe system cannot support live queries and only allows nightly dump-file generation, which is then read by the ETL tool. Which statements correctly apply to this situation?\n\na) This is best modeled as Offline Extraction\nb) The dump file acts as staged data outside the original source system\nc) This is Online Extraction since data eventually reaches the warehouse\nd) This scenario is more compatible with Push-based, batch-oriented delivery\ne) No extraction window limitations apply since data is dumped nightly\n\n---\n---\n\n# SECTION 2: ANSWER KEY\n\n| Q# | Correct Options |\n|----|-----------------|\n| 1  | a, b, d |\n| 2  | a, b, d |\n| 3  | a, b, d |\n| 4  | a, b, d |\n| 5  | a, b, d |\n| 6  | a, b, d |\n| 7  | a, b, d |\n| 8  | a, b, d |\n| 9  | a, b, d |\n| 10 | a, b, e |\n| 11 | a, b, d |\n| 12 | a, b, c |\n| 13 | a, b, d |\n| 14 | a, b, c (e also valid \u2014 accept a, b, c, e) |\n| 15 | a, c |\n| 16 | a, b, d |\n| 17 | a, b, d |\n| 18 | a, b, d |\n| 19 | a, b, c, e (any 2-3 most defensible: a, b, c) |\n| 20 | a, b, c, e (core: a, b, c) |\n| 21 | a, b, d |\n| 22 | a, b, d |\n| 23 | a, b, d |\n| 24 | a, b, d |\n| 25 | a, b, d |\n\n*Note: For Q14, Q19, Q20 more than 3 options are defensible; examiners may accept the broader set or narrow to the 3 strongest.*\n\n---\n---\n\n# SECTION 3: SHORT NOTES (Quick Revision)\n\n## 1. Data Integration \u2014 Core Idea\n- Combines data from multiple, possibly differently-formatted sources into a **unified view**.\n- Goals: remove data silos, improve accessibility, support enterprise-wide analysis.\n\n## 2. Operational Data Store (ODS)\n- Sits **between operational systems and the DW**.\n- Purpose: near real-time integrated view, reduces load on operational systems, cleans/transforms data before DW load, supports operational reporting.\n- **Not a replacement** for the DW \u2014 it's a bridge/staging layer.\n\n## 3. Three Key Integration Techniques\n\n| Technique | How it works | Data movement? | Best for |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Data Federation** | Virtual/mediated schema; queries hit sources live | No physical copy | Real-time views, no duplication needed |\n| **Data Propagation** | Copies changes from source \u2192 target (event-driven, sync, or async) | Yes, continuous/change-based | Immediate updates (e.g., payments, fraud detection) via **EAI** or **EDR** |\n| **Data Consolidation** | Physically moves, transforms, and stores data in one repository | Yes, batch/near-real-time/real-time | Long-term BI reporting, historical analytics |\n\n**Exam tip:** \"No copying + on-demand\" \u2192 Federation. \"Immediate/continuous copy of changes\" \u2192 Propagation. \"Central historical store for reporting\" \u2192 Consolidation.\n\n## 4. ETL \u2014 Key Considerations\n- **Source variety:** databases, files (CSV/XLSX), documents (JSON/XML), legacy systems, APIs \u2014 each has different connectivity/security needs.\n- **Frequency:** near real-time, hourly, daily, weekly.\n- **Extraction window:** limited time slots (often off-peak) to pull data; tighter for near-real-time needs.\n- **Source realities:** data quality issues, tool limitations, poor real-time support in older ETL tools.\n\n## 5. Extraction Types\n\n**Full vs Incremental**\n- **Full Extraction:** entire dataset every run \u2192 simple but resource-heavy.\n- **Incremental Extraction:** only new/changed data \u2192 efficient, preferred for large, frequently-updated warehouses.\n\n**Online vs Offline**\n- **Online:** direct access to live source, real-time capable, no staging needed.\n- **Offline:** data staged first (flat files/dumps), then extracted \u2192 typical for batch processing.\n\n**Push vs Pull**\n- **Push:** source sends data unprompted (source controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with incremental + offline extraction.\n- **Pull:** target requests/retrieves data (target controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with online extraction; supports both full and incremental.\n\n**Exam tip:** \"System automatically sends/exports\" = Push. \"Warehouse queries/connects to fetch\" = Pull.\n\n## 6. Data Profiling \u2014 6 Core Activities\n1. **Column Profiling** \u2013 types, lengths, nulls, uniqueness, frequency per field.\n2. **Statistical Analysis** \u2013 min, max, mean, mode, median, std deviation.\n3. **Cross-Column Profiling** \u2013 dependencies within a table; testing primary key candidates.\n4. **Cross-Table Profiling** \u2013 relationships between tables via foreign keys; finds orphaned records.\n5. **Data Rule Validation** \u2013 checks against business rules/formats/regulations.\n6. **Pattern Discovery** \u2013 finds recurring formats (phone numbers, dates, postal codes) to catch format errors.\n\n**Exam tip:** Single column \u2192 Column Profiling/Statistical Analysis. Same table, multiple columns \u2192 Cross-Column. Multiple tables \u2192 Cross-Table. Format-based checks \u2192 Pattern Discovery. Rule/regulation-based checks \u2192 Data Rule Validation.\n\n## 7. Data Quality Dimensions (apply to sample data problems)\n- **Accuracy** \u2013 values reflect real-world truth (e.g., Age = -5 is inaccurate).\n- **Completeness** \u2013 no missing/NULL values.\n- **Consistency** \u2013 same fact represented the same way everywhere (e.g., \"Sri Lanka\" vs \"LK\").\n- **Uniqueness** \u2013 no unintended duplicate records.\n- **Timeliness** \u2013 data is current enough for use.\n- **Validity** \u2013 data conforms to defined formats/rules.\n\n## 8. Quick Decision Framework (for situational questions)\n- **No duplication + live access needed** \u2192 Federation\n- **Immediate/continuous sync of changes** \u2192 Propagation (EAI/EDR)\n- **Central historical repository for BI** \u2192 Consolidation\n- **Large volume + frequent updates** \u2192 Incremental extraction\n- **Source initiates transfer** \u2192 Push; **Target initiates transfer** \u2192 Pull\n- **Direct live query** \u2192 Online; **Staged file first** \u2192 Offline\n- **Checking one field** \u2192 Column Profiling; **checking across tables** \u2192 Cross-Table Profiling\n", Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\"\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis\n     8\t\n     9\tA `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:\n    10\t\n    11\t| Task | Approach |\n    12\t|---|---|\n    13\t| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script \u2014 see gotchas below |\n    14\t| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` \u2192 edit `word/document.xml` \u2192 `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |\n    15\t| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |\n    16\t\n    17\t> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.\n    18\t\n    19\t## Creating with docx-js \u2014 gotchas\n    20\t\n    21\t`docx` is preinstalled \u2014 do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:\n    22\t\n    23\t- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1\u2033).\n    24\t- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` \u2014 docx-js swaps width/height internally.\n    25\t- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.\n    26\t- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).\n    27\t- **Lists:** never insert `\u2022` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.\n    28\t- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`\"png\"`, `\"jpg\"`, \u2026).\n    29\t- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**\n    30\t- **Never use `\\n`** \u2014 use separate `Paragraph` elements.\n    31\t- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.\n    32\t- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** \u2014 use a paragraph bottom border instead.\n    33\t- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.\n    34\t\n    35\t## Verify the output\n    36\t\n    37\tAfter writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:\n    38\t\n    39\t```bash\n    40\tpython scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx\n    41\tpdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page\n    42\tls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images\n    43\t```\n    44\t\n    45\t`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`\u2026`page-12.jpg`).\n    46\t\n    47\t## Editing existing documents\n    48\t\n    49\tLegacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.\n    50\t\n    51\t```bash\n    52\tunzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/\n    53\tfind unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries \u2014 docx from external parties is untrusted\n    54\tpython scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable\n    55\t# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place \u2014 do NOT reformat or pretty-print\n    56\t(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)\n    57\tpython scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues\n    58\t# redlining? add --author \"<the name you redlined under>\" to check every edit is tracked\n    59\t```\n    60\t\n    61\tWord splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).\n    62\t\n    63\t**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author \"<the name you redlined under>\"` (needs `--original`) \u2014 it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=\"..\" w:author=\"..\" w:date=\"..\"/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means \"merge this paragraph into the next\" \u2014 so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.\n    64\t\n    65\tTo produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.\n    66\t\n    67\tAccepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way \u2014 they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:\n    68\t\n    69\t- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.\n    70\t- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.\n    71\t\n    72\tAn empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.\n    73\t\n    74\t## Comments\n    75\t\n    76\tComments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper \u2014 directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:\n    77\t\n    78\t```bash\n    79\t# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)\n    80\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Fees & expenses cap is too low\"\n    81\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Agreed\" --parent 0\n    82\t\n    83\t# Against a .docx directly\n    84\tpython scripts/comment.py contract.docx \"This cap is too low\" -o annotated.docx\n    85\t```\n    86\t\n    87\tThe script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text \u2014 until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.\n    88\t\n    89\t## Dependencies\n    90\t\n    91\t`docx` (npm, preinstalled \u2014 install only if `require('docx')` fails) \u00b7 `pandoc` \u00b7 Extraction Types\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Full vs Incremental\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Full Extraction: entire dataset every run \u2192 simple but resource-heavy.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Incremental Extraction: only new/changed data \u2192 efficient, preferred for large, frequently-updated warehouses.\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Online vs Offline\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Online: direct access to live source, real-time capable, no staging needed.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Offline: data staged first (flat files/dumps), then extracted \u2192 typical for batch processing.\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Push vs Pull\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Push: source sends data unprompted (source controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with incremental + offline extraction.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pull: target requests/retrieves data (target controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with online extraction; supports both full and incremental.\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: \\\"System automatically sends/exports\\\" = Push. \\\"Warehouse queries/connects to fetch\\\" = Pull.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"6. Data Profiling \u2014 6 Core Activities\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Column Profiling \u2013 types, lengths, nulls, uniqueness, frequency per field.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Statistical Analysis \u2013 min, max, mean, mode, median, std deviation.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Cross-Column Profiling \u2013 dependencies within a table; testing primary key candidates.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Cross-Table Profiling \u2013 relationships between tables via foreign keys; finds orphaned records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Data Rule Validation \u2013 checks against business rules/formats/regulations.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pattern Discovery \u2013 finds recurring formats (phone numbers, dates, postal codes) to catch format errors.\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: Single column \u2192 Column Profiling/Statistical Analysis. Same table, multiple columns \u2192 Cross-Column. Multiple tables \u2192 Cross-Table. Format-based checks \u2192 Pattern Discovery. Rule/regulation-based checks \u2192 Data Rule Validation.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"7. Data Quality Dimensions\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Accuracy \u2013 values reflect real-world truth (e.g., Age = -5 is inaccurate).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Completeness \u2013 no missing/NULL values.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Consistency \u2013 same fact represented the same way everywhere (e.g., \\\"Sri Lanka\\\" vs \\\"LK\\\").\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Uniqueness \u2013 no unintended duplicate records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Timeliness \u2013 data is current enough for use.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Validity \u2013 data conforms to defined formats/rules.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"8. changes \u2192 Propagation (EAI/EDR)\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Central historical repository for BI \u2192 Consolidation\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Large volume + frequent updates \u2192 Incremental extraction\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Source initiates transfer \u2192 Push; Target initiates transfer \u2192 Pull\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Direct live query \u2192 Online; Staged require(\"fs\");\n\nconst PAGE_WIDTH_DXA = 12240; // US Letter width\nconst PAGE_HEIGHT_DXA = 15840;\nconst MARGIN = 1080; // 0.75\"\nconst USABLE_WIDTH = PAGE_WIDTH_DXA - MARGIN * 2;\n\nfunction HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\n\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA ----------\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A retail chain wants a live dashboard that pulls current inventory counts directly from three regional warehouse databases, without storing a copy anywhere. Which statements justify choosing Data Federation here?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Data stays in the original source systems at all times\",\n      \"A mediated/virtual schema presents a unified view to the dashboard\",\n      \"Historical trend analysis over 5 years will be fast and efficient\",\n      \"Query results are integrated and transformed dynamically at run-time\",\n      \"Data is physically copied into a central repository nightly\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A bank replicates every transaction from its core banking system to a fraud-detection system the instant it occurs. Which technique(s) and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Propagation, since changes are copied to target systems\",\n      \"This could be event-driven since the trigger is the transaction itself\",\n      \"This is Data Federation because no physical copy occurs\",\n      \"This could be implemented using Enterprise Data Replication (EDR)\",\n      \"Full extraction must be used since propagation requires complete datasets\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An organization builds a central repository combining 5 years of HR, sales, and finance data purely for BI reporting and trend analysis. Which are true of this approach?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Consolidation\",\n      \"Data is physically moved and typically transformed before storage\",\n      \"Updates always occur in true real-time with zero latency\",\n      \"The repository can serve as a central source for downstream analytics\",\n      \"No transformation or cleaning is ever required before loading\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"University activity: the university wants a dashboard showing current student information without copying data into another database. Which reasons support the chosen technique?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Data Federation avoids physical duplication of data\",\n      \"A virtual/mediated schema can serve real-time queries on demand\",\n      \"Data Consolidation is better since it guarantees no latency\",\n      \"Data Propagation is unnecessary since no data movement is required\",\n      \"Batch loading is required to keep the dashboard updated\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The university wants student payment updates copied immediately from the Finance System to the reporting database. Which justify using Data Propagation here?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Immediate copying suggests an event-driven or synchronous update\",\n      \"EAI or EDR mechanisms could implement this transfer\",\n      \"Data Federation is preferred since payments must never be duplicated\",\n      \"This differs from consolidation because updates are continuous, not batch-delayed\",\n      \"This requires full extraction of five years of payment history each time\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The university wants five years of student performance data for BI reports. Which statements are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Data Consolidation fits since a persistent, transformed dataset is needed\",\n      \"Batch updates are acceptable since real-time freshness isn't required\",\n      \"Data Federation is ideal because it avoids storing historical data\",\n      \"The consolidated store becomes the analytical source of truth\",\n      \"Propagation is mandatory since historical data must be event-driven\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An ODS is being introduced between four operational systems and a data warehouse. Which ETL considerations are most relevant to this mixed-source scenario?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Data source connectivity and security differ across each source type\",\n      \"Different sources may require different extraction frequencies\",\n      \"All sources will always support real-time extraction equally well\",\n      \"Legacy systems and APIs may need different extraction tooling/capabilities\",\n      \"File-based sources eliminate the need to check data quality\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company can only extract from its production database during a narrow 2 AM\u20133 AM maintenance window. Which statements correctly reflect this constraint?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is an extraction window limitation\",\n      \"Scheduling extraction during off-peak hours minimizes operational impact\",\n      \"This constraint disappears automatically once incremental extraction is used\",\n      \"Near real-time requirements would be difficult to satisfy under this window\",\n      \"The extraction window has no relation to source system load\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A supermarket's sales database holds 500 million transactions with 100,000 new transactions added daily. For nightly ETL refreshes, which choices are best justified?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Incremental extraction, since only new/modified records need processing\",\n      \"Incremental extraction reduces resource usage compared to reloading all 500M rows\",\n      \"Full extraction, since it guarantees the freshest possible data every run\",\n      \"Full extraction is preferable purely because it is simpler to implement, regardless of cost\",\n      \"Incremental extraction is commonly used for large, regularly updated warehouses\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The supermarket's sales system automatically exports a daily transaction file to the warehouse without the warehouse requesting it. Which are accurate about this method?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Pull extraction, as the target initiates the request\",\n      \"This is commonly associated with online extraction\",\n      \"It can support either full or incremental extraction\",\n      \"This is inherently a Push-based mechanism\",\n      \"The source system decides independently when to send data, without being asked\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which scenario(s) correctly describe Online Extraction?\",\n    options: [\n      \"SQL queries are run directly against the live operational database\",\n      \"Data can be retrieved in real-time or near real-time\",\n      \"Data is first dumped into flat files before being read\",\n      \"No intermediate staging storage is required\",\n      \"It is typically the only method used for batch dump-file processing\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which scenario(s) correctly describe Offline Extraction?\",\n    options: [\n      \"The source system pushes data into separate staging storage first\",\n      \"Extraction reads from staged files/dumps rather than the live system\",\n      \"It commonly uses formats like CSV, TXT, or database dump files\",\n      \"It requires direct real-time querying of the operational database\",\n      \"It is usually associated with batch-oriented data movement\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A data profiling team examines a \\\"CustomerID\\\" column and finds it has no nulls, all unique values, and a consistent numeric pattern. Three Key Integration Techniques\"));\nconst techRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Technique\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2200}), cell(\"How it works\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3400}), cell(\"Data movement?\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:1800}), cell(\"Best for\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2600})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Data Federation\", {width:2200}), cell(\"Virtual/mediated schema; queries hit sources live\", {width:3400}), cell(\"No physical copy\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Real-time views, no duplication needed\", {width:2600})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Data Propagation\", {width:2200}), cell(\"Copies changes from source to target (event-driven, sync, or async)\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Yes, continuous/change-based\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Immediate updates via EAI or EDR\", {width:2600})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Data Consolidation\", {width:2200}), cell(\"Physically moves, transforms, and stores data in one repository\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Yes, batch/near-real-time/real-time\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Long-term BI reporting, historical analytics\", {width:2600})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [2200,3400,1800,2600], rows: techRows }));\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: \\\"No copying + on-demand\\\" \u2192 Federation. \\\"Immediate/continuous copy of changes\\\" \u2192 Propagation. \\\"Central historical store for reporting\\\" \u2192 Consolidation.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"4. ETL \u2014 Key Considerations\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Source variety: databases, files (CSV/XLSX), documents (JSON/XML), legacy systems, APIs \u2014 each has different connectivity/security needs.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Frequency: near real-time, hourly, daily, weekly.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Extraction window: limited time slots (often off-peak) to pull data; tighter for near-real-time needs.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Source realities: data quality issues, tool limitations, poor real-time support in older ETL tools.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"5. Extraction Types\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Full vs Incremental\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Full Extraction: entire dataset every run \u2192 simple but resource-heavy.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Incremental Extraction: only new/changed data \u2192 efficient, preferred for large, frequently-updated warehouses.\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Online vs Offline\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Online: direct access to live source, real-time capable, no staging needed.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Offline: data staged first (flat files/dumps), then extracted \u2192 typical for batch processing.\"));\nchildren.push(h3(\"Push vs Pull\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Push: source sends data unprompted (source controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with incremental + offline extraction.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pull: target requests/retrieves data (target controls timing) \u2192 pairs well with online extraction; supports both full and incremental.\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: \\\"System automatically sends/exports\\\" = Push. \\\"Warehouse queries/connects to fetch\\\" = Pull.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"6. Data Profiling \u2014 6 Core Activities\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Column Profiling \u2013 types, lengths, nulls, uniqueness, frequency per field.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Statistical Analysis \u2013 min, max, mean, mode, median, std deviation.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Cross-Column Profiling \u2013 dependencies within a table; testing primary key candidates.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Cross-Table Profiling \u2013 relationships between tables via foreign keys; finds orphaned records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Data Rule Validation \u2013 checks against business rules/formats/regulations.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pattern Discovery \u2013 finds recurring formats (phone numbers, dates, postal codes) to catch format errors.\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: Single column \u2192 Column Profiling/Statistical Analysis. Same table, multiple columns \u2192 Cross-Column. Multiple tables \u2192 Cross-Table. Format-based checks \u2192 Pattern Discovery. Rule/regulation-based checks \u2192 Data Rule Validation.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"7. Data Quality Dimensions\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Accuracy \u2013 values reflect real-world truth (e.g., Age = -5 is inaccurate).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Completeness \u2013 no missing/NULL values.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Consistency \u2013 same fact represented the same way everywhere (e.g., \\\"Sri Lanka\\\" vs \\\"LK\\\").\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Uniqueness \u2013 no unintended duplicate records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Timeliness \u2013 data is current enough for use.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Validity \u2013 data conforms to defined formats/rules.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"8. Quick Decision Framework (for situational questions)\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"No duplication + live access needed \u2192 Federation\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Immediate/continuous sync of changes \u2192 Propagation (EAI/EDR)\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Central historical repository for BI \u2192 Consolidation\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Large volume + frequent updates \u2192 Incremental extraction\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Source initiates transfer \u2192 Push; Target initiates transfer \u2192 Pull\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Direct live query \u2192 Online; Staged "2026-09-05T03:41:36.782798Z", "attachments": [{"file_name": "", "file_size": 12685, "file_type": "txt", "extracted_content": "Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology\r\nB.Sc. Honours in Information Technology - Specialization in Data Science\r\nIT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence\r\nLecture 06\r\nMr. Nadana Swasthi\r\nContent\r\n1. Data transformation and cleansing\r\n2. Loading data into the data warehouse\r\n3. Incremental loading vs. full loading\r\n4. Change Data Capture (CDC) techniques\r\n5. ETL tools and technologies\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 2\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\nChange data capture (CDC) is a technique for detecting and capturing changes\r\nmade to data in a database and transmitting those changes to downstream\r\nsystems.\r\nCDC enables near real-time or real-time data synchronization, replication and\r\nevent-driven processing across systems after database changes occur.\r\nCDC minimizes the resources required for ETL processes because it only deals with\r\ndata changes.\r\nCDC\u2019s ability to keep downstream processes and systems updated in near real-time\r\nor real-time with low latency is instrumental to the success of real-time\r\ndata analytics, cloud migrations and artificial intelligence (AI) models.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 3\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 4\r\nIt supports a variety of use cases across industries, including fraud\r\ndetection, supply chain management and regulatory compliance in sectors such as\r\nretail, finance and healthcare.\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\n1. CDC captures only the changes made to source data after the initial load.\r\n2. It identifies INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations and isolates them\r\nfor efficient processing.\r\n3. Captured changes are tagged with operation codes (I, U, D) and optional reason\r\ncodes to identify the type and cause of the change to support accurate data\r\nloading and auditing.\r\n4. CDC improves ETL performance by avoiding full data reloads and helps\r\nmaintain historical tracking and compliance.\r\n5. Initial data load does not require CDC; CDC is used for subsequent incremental\r\nchanges.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 5\r\nIncremental Loading vs CDC\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 6\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n1. Full-Diff Compare\r\nCompares previous data snapshot with the current snapshot.\r\nDetects changes by comparing records and fields.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Simple and accurate.\r\n\u2022 Does not require changes to source systems.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Resource-intensive for large datasets.\r\n\u2022 Requires comparing entire datasets.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 7\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n2. Timed Extracts (Timestamp-Based CDC)\r\nIdentifies changes using created date or modified date/time columns.\r\nExtracts records that have changed since the last successful load.\r\nExample:\r\nSELECT * FROM Customer WHERE Modified_Date >= Last_Extract_Date\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Simple and easy to implement.\r\n\u2022 Works well for batch ETL processes.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Cannot reliably detect deleted records.\r\n\u2022 Failed jobs may create duplicate records.\r\n\u2022 Requires proper handling of timestamps and recovery logic.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 8\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n3. Delta File (CDC Approach)\r\n\u2022 Contains records of data changes made by source applications.\r\n\u2022 Generated by the source system during business operations.\r\n\u2022 ETL processes only the changed records, making CDC efficient.\r\n\u2022 Depends on the source system's ability to generate change files.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 9\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n4. Trigger-Based CDC\r\nDatabase triggers capture changes automatically.\r\nTriggers run when:\r\nINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations occur.\r\nChanges are stored in a separate change table.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Captures changes immediately.\r\n\u2022 Easy to understand and implement.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Adds extra workload to the source database.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 10\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n5. Database Log Scraping\r\nReads database transaction logs to identify changes.\r\nCaptures INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations.\r\nDoes not require modifying application code.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Efficient and scalable.\r\n\u2022 Minimal impact on source systems.\r\n\u2022 Supports near real-time data pipelines.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Depends on database log availability.\r\n\u2022 Requires database-specific implementation.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 11\r\nActivity\r\nMatch the situation with the best CDC approach:\r\n1. A database keeps a transaction log containing all changes.\r\n2. A source system provides a daily file containing changed records.\r\n3. A table contains a last_updated timestamp column.\r\n4. The ETL system compares yesterday's data with today's data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 12\r\nChange Data Capture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 13\r\nETL Process\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 14\r\nData Profiling and Data Quality Assessment\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 15\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 16\r\nData Quality Dimensions\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 17\r\nTransformation\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 18\r\nTransformation\r\nTransform data stored in different data structures to a uniform data structure.\r\nApply data cleansing approaches to deal with data issues.\r\nApply business logic to generate expected data set that needs to be stored in data\r\nwarehouse.\r\nAdd value to data by enhancing raw data.\r\nCan be architected to generate metadata that can be used to diagnose what\u2019s wrong\r\nwith source systems.\r\nThus, provide suggestions to source systems to correct erroneous data within\r\nthe source.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 19\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 20\r\nTransformation Techniques\r\nMultistage Data Transformation\r\n(ETL)\r\nExtracted data is moved to a staging\r\narea where transformations occur prior\r\nto loading the data into the warehouse\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 21\r\nIn-warehouse Data Transformation\r\n(ELT)\r\nData is extracted and loaded into the\r\nanalytics warehouse, and\r\ntransformations are done there\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n1. Application of Business Logic\r\nApplies rules and calculations to create meaningful data.\r\nGenerates new attributes (derived columns).\r\nExamples:\r\nCalculate sale_amount = quantity \u00d7 unit_price\r\nCalculate customer lifetime value (CLV)\r\nJoin data from multiple sources\r\nSplit combined fields into separate attributes\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 22\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n2. Data Cleansing\r\nImproves data quality by identifying and correcting issues.\r\nCommon activities:\r\nRemove duplicate records (deduplication)\r\nHandle missing/NULL values\r\nStandardize units of measurement\r\nFormat text values (case conversion, removing extra spaces)\r\nCorrect data type issues (e.g., text numbers \u2192 numeric values)\r\nPerform spelling corrections\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 23\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n3. Data Filtering\r\nSelect required attributes/columns from source data.\r\nFilter records based on business rules and data quality requirements.\r\nIdentify unwanted or invalid data for further handling.\r\nExamples:\r\nSelecting only customer details required for analysis.\r\nSeparating incomplete records for data quality review.\r\nRemoving duplicate records while preserving the original data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 24\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n4. Data Enrichment\r\nAdds additional information to improve the value of raw data.\r\nCreates new attributes or derived values.\r\nExamples:\r\nSplitting full name into first, middle, and last name.\r\nAdding customer demographic information.\r\nCalculating customer lifetime value (CLV).\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 25\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n5. Data Validation\r\nEnsures data meets quality and business rules before loading.\r\nDetects incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data.\r\nExamples:\r\nReject records with missing mandatory fields.\r\nValidate data types and allowed values.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 26\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n6. Generating Surrogate Keys\r\nCreates unique identifiers for warehouse\r\ntables.\r\nCommonly used in dimensional\r\nmodelling.\r\nExample:\r\nCustomer_ID = 10001 (warehouse\r\nkey)\r\n7. Lookups\r\nRetrieves additional information from\r\nreference tables.\r\nUsed to replace codes with meaningful\r\nvalues.\r\nExample:\r\nCountry_Code \u2192 Country_Name\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 27\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n8. Transposing / Pivoting\r\nChanges the structure of data for better\r\nanalysis.\r\nConverts rows into columns or columns\r\ninto rows.\r\n9. Aggregation\r\nSummarizes detailed data into higherlevel information.\r\nCombines data from multiple sources.\r\nExamples:\r\nTotal sales by store.\r\nMonthly revenue by region.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 28\r\nData Quality \u2013 Handling Missing Data\r\nWhy Missing Data Matters\r\nMissing values can reduce data quality and affect analysis.\r\nSimply removing records may result in losing valuable information.\r\nMissingness itself can provide useful information.\r\nApproaches to Handle Missing Data\r\n1. Data Imputation\r\nGenerate missing values using business rules or statistical methods.\r\n2. Flag Missing Values\r\nMark missing values so models and processes know the data was unavailable.\r\n3. Use \"Missing/Unknown\" Category\r\nFor categorical data, treat missing values as a separate category.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 29\r\nData Quality Systems\r\nDedicated data quality tools are used to profile, cleanse, and monitor data\r\nquality.\r\nProvide a framework for data cleansing, data quality monitoring, capturing and\r\nmanaging quality issues\r\nPerform data profiling to understand data problems and identify areas for\r\nimprovement.\r\nDetect and report data errors that may occur during ETL processes.\r\nCan be integrated with ETL pipelines to automate data quality checks and\r\ncleansing activities.\r\nExamples\r\nInformatica Data Quality, Talend Data Quality, Great Expectations\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 30\r\nData Quality Validation\r\nValidation Checks\r\n1. Column-Level Checks\r\nData type validation\r\nMissing value checks\r\nRange checks\r\n2. Structure-Level Checks\r\nRelationships between tables\r\nPrimary/foreign key validation\r\n3. Business Rule Checks\r\nVerify data against business\r\nrequirements.\r\nHandling Errors\r\nStop processing.\r\nSend incorrect records to an error\r\ntable.\r\nTag records with error codes for\r\ncorrection.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 31\r\nEnsures data meets quality requirements before load data into the data warehouse.\r\nActs as a testing stage in ETL pipelines.\r\nData Quality Validation\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 32\r\nData Loading\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 33\r\nData Loading Considerations\r\n1. Loading Order\r\nLoad dimension tables before\r\nfact tables then aggregate\r\ntables.\r\nFact tables require dimension keys\r\nfor references.\r\n2. Surrogate Key Generation\r\nCreates unique warehouse keys for\r\ndimension records.\r\nSeparates warehouse keys from\r\nsource system keys.\r\nHelps manage historical changes.\r\n3. Handling Slowly Changing\r\nDimensions (SCD)\r\nMaintains historical changes in\r\ndimension data.\r\nCommon approaches:\r\nType 1: Overwrite old values.\r\nType 2: Add a new record and\r\npreserve history.\r\nType 3: Store current and\r\nprevious values.\r\nType 4: update main dimension\r\nmini-dimension appropriately\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 34\r\nFull Load\r\nA Full Load is a method where all the data from the source is loaded into the\r\ndestination, regardless of whether it has been loaded before.\r\nIt essentially wipes the existing data in the target system and replaces it with a\r\ncomplete, fresh copy from the source.\r\nHow it works:\r\nDeletes or truncates the existing table in the destination.\r\nExtracts all records from the source.\r\nLoads all records into the destination table.\r\nExample Use Cases:\r\nInitial data load.\r\nWhen data volume is manageable.\r\nWhen source data changes frequently and it\u2019s hard to detect what changed.\r\nWhen historical consistency is not critical or required.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 35\r\nIncremental Load\r\nAn Incremental Load only transfers new or changed data (based on timestamps,\r\nIDs, or change tracking) from the source to the destination.\r\nIt avoids reloading all data, thus saving time and resources. Incremental Load is\r\nalso called as Delta Load.\r\nHow it works:\r\nTracks changes since the last load (e.g., using a last_updated timestamp\r\ncolumn).\r\nLoads only new or modified records.\r\nCan use methods like change data capture (CDC), timestamps, or log files.\r\nExample Use Cases:\r\nFrequent updates with large datasets.\r\nReal-time or near-real-time data processing.\r\nWhen minimizing data transfer and processing time is essential.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 36\r\nETL Tools and Technologies\r\nETL tools automate the process of extracting, transforming, and loading data\r\nfrom multiple sources into data warehouses or data platforms.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 37\r\n1. Informatica PowerCenter\r\nEnterprise-level ETL tool.\r\nSupports data integration,\r\ntransformation, and workflow\r\nmanagement. Commonly used in large\r\norganizations.\r\n2. Talend\r\nOpen-source and commercial ETL\r\nplatform. Provides data integration and\r\ndata quality features.\r\n3. Microsoft SQL Server Integration\r\nServices (SSIS)\r\nETL tool for Microsoft SQL Server\r\nenvironments.\r\nUsed for data migration, transformation,\r\nand warehouse loading.\r\nNext Lecture\r\n1. SQL querying for data analysis\r\n2. Aggregation and grouping functions\r\n3. Joins and subqueries\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 38\r\nThank you\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 39"}], "files": [{"file_uuid": "6df273d4-dfec-495d-822d-60cb790a20e6", "file_name": ""}], "parent_message_uuid": "01a06fa8-1e1c-7c79-b91d-621ea15d13b8"}, {"uuid": "01a06fa8-4866-723b-9a21-032c45498e04", "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nThis all renders cleanly.
