{\n  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, Table, TableRow, TableCell,\n  WidthType, ShadingType, BorderStyle, AlignmentType, LevelFormat\n} = require(\"docx\");\nconst fs = require(\"fs\");\n\nconst PAGE_WIDTH_DXA = 12240;\nconst PAGE_HEIGHT_DXA = 15840;\nconst MARGIN = 1080;\nconst USABLE_WIDTH = PAGE_WIDTH_DXA - MARGIN * 2;\n\nfunction h1(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 150 } });\n}\nfunction h2(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA (Lecture 06) ----------\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A financial services firm wants near real-time fraud detection by syncing every database change to an analytics engine with minimal load on the source database. Which statements justify using CDC here?\",\n    options: [\n      \"CDC captures only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE changes instead of full reloads\",\n      \"CDC enables near real-time or real-time synchronization with downstream systems\",\n      \"CDC requires reloading the entire dataset on every change to work correctly\",\n      \"CDC minimizes ETL resource usage since only changes are processed\",\n      \"CDC eliminates the need for an initial full data load entirely\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A team must detect changes without modifying the source system at all, and can only compare a saved copy of yesterday's data with today's extract. Which statements correctly describe this approach?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the Full-Diff Compare approach\",\n      \"It is simple and accurate since it directly compares records and fields\",\n      \"It requires triggers to be installed on the source database\",\n      \"It becomes resource-intensive as dataset size grows\",\n      \"It relies on reading the database transaction log\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An ETL job runs nightly using: SELECT * FROM Customer WHERE Modified_Date >= Last_Extract_Date. Which statements correctly describe the risks and nature of this approach?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Timestamp-Based CDC (Timed Extracts)\",\n      \"It cannot reliably detect deleted records\",\n      \"A failed job may cause duplicate records to be reprocessed\",\n      \"It captures changes immediately at the moment they occur\",\n      \"It requires no handling of timestamps or recovery logic\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A source application generates a file each day listing only the records that changed, which the ETL process then consumes. Which statements are accurate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the Delta File CDC approach\",\n      \"ETL only needs to process the changed records, improving efficiency\",\n      \"This approach depends on the source system's ability to generate change files\",\n      \"This approach requires scanning the full database transaction log\",\n      \"This approach is identical to Full-Diff Compare since both use files\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company installs database triggers that fire on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and write changes into a separate change table. Which statements correctly evaluate this design?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Trigger-Based CDC\",\n      \"Changes are captured immediately as they happen\",\n      \"It adds extra processing workload to the source database\",\n      \"It has zero impact on the performance of the source system\",\n      \"It requires reading the database's transaction log files\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A team wants to capture all changes with minimal impact on the live source database and without altering application code, using the database's own transaction records. Which statements are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Database Log Scraping\",\n      \"It supports near real-time data pipelines efficiently\",\n      \"It requires the database transaction log to be available and accessible\",\n      \"It requires adding new triggers to every source table\",\n      \"It always requires modifying the source application's code\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Match reasoning: 'A database keeps a transaction log containing all changes' and 'A source system provides a daily file containing changed records.' Which CDC approach pairing is correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Transaction log scenario best fits Database Log Scraping\",\n      \"Daily change file scenario best fits the Delta File approach\",\n      \"Both scenarios must use Trigger-Based CDC only\",\n      \"Transaction log scenario could reasonably use Log Scraping instead of Full-Diff Compare\",\n      \"Daily file scenario requires comparing full snapshots each time\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Match reasoning: 'A table contains a last_updated timestamp column' and 'The ETL system compares yesterday's data with today's data.' Which pairing is correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Timestamp column scenario best fits Timestamp-Based CDC (Timed Extracts)\",\n      \"Comparing yesterday vs today's data best fits Full-Diff Compare\",\n      \"Both scenarios necessarily require database triggers\",\n      \"The timestamp scenario could miss detecting deleted records\",\n      \"The compare-snapshots scenario is the most resource-efficient of all CDC methods\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements are generally true about Change Data Capture (CDC) as a concept?\",\n    options: [\n      \"CDC captures only changes made after the initial load, not the initial load itself\",\n      \"Changes can be tagged with operation codes (I, U, D) for auditing and accurate loading\",\n      \"CDC always requires a full reload of the source dataset to function\",\n      \"CDC helps maintain historical tracking and supports compliance needs\",\n      \"CDC is irrelevant to real-time analytics and AI model use cases\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company is deciding between Multistage (ETL) and In-Warehouse (ELT) transformation architectures. Which statements are accurate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"In ETL, transformations occur in a staging area before loading into the warehouse\",\n      \"In ELT, data is loaded into the warehouse first and transformed there\",\n      \"ETL and ELT are identical approaches with no architectural difference\",\n      \"The choice affects where processing load and staging infrastructure sit\",\n      \"ELT never requires any transformation logic since raw data is always analysis-ready\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst creates a new column sale_amount = quantity \u00d7 unit_price and calculates customer lifetime value (CLV) from historical purchase data. Which transformation technique(s) does this represent?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Application of Business Logic\",\n      \"Generating derived/new attributes from existing data\",\n      \"Data Filtering, since only certain rows are being selected\",\n      \"Data Enrichment, since CLV adds value to the raw customer record\",\n      \"Surrogate Key Generation, since a new column is created\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"During ETL, duplicate customer records are removed, missing values are handled, and inconsistent text casing is standardized. Which statement(s) correctly describe this stage?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Cleansing\",\n      \"Deduplication is a common data cleansing activity\",\n      \"Standardizing units and formatting text values are cleansing activities\",\n      \"This is the same activity as Data Validation, since both check quality\",\n      \"This stage always requires generating surrogate keys\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An ETL process selects only the customer attributes needed for analysis and separates out incomplete records for later review. Which statement(s) are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents Data Filtering\",\n      \"It can be used to identify unwanted or invalid data for further handling\",\n      \"It always deletes the excluded records permanently with no further use\",\n      \"It may select required attributes/columns based on business rules\",\n      \"This is identical to Data Enrichment since both handle raw data\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A transformation step splits a customer's full name into first, middle, and last name, and appends demographic data to each customer record. Which statement(s) apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Enrichment\",\n      \"It adds additional information to improve the value of raw data\",\n      \"It creates new attributes or derived values from existing data\",\n      \"This is the same as Data Validation since both modify records\",\n      \"This step must occur before any data extraction happens\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Before loading, the ETL pipeline rejects records with missing mandatory fields and checks that data types and allowed values are correct. Which statement(s) are true?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents Data Validation\",\n      \"It ensures data meets quality/business rules before loading\",\n      \"It detects incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data\",\n      \"This step generates surrogate keys for dimension tables\",\n      \"This step is only relevant for ELT, never for ETL\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A warehouse creates unique internal keys (Customer_ID = 10001) separate from source system IDs, and separately replaces Country_Code values with full Country_Name values from a reference table. Which statement(s) correctly distinguish these two activities?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Creating unique internal keys is Surrogate Key Generation\",\n      \"Replacing codes with descriptive values using a reference table is a Lookup\",\n      \"Both activities are examples of the same single technique with no distinction\",\n      \"Surrogate keys are commonly used in dimensional modelling\",\n      \"Lookups eliminate the need for any dimension tables in the warehouse\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A report requires converting monthly sales rows into columns (one column per month) for easier comparison, and separately requires computing total sales by store. Which statement(s) correctly identify these techniques?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Converting rows into columns is Transposing/Pivoting\",\n      \"Computing total sales by store is Aggregation\",\n      \"Both techniques are identical since both summarize the data\",\n      \"Aggregation summarizes detailed data into higher-level information\",\n      \"Pivoting is required before any aggregation can ever occur\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A dataset has several NULL values in the 'Income' column. The team decides not to simply delete these records. Which approaches are valid ways to handle this missing data?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Impute missing values using business rules or statistical methods\",\n      \"Flag missing values so downstream models know data was unavailable\",\n      \"Treat missing values as a separate 'Missing/Unknown' category for categorical fields\",\n      \"Always delete any record containing a missing value regardless of importance\",\n      \"Ignore the issue since missingness never carries useful information\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Before loading data into the warehouse, the team validates data types, checks primary/foreign key relationships, and verifies compliance with business requirements. Which validation categories are represented?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Column-Level Checks (data type, missing values, range checks)\",\n      \"Structure-Level Checks (table relationships, key validation)\",\n      \"Business Rule Checks (verifying against business requirements)\",\n      \"This is entirely a Data Enrichment activity, not validation\",\n      \"Failed records can be routed to an error table or tagged with error codes\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An organization adopts tools like Informatica Data Quality or Great Expectations, integrated with its ETL pipelines. Summarized totals \u2192 Aggregation.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"5. 2;\n\nfunction h1(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 150 } });\n}\nfunction h2(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA (Lecture 06) ----------\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A financial services firm wants near real-time fraud detection by syncing every database change to an Which statements correctly describe this approach?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the Full-Diff Compare approach\",\n      \"It is simple and accurate since it directly compares records and fields\",\n      \"It requires triggers to be installed on the source database\",\n      \"It becomes resource-intensive as dataset size grows\",\n      \"It relies on reading the database transaction log\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An ETL job runs nightly using: SELECT * FROM Customer WHERE Modified_Date >= Last_Extract_Date. Which statements correctly describe the risks and nature of this approach?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Timestamp-Based CDC (Timed Extracts)\",\n      \"It cannot reliably detect deleted records\",\n      \"A failed job may cause duplicate records to be reprocessed\",\n      \"It captures changes immediately at the moment they occur\",\n      \"It requires no handling of timestamps or recovery logic\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A source application generates a file each day listing only the records that changed, which the ETL process then consumes. Which statements are accurate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the Delta File CDC approach\",\n      \"ETL only needs to process the changed records, improving efficiency\",\n      \"This approach depends on the source system's ability to generate change files\",\n      \"This approach requires scanning the full database transaction log\",\n      \"This approach is identical to Full-Diff Compare since both use files\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company installs database triggers that fire on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and write changes into a separate change table. Which statements correctly evaluate this design?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Trigger-Based CDC\",\n      \"Changes are captured immediately as they happen\",\n      \"It adds extra processing workload to the source database\",\n      \"It has zero impact on the performance of the source system\",\n      \"It requires reading the database's transaction log files\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A team wants to capture all changes with minimal impact on the live source database and without altering application code, using the database's own transaction records. Which statements are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Database Log Scraping\",\n      \"It supports near real-time data pipelines efficiently\",\n      \"It requires the database transaction log to be available and accessible\",\n      \"It requires adding new triggers to every source table\",\n      \"It always requires modifying the source application's code\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Match reasoning: 'A database keeps a transaction log containing all changes' and 'A source system provides a daily file containing changed records.' Which CDC approach pairing is correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Transaction log scenario best fits Database Log Scraping\",\n      \"Daily change file scenario best fits the Delta File approach\",\n      \"Both scenarios must use Trigger-Based CDC only\",\n      \"Transaction log scenario could reasonably use Log Scraping instead of Full-Diff Compare\",\n      \"Daily file scenario requires comparing full snapshots each time\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Match reasoning: 'A table contains a last_updated timestamp column' and 'The ETL system compares yesterday's data with today's data.' Which pairing is correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Timestamp column scenario best fits Timestamp-Based CDC (Timed Extracts)\",\n      \"Comparing yesterday vs today's data best fits Full-Diff Compare\",\n      \"Both scenarios necessarily require database triggers\",\n      \"The timestamp scenario could miss detecting deleted records\",\n      \"The compare-snapshots scenario is the most resource-efficient of all CDC methods\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements are generally true about Change Data Capture (CDC) as a concept?\",\n    options: [\n      \"CDC captures only changes made after the initial load, not the initial load itself\",\n      \"Changes can be tagged with operation codes (I, U, D) for auditing and accurate loading\",\n      \"CDC always requires a full reload of the source dataset to function\",\n      \"CDC helps maintain historical tracking and supports compliance needs\",\n      \"CDC is irrelevant to real-time analytics and AI model use cases\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company is deciding between Multistage (ETL) and In-Warehouse (ELT) transformation architectures. Which statements are accurate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"In ETL, transformations occur in a staging area before loading into the warehouse\",\n      \"In ELT, data is loaded into the warehouse first and transformed there\",\n      \"ETL and ELT are identical approaches with no architectural difference\",\n      \"The choice affects where processing load and staging infrastructure sit\",\n      \"ELT never requires any transformation logic since raw data is always analysis-ready\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst creates a new column sale_amount = quantity \u00d7 unit_price and calculates customer lifetime value (CLV) from historical purchase data. Which transformation technique(s) does this represent?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Application of Business Logic\",\n      \"Generating derived/new attributes from existing data\",\n      \"Data Filtering, since only certain rows are being selected\",\n      \"Data Enrichment, since CLV adds value to the raw customer record\",\n      \"Surrogate Key Generation, since a new column is created\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"During ETL, duplicate customer records are removed, missing values are handled, and inconsistent text casing is standardized. Which statement(s) correctly describe this stage?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Cleansing\",\n      \"Deduplication is a common data cleansing activity\",\n      \"Standardizing units and formatting text values are cleansing activities\",\n      \"This is the same activity as Data Validation, since both check quality\",\n      \"This stage always requires generating surrogate keys\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An ETL process selects only the customer attributes needed for analysis and separates out incomplete records for later review. Which statement(s) are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents Data Filtering\",\n      \"It can be used to identify unwanted or invalid data for further handling\",\n      \"It always deletes the excluded records permanently with no further use\",\n      \"It may select required attributes/columns based on business rules\",\n      \"This is identical to Data Enrichment since both handle raw data\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A transformation step splits a customer's full name into first, middle, and last name, and appends demographic data to each customer record. Which statement(s) apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Data Enrichment\",\n      \"It adds additional information to improve the value of raw data\",\n      \"It creates new attributes or derived values from existing data\",\n      \"This is the same as Data Validation since both modify records\",\n      \"This step must occur before any data extraction happens\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Before loading, the ETL pipeline rejects records with missing mandatory fields and checks that data types and allowed values are correct. Which statement(s) are true?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents Data Validation\",\n      \"It ensures data meets quality/business rules before loading\",\n      \"It detects incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data\",\n      \"This step generates surrogate keys for dimension tables\",\n      \"This step is only relevant for ELT, never for ETL\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A warehouse creates unique internal keys (Customer_ID = 10001) separate from source system IDs, and separately replaces Country_Code values with full Country_Name values from a reference table. Which statement(s) correctly distinguish these two activities?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Creating unique internal keys is Surrogate Key Generation\",\n      \"Replacing codes with descriptive values using a reference table is a Lookup\",\n      \"Both activities are examples of the same single technique with no distinction\",\n      \"Surrogate keys are commonly used in dimensional modelling\",\n      \"Lookups eliminate the need for any dimension tables in the warehouse\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A report requires converting monthly sales rows into columns (one column per month) for easier comparison, and separately requires computing total sales by store. Which statement(s) correctly identify these techniques?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Converting rows into columns is Transposing/Pivoting\",\n      \"Computing total sales by store is Aggregation\",\n      \"Both techniques are identical since both summarize the data\",\n      \"Aggregation summarizes detailed data into higher-level information\",\n      \"Pivoting is required before any aggregation can ever occur\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A dataset has several NULL values in the 'Income' column. Summarized totals \u2192 Aggregation.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"5. Handling Missing Data\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Missing data can reduce quality, but deleting records may lose valuable information \u2014 missingness itself can be informative.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Data Imputation \u2014 fill in values using business rules or statistics.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Flagging \u2014 mark values as missing so downstream processes are aware.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"'Missing/Unknown' Category \u2014 treat missing as its own category for categorical data.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"6. "stop_timestamp": "2026-09-05T03:46:50.220731Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-09-05T03:46:50.220876Z", "updated_at": "2026-09-05T03:46:50.220876Z", "attachments": [{"file_name": "", "file_size": 12685, "file_type": "txt", "extracted_content": "Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology\r\nB.Sc. Honours in Information Technology - Specialization in Data Science\r\nIT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence\r\nLecture 06\r\nMr. Nadana Swasthi\r\nContent\r\n1. Data transformation and cleansing\r\n2. Loading data into the data warehouse\r\n3. Incremental loading vs. full loading\r\n4. Change Data Capture (CDC) techniques\r\n5. ETL tools and technologies\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 2\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\nChange data capture (CDC) is a technique for detecting and capturing changes\r\nmade to data in a database and transmitting those changes to downstream\r\nsystems.\r\nCDC enables near real-time or real-time data synchronization, replication and\r\nevent-driven processing across systems after database changes occur.\r\nCDC minimizes the resources required for ETL processes because it only deals with\r\ndata changes.\r\nCDC\u2019s ability to keep downstream processes and systems updated in near real-time\r\nor real-time with low latency is instrumental to the success of real-time\r\ndata analytics, cloud migrations and artificial intelligence (AI) models.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 3\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 4\r\nIt supports a variety of use cases across industries, including fraud\r\ndetection, supply chain management and regulatory compliance in sectors such as\r\nretail, finance and healthcare.\r\nChange Data Capture (CDC)\r\n1. CDC captures only the changes made to source data after the initial load.\r\n2. It identifies INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations and isolates them\r\nfor efficient processing.\r\n3. Captured changes are tagged with operation codes (I, U, D) and optional reason\r\ncodes to identify the type and cause of the change to support accurate data\r\nloading and auditing.\r\n4. CDC improves ETL performance by avoiding full data reloads and helps\r\nmaintain historical tracking and compliance.\r\n5. Initial data load does not require CDC; CDC is used for subsequent incremental\r\nchanges.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 5\r\nIncremental Loading vs CDC\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 6\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n1. Full-Diff Compare\r\nCompares previous data snapshot with the current snapshot.\r\nDetects changes by comparing records and fields.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Simple and accurate.\r\n\u2022 Does not require changes to source systems.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Resource-intensive for large datasets.\r\n\u2022 Requires comparing entire datasets.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 7\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n2. Timed Extracts (Timestamp-Based CDC)\r\nIdentifies changes using created date or modified date/time columns.\r\nExtracts records that have changed since the last successful load.\r\nExample:\r\nSELECT * FROM Customer WHERE Modified_Date >= Last_Extract_Date\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Simple and easy to implement.\r\n\u2022 Works well for batch ETL processes.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Cannot reliably detect deleted records.\r\n\u2022 Failed jobs may create duplicate records.\r\n\u2022 Requires proper handling of timestamps and recovery logic.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 8\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n3. Delta File (CDC Approach)\r\n\u2022 Contains records of data changes made by source applications.\r\n\u2022 Generated by the source system during business operations.\r\n\u2022 ETL processes only the changed records, making CDC efficient.\r\n\u2022 Depends on the source system's ability to generate change files.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 9\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n4. Trigger-Based CDC\r\nDatabase triggers capture changes automatically.\r\nTriggers run when:\r\nINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations occur.\r\nChanges are stored in a separate change table.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Captures changes immediately.\r\n\u2022 Easy to understand and implement.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Adds extra workload to the source database.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 10\r\nChange Data Capture: Approaches\r\n5. Database Log Scraping\r\nReads database transaction logs to identify changes.\r\nCaptures INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations.\r\nDoes not require modifying application code.\r\nAdvantages\r\n\u2022 Efficient and scalable.\r\n\u2022 Minimal impact on source systems.\r\n\u2022 Supports near real-time data pipelines.\r\nLimitations\r\n\u2022 Depends on database log availability.\r\n\u2022 Requires database-specific implementation.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 11\r\nActivity\r\nMatch the situation with the best CDC approach:\r\n1. A database keeps a transaction log containing all changes.\r\n2. A source system provides a daily file containing changed records.\r\n3. A table contains a last_updated timestamp column.\r\n4. The ETL system compares yesterday's data with today's data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 12\r\nChange Data Capture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 13\r\nETL Process\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 14\r\nData Profiling and Data Quality Assessment\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 15\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 16\r\nData Quality Dimensions\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 17\r\nTransformation\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 18\r\nTransformation\r\nTransform data stored in different data structures to a uniform data structure.\r\nApply data cleansing approaches to deal with data issues.\r\nApply business logic to generate expected data set that needs to be stored in data\r\nwarehouse.\r\nAdd value to data by enhancing raw data.\r\nCan be architected to generate metadata that can be used to diagnose what\u2019s wrong\r\nwith source systems.\r\nThus, provide suggestions to source systems to correct erroneous data within\r\nthe source.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 19\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 20\r\nTransformation Techniques\r\nMultistage Data Transformation\r\n(ETL)\r\nExtracted data is moved to a staging\r\narea where transformations occur prior\r\nto loading the data into the warehouse\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 21\r\nIn-warehouse Data Transformation\r\n(ELT)\r\nData is extracted and loaded into the\r\nanalytics warehouse, and\r\ntransformations are done there\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n1. Application of Business Logic\r\nApplies rules and calculations to create meaningful data.\r\nGenerates new attributes (derived columns).\r\nExamples:\r\nCalculate sale_amount = quantity \u00d7 unit_price\r\nCalculate customer lifetime value (CLV)\r\nJoin data from multiple sources\r\nSplit combined fields into separate attributes\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 22\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n2. Data Cleansing\r\nImproves data quality by identifying and correcting issues.\r\nCommon activities:\r\nRemove duplicate records (deduplication)\r\nHandle missing/NULL values\r\nStandardize units of measurement\r\nFormat text values (case conversion, removing extra spaces)\r\nCorrect data type issues (e.g., text numbers \u2192 numeric values)\r\nPerform spelling corrections\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 23\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n3. Data Filtering\r\nSelect required attributes/columns from source data.\r\nFilter records based on business rules and data quality requirements.\r\nIdentify unwanted or invalid data for further handling.\r\nExamples:\r\nSelecting only customer details required for analysis.\r\nSeparating incomplete records for data quality review.\r\nRemoving duplicate records while preserving the original data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 24\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n4. Data Enrichment\r\nAdds additional information to improve the value of raw data.\r\nCreates new attributes or derived values.\r\nExamples:\r\nSplitting full name into first, middle, and last name.\r\nAdding customer demographic information.\r\nCalculating customer lifetime value (CLV).\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 25\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n5. Data Validation\r\nEnsures data meets quality and business rules before loading.\r\nDetects incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data.\r\nExamples:\r\nReject records with missing mandatory fields.\r\nValidate data types and allowed values.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 26\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n6. Generating Surrogate Keys\r\nCreates unique identifiers for warehouse\r\ntables.\r\nCommonly used in dimensional\r\nmodelling.\r\nExample:\r\nCustomer_ID = 10001 (warehouse\r\nkey)\r\n7. Lookups\r\nRetrieves additional information from\r\nreference tables.\r\nUsed to replace codes with meaningful\r\nvalues.\r\nExample:\r\nCountry_Code \u2192 Country_Name\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 27\r\nData Transformations in ETL\r\n8. Transposing / Pivoting\r\nChanges the structure of data for better\r\nanalysis.\r\nConverts rows into columns or columns\r\ninto rows.\r\n9. Aggregation\r\nSummarizes detailed data into higherlevel information.\r\nCombines data from multiple sources.\r\nExamples:\r\nTotal sales by store.\r\nMonthly revenue by region.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 28\r\nData Quality \u2013 Handling Missing Data\r\nWhy Missing Data Matters\r\nMissing values can reduce data quality and affect analysis.\r\nSimply removing records may result in losing valuable information.\r\nMissingness itself can provide useful information.\r\nApproaches to Handle Missing Data\r\n1. Data Imputation\r\nGenerate missing values using business rules or statistical methods.\r\n2. Flag Missing Values\r\nMark missing values so models and processes know the data was unavailable.\r\n3. Use \"Missing/Unknown\" Category\r\nFor categorical data, treat missing values as a separate category.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 29\r\nData Quality Systems\r\nDedicated data quality tools are used to profile, cleanse, and monitor data\r\nquality.\r\nProvide a framework for data cleansing, data quality monitoring, capturing and\r\nmanaging quality issues\r\nPerform data profiling to understand data problems and identify areas for\r\nimprovement.\r\nDetect and report data errors that may occur during ETL processes.\r\nCan be integrated with ETL pipelines to automate data quality checks and\r\ncleansing activities.\r\nExamples\r\nInformatica Data Quality, Talend Data Quality, Great Expectations\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 30\r\nData Quality Validation\r\nValidation Checks\r\n1. Column-Level Checks\r\nData type validation\r\nMissing value checks\r\nRange checks\r\n2. Structure-Level Checks\r\nRelationships between tables\r\nPrimary/foreign key validation\r\n3. Business Rule Checks\r\nVerify data against business\r\nrequirements.\r\nHandling Errors\r\nStop processing.\r\nSend incorrect records to an error\r\ntable.\r\nTag records with error codes for\r\ncorrection.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 31\r\nEnsures data meets quality requirements before load data into the data warehouse.\r\nActs as a testing stage in ETL pipelines.\r\nData Quality Validation\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 32\r\nData Loading\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 33\r\nData Loading Considerations\r\n1. Loading Order\r\nLoad dimension tables before\r\nfact tables then aggregate\r\ntables.\r\nFact tables require dimension keys\r\nfor references.\r\n2. Surrogate Key Generation\r\nCreates unique warehouse keys for\r\ndimension records.\r\nSeparates warehouse keys from\r\nsource system keys.\r\nHelps manage historical changes.\r\n3. Handling Slowly Changing\r\nDimensions (SCD)\r\nMaintains historical changes in\r\ndimension data.\r\nCommon approaches:\r\nType 1: Overwrite old values.\r\nType 2: Add a new record and\r\npreserve history.\r\nType 3: Store current and\r\nprevious values.\r\nType 4: update main dimension\r\nmini-dimension appropriately\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 34\r\nFull Load\r\nA Full Load is a method where all the data from the source is loaded into the\r\ndestination, regardless of whether it has been loaded before.\r\nIt essentially wipes the existing data in the target system and replaces it with a\r\ncomplete, fresh copy from the source.\r\nHow it works:\r\nDeletes or truncates the existing table in the destination.\r\nExtracts all records from the source.\r\nLoads all records into the destination table.\r\nExample Use Cases:\r\nInitial data load.\r\nWhen data volume is manageable.\r\nWhen source data changes frequently and it\u2019s hard to detect what changed.\r\nWhen historical consistency is not critical or required.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 35\r\nIncremental Load\r\nAn Incremental Load only transfers new or changed data (based on timestamps,\r\nIDs, or change tracking) from the source to the destination.\r\nIt avoids reloading all data, thus saving time and resources. Incremental Load is\r\nalso called as Delta Load.\r\nHow it works:\r\nTracks changes since the last load (e.g., using a last_updated timestamp\r\ncolumn).\r\nLoads only new or modified records.\r\nCan use methods like change data capture (CDC), timestamps, or log files.\r\nExample Use Cases:\r\nFrequent updates with large datasets.\r\nReal-time or near-real-time data processing.\r\nWhen minimizing data transfer and processing time is essential.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 36\r\nETL Tools and Technologies\r\nETL tools automate the process of extracting, transforming, and loading data\r\nfrom multiple sources into data warehouses or data platforms.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 37\r\n1. Informatica PowerCenter\r\nEnterprise-level ETL tool.\r\nSupports data integration,\r\ntransformation, and workflow\r\nmanagement. Commonly used in large\r\norganizations.\r\n2. Talend\r\nOpen-source and commercial ETL\r\nplatform. Provides data integration and\r\ndata quality features.\r\n3. Microsoft SQL Server Integration\r\nServices (SSIS)\r\nETL tool for Microsoft SQL Server\r\nenvironments.\r\nUsed for data migration, transformation,\r\nand warehouse loading.\r\nNext Lecture\r\n1. SQL querying for data analysis\r\n2. Aggregation and grouping functions\r\n3. Joins and subqueries\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 38\r\nThank you\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 39"}], "files": [{"file_uuid": "6c06b800-dbcd-4850-b5d7-80e03adc09a9", "file_name": ""}], "parent_message_uuid": "01a06fac-f7cf-77b4-9fcf-5ea252d667e6"}, {"uuid": "01a06fad-100d-7643-a84a-ee9f8b1c10f0", "text": "This is the same content as Lecture 06 (it's labeled \"Lecture 06\" inside the document, and it's identical to what you shared last time). Honours in Information Technology - Specialization in Data Science\r\nIT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence\r\nLecture 07\r\nMr. Nadana Swasthi\r\nContent\r\n1. Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) concepts and architecture\r\n2. Multidimensional data analysis\r\n3. OLAP operations: drill-down, roll-up, slice and dice, pivoting\r\n4. OLAP cube design and implementation\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 2\r\nWhat is OLAP?\r\nOnline Analytical Processing (OLAP) is a technology used for analysing large\r\nvolumes of historical data stored in a data warehouse.\r\nOLAP enables users to:\r\n\u2022 Analyse data from different perspectives\r\n\u2022 Identify trends and patterns\r\n\u2022 Compare business performance\r\n\u2022 Generate summaries and reports\r\n\u2022 Support strategic decision-making\r\nA data warehouse stores integrated historical data, but OLAP provides the\r\nanalytical capabilities to explore that data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 3\r\nOLTP vs OLAP\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 4\r\nOLTP vs OLAP\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 5\r\nRole of OLAP in Data Warehousing\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 6\r\nOLAP is the analytical layer between the Data Warehouse and end users.\r\nRole of OLAP in Data Warehousing\r\nBottom Tier: Data Warehouse Layer\r\nStores integrated and historical data collected through ETL processes.\r\nContains fact tables and dimension tables used for analysis.\r\nExample:\r\nSales fact table with Product, Customer, and Time dimensions.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 7\r\nRole of OLAP in Data Warehousing\r\nMiddle Tier: OLAP Layer\r\nThe OLAP server transforms warehouse data into multidimensional cubes.\r\nEnables fast analytical queries and interactive data exploration.\r\nSupports operations such as:\r\nRoll-up\r\nDrill-down\r\nSlice\r\nDice\r\nPivot\r\nExample:\r\nAnalysing sales by product, region, and year using a sales cube.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 8\r\nRole of OLAP in Data Warehousing\r\nTop Tier: Analysis and Reporting Layer\r\nProvides interfaces for users to explore OLAP results.\r\nIncludes dashboards, reports, and visualization tools.\r\nExamples:\r\nPower BI\r\nTableau\r\nExcel Pivot Tables\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 9\r\nRole of OLAP in DW\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 10\r\nOLAP Cubes\r\nAn OLAP cube is a multidimensional data structure that organizes data from a\r\ndata warehouse to support fast and interactive analysis.\r\nIt allows users to analyse measures (facts) from different perspectives\r\n(dimensions).\r\nPre-calculates most of the queries that are typically time taking to execute over\r\ntabular databases such as aggregation, joining and grouping\r\nSpecially optimized for OLAP operations:\r\n\u2022 Roll-up, Drill-down, Slice, Dice, Pivot\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 11\r\nRepresenting Multi-dimensional Data\r\nTable vs Matrix\r\nA normal relational table represents data in rows and columns. However, OLAP\r\nanalysis requires viewing data from multiple dimensions.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 12\r\nRepresenting Multi-dimensional Data\r\nTable vs. Cube\r\nAn OLAP cube organizes data using dimensions and measures.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 13\r\nRepresenting Multi-dimensional Data\r\nMatrix vs Cube\r\nA matrix can represent data using 2 dimensions, but OLAP analysis often requires\r\nmore. When we add another dimension, the representation becomes a cube.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 14\r\nRepresenting Multi-dimensional Data\r\nSeries of Cubes\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 15\r\nActivity\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 16\r\nThis table represents sales data from a retail company. Your task is to identify the\r\ndimensions and measure and convert this tabular representation into an\r\nOLAP cube.\r\nDimensional Hierarchy\r\nA dimension is not always a single level. Dimensions often have multiple levels of\r\ndetail. These levels form a hierarchy.\"\r\nA hierarchy defines how we move from detailed data to summarized data.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 17\r\nOLAP Operations: Roll-up\r\nClimbing up a hierarchy of a dimension\r\nto aggregate data\r\nAlso known as consolidation or\r\naggregation\r\nExample: roll-up through country-city\r\nhierarchy in Location dimension\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 18\r\nOLAP Operations: Drill-down\r\nStepping down a hierarchy of a\r\ndimension allowing navigation through\r\ndetails\r\nData is fragmented into smaller parts\r\nIt is the opposite of the rollup process\r\nExample: drill-down through quartermoth hierarchy in Time dimension\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 19\r\nOLAP Operations: Slice\r\nA rectangular subset of a cube, by\r\nchoosing a single value for one of its\r\ndimensions\r\nExample: dimension Time is sliced\r\nwith \u201cQ1\u201d as the filter\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 20\r\nOLAP Operations: Dice\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 21\r\nSelects two or more dimensions from a\r\ngiven cube and provides a new sub-cube\r\nby selecting specific values on those\r\nselected dimensions\r\nExample: (Product = \u201cModems\u201d or\r\n\u201cWireless Mouse\u201d) and\r\n(Time = \u201c2000\u201d or \u201c2001\u201d) and\r\n(Location = \u201cEuro\u201d or \u201cAsia\u201d)\r\nOLAP Operations: Pivot\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 22\r\nPivot is a visualization operations which\r\nrotates the data axes to provide an\r\nalternative presentation of the data.\r\nRotate the cube to see its various faces.\r\nIt may contain swapping the rows and\r\ncolumns or moving one of the rowdimensions into the column dimensions.\r\nOLAP Operations: Pivot\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 23\r\nAggregations in OLAP Cubes\r\nOLAP cubes often store pre-computed aggregations at different levels of detail.\r\nThis allows analytical queries to return results quickly without repeatedly\r\nscanning millions of records.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 24\r\nActivity\r\nIdentify the operations\r\nperformed.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 25\r\nOLAP Operations\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 26\r\nOLAP Storage Types\r\n1. ROLAP (Relational OLAP)\r\nOLAP analysis is performed directly on\r\nrelational database tables.\r\nData is stored as:\r\n\u2022 Fact tables\r\n\u2022 Dimension tables\r\nExample:\r\n\u2022 Sales_Fact\r\n\u2022 Product_Dim\r\n\u2022 Time_Dim\r\n\u2022 Store_Dim\r\nThe OLAP engine uses SQL queries to\r\nperform analysis.\r\nAdvantages:\r\nHandles very large datasets\r\nUses existing relational database\r\ntechnology\r\nDisadvantage:\r\nQuery performance can be slower\r\ncompared with pre-built cubes\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 27\r\nOLAP Storage Types\r\n2. MOLAP (Multidimensional OLAP)\r\nData is stored in a multidimensional\r\ncube structure.\r\nExample:\r\nSales Cube\r\nTime\r\nProduct\r\nLocation\r\nMeasure: Sales Amount\r\nThe system pre-calculates many\r\naggregations.\r\nAdvantages:\r\nVery fast analytical queries\r\nGood for interactive analysis\r\nDisadvantages:\r\nRequires additional storage\r\nCube processing can take time\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 28\r\nOLAP Storage Types\r\n3. HOLAP (Hybrid OLAP)\r\nCombination of ROLAP and MOLAP.\r\nDetailed data:\r\nRelational Database\r\nSummary data:\r\nMultidimensional Cube\r\nExample:\r\nTransaction-level sales \u2192 ROLAP\r\nMonthly sales summaries \u2192 MOLAP\r\nROLAP, MOLAP, and HOLAP differ\r\nin how data is stored, but they all use\r\nthe same OLAP concepts: dimensions,\r\nmeasures, hierarchies, and\r\noperations.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 29\r\nOLAP Cube Design and Implementation\r\nOLAP cube design is the process of creating a multidimensional structure that\r\nallows users to analyse data from different perspectives.\r\nAn OLAP cube is designed by defining:\r\n1. Business process to analyze\r\n2. Measures (facts)\r\n3. Dimensions\r\n4. Hierarchies\r\n5. Relationships between dimensions and facts\r\nThe goal is to provide fast analytical queries for decision-making.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 30\r\nOLAP Cube\r\nDesign\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 31\r\nOLAP Cube Design\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 32\r\nOLAP Cube Implementation\r\n1. Data Warehouse Ready\r\n2. Select Fact and Dimension Tables\r\n3. Define Cube Structure\r\n(Dimensions, Measures, Hierarchies)\r\n4. Process Cube\r\n(Calculate Aggregations)\r\n5. Analyse Using BI Tools\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 33\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 34\r\nNext Lecture\r\n1. SQL querying for data analysis\r\n2. Aggregation and grouping functions\r\n3. Joins and subqueries\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 35\r\nThank you\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 36"}], "files": [{"file_uuid": "d46ef2d1-a813-4a0c-bfbc-fcf9f7a66d59", "file_name": ""}], "parent_message_uuid": "01a06fad-100d-7643-a84a-ee9f8b1c10f0"}, {"uuid": "01a06fad-7295-7ac8-8a30-890f1116e42c", "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nRenders cleanly. Which statements about the representation are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Two dimensions can typically be represented using a matrix\",\n      \"Adding a third dimension moves the representation toward a cube structure\",\n      \"A cube can only ever represent exactly two dimensions\",\n      \"Multiple related cubes can be used to represent additional dimensional combinations\",\n      \"A relational table alone is the most natural way to view three or more dimensions simultaneously\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A Location dimension contains levels such as Country \u2192 State \u2192 City, and a Time dimension contains Year \u2192 Quarter \u2192 Month. Which statements about this structure are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents a dimensional hierarchy within each dimension\",\n      \"A hierarchy defines how to move between detailed and summarized data\",\n      \"Every dimension must always have exactly one level with no hierarchy\",\n      \"Hierarchies enable operations like roll-up and drill-down along a dimension\",\n      \"Hierarchies exist only in the Time dimension and never in other dimensions\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst is viewing sales broken down by City and wants to see totals aggregated at the Country level instead. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Roll-up operation\",\n      \"It involves climbing up the Location hierarchy from City toward Country\",\n      \"This operation is also known as consolidation or aggregation\",\n      \"This is the opposite of roll-up, known as drill-down\",\n      \"This requires selecting a single dimension value to create a sub-cube\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst is viewing sales at the Quarter level and wants to see the more detailed Month-level breakdown within each quarter. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Slice operation\",\n      \"It selects a single value for one dimension (Time = Q1)\",\n      \"The result is a rectangular subset of the original cube\",\n      \"This selects specific values across two or more dimensions simultaneously\",\n      \"This operation rotates the cube to present an alternate view\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst filters the sales cube where (Product = 'Modems' or 'Wireless Mouse') AND (Time = '2000' or '2001') AND (Location = 'Euro' or 'Asia'). Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Dice operation\",\n      \"It selects specific values across two or more dimensions to form a new sub-cube\",\n      \"This differs from Slice, which restricts only a single dimension\",\n      \"This is identical to Slice since both filter the cube\",\n      \"This operation only ever applies to exactly one dimension at a time\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A report currently shows Products as rows and Regions as columns. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Pivot operation\",\n      \"It rotates the data axes to provide an alternative presentation\",\n      \"It may involve swapping rows and columns or moving a dimension between axes\",\n      \"This changes the underlying data values stored in the cube\",\n      \"This is the same as a Roll-up, since both reorganize the view\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly distinguish Roll-up from Drill-down?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Roll-up aggregates data by climbing up a hierarchy\",\n      \"Drill-down navigates into more detailed data by stepping down a hierarchy\",\n      \"Roll-up and drill-down are functionally identical operations\",\n      \"Drill-down is the opposite process of roll-up\",\n      \"Both operations require selecting exactly one value from each dimension\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly distinguish Slice from Dice?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Slice restricts the cube using a single value on one dimension\",\n      \"Dice restricts the cube using values across two or more dimensions\",\n      \"Slice and Dice both always produce a single data point, never a sub-cube\",\n      \"Dice can be viewed as an extension of slicing across multiple dimensions\",\n      \"Slice always requires selecting exactly three dimensions simultaneously\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company implements ROLAP for its analytics platform, storing data directly in fact and dimension tables and using SQL queries for analysis. What is OLAP?\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) analyses large volumes of historical data stored in a data warehouse.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Enables: analysing data from different perspectives, identifying trends, comparing performance, generating summaries/reports, supporting decision-making.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"The DW stores integrated historical data; OLAP provides the analytical capability to explore it.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"2. OLTP vs OLAP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLTP \u2014 optimized for day-to-day transaction processing (fast inserts/updates, operational systems).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLAP \u2014 optimized for analysing historical, integrated data for trends and strategic decisions.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"3. Role of OLAP in Data Warehousing \u2014 Three Tiers\"));\nconst tierRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Tier\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2000}), cell(\"Role\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:4700}), cell(\"Example\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Bottom \u2014 Data Warehouse\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Stores integrated historical data; fact and dimension tables from ETL\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Sales fact table with Product, Customer, Time dimensions\", {width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Middle \u2014 OLAP Layer\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Transforms warehouse data into multidimensional cubes; enables fast queries\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot operations\", {width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Top \u2014 Analysis/Reporting\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Interfaces for exploring OLAP results\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Power BI, Tableau, Excel Pivot Tables\", {width:3300})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [2000,4700,3300], rows: tierRows }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"4. OLAP Cubes\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"A multidimensional structure organizing data from a DW to support fast, interactive analysis.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Analyses measures (facts) from different perspectives (dimensions).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pre-calculates aggregation, joining, and grouping so queries run fast without scanning raw records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Table \u2192 Matrix \u2192 Cube: a table is 2D at best; a matrix handles 2 dimensions; a cube handles 3+ dimensions; multiple related cubes can represent even more combinations.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"5. Dimensional Hierarchy\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"A dimension often has multiple levels of detail forming a hierarchy (e.g., Country \u2192 State \u2192 City; Year \u2192 Quarter \u2192 Month).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Hierarchies define how to move between detailed and summarized data \u2014 the basis for roll-up and drill-down.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"6. OLAP Operations\"));\nconst opRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Operation\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:1800}), cell(\"What it does\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:5000}), cell(\"Direction/Note\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Roll-up\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Climbs up a hierarchy to aggregate data (e.g., City \u2192 Country)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Aka consolidation/aggregation\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Drill-down\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Steps down a hierarchy for more detail (e.g., Quarter \u2192 Month)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Opposite of roll-up\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Slice\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Selects a single value on ONE dimension\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Produces a rectangular subset of the cube\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Dice\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Selects specific values across TWO OR MORE dimensions\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Produces a smaller sub-cube\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Pivot\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Rotates data axes for an alternate view (swap rows/columns)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Visualization only \u2014 doesn't change stored values\", {width:3200})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [1800,5000,3200], rows: opRows }));\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: One dimension filtered \u2192 Slice. Two+ dimensions filtered \u2192 Dice. Aggregating upward \u2192 Roll-up. Going more detailed \u2192 Drill-down. Just changing the view's orientation \u2192 Pivot.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"7. OLAP Storage Types\"));\nconst storageRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Type\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:1600}), cell(\"Storage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3400}), cell(\"Advantage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2500}), cell(\"Disadvantage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"ROLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Relational tables (fact + dimension); SQL-based analysis\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Handles very large datasets; uses existing RDBMS tech\", {width:2500}), cell(\"Slower query performance vs. pre-built cubes\", {width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"MOLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Multidimensional cube structure; pre-calculated aggregations\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Very fast queries; great for interactive analysis\", {width:2500}), cell(\"Needs extra storage; cube processing takes time\", {width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"HOLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Hybrid \u2014 detail in relational DB, summary in cube\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Balances scalability and speed\", {width:2500}), cell(\"More complex to design/manage\", {width:2500})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [1600,3400,2500,2500], rows: storageRows }));\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Note: ROLAP, MOLAP, and HOLAP differ only in how data is stored \u2014 all three still use the same OLAP concepts (dimensions, measures, hierarchies, operations).\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"8. OLAP Cube Design\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Define: (1) business process to analyze, (2) measures/facts, (3) dimensions, (4) hierarchies, (5) relationships between dimensions and facts.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Goal: enable fast analytical queries for decision-making.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"9. OLAP Cube Implementation Steps\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"1) Ensure the data warehouse is ready.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"2) Select fact and dimension tables.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"3) Define cube structure (dimensions, measures, hierarchies).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"4) Process the cube (calculate aggregations).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"5) Analyse using BI tools.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"10. Quick Decision Framework\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Historical, multi-year trend/comparison question \u2192 OLAP, not OLTP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Aggregating up a hierarchy \u2192 Roll-up; going into detail \u2192 Drill-down\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"One dimension fixed \u2192 Slice; multiple dimensions fixed \u2192 Dice\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Changing view orientation only \u2192 Pivot\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Huge data, must stay relational, tolerate slower queries \u2192 ROLAP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Need blazing-fast interactive queries, can afford "language": "javascript", "code": "const {\n  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, Table, TableRow, TableCell,\n  WidthType, ShadingType, BorderStyle, AlignmentType, LevelFormat\n} = require(\"docx\");\nconst fs = require(\"fs\");\n\nconst PAGE_WIDTH_DXA = 12240;\nconst PAGE_HEIGHT_DXA = 15840;\nconst MARGIN = 1080;\nconst USABLE_WIDTH = PAGE_WIDTH_DXA - MARGIN * 2;\n\nfunction h1(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 150 } });\n}\nfunction h2(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA (Lecture 07) ----------\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A manager wants to compare regional sales performance across the last five years and spot long-term trends, rather than process individual customer orders. Which statements correctly justify using OLAP rather than OLTP here?\",\n    options: [\n      \"OLAP is designed for analysing large volumes of historical data\",\n      \"OLAP supports identifying trends and comparing performance over time\",\n      \"OLTP is optimized for this kind of multi-year trend analysis\",\n      \"OLAP supports strategic decision-making through summarized views\",\n      \"OLTP would be the better fit since it is optimized for daily transaction processing, not analysis\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the three-tier OLAP architecture within a data warehousing environment, which statements correctly describe the roles of each tier?\",\n    options: [\n      \"The bottom tier (DW layer) stores integrated historical data via fact and dimension tables\",\n      \"The middle tier (OLAP layer) transforms warehouse data into multidimensional cubes\",\n      \"The top tier (analysis/reporting layer) includes tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Excel Pivot Tables\",\n      \"The bottom tier is responsible for performing roll-up, drill-down, and pivot operations\",\n      \"The middle tier is where end users directly view dashboards and visualizations\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analytics team notices that queries involving aggregation, joining, and grouping run extremely fast against their OLAP cube compared to equivalent tabular queries. Which statements explain this behavior?\",\n    options: [\n      \"OLAP cubes often pre-calculate common aggregations at different levels of detail\",\n      \"The cube structure is specifically optimized for operations like roll-up and drill-down\",\n      \"This speed advantage occurs because OLAP cubes never store any data, only formulas\",\n      \"Avoiding repeated scans of millions of records improves query response time\",\n      \"This behavior only occurs when cubes are implemented using pure ROLAP storage\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A dataset is analysed with only two dimensions (e.g., Product and Time), and later a third dimension (Location) is introduced. Which statements about the representation are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Two dimensions can typically be represented using a matrix\",\n      \"Adding a third dimension moves the representation toward a cube structure\",\n      \"A cube can only ever represent exactly two dimensions\",\n      \"Multiple related cubes can be used to represent additional dimensional combinations\",\n      \"A relational table alone is the most natural way to view three or more dimensions simultaneously\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A Location dimension contains levels such as Country \u2192 State \u2192 City, and a Time dimension contains Year \u2192 Quarter \u2192 Month. Which statements about this structure are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents a dimensional hierarchy within each dimension\",\n      \"A hierarchy defines how to move between detailed and summarized data\",\n      \"Every dimension must always have exactly one level with no hierarchy\",\n      \"Hierarchies enable operations like roll-up and drill-down along a dimension\",\n      \"Hierarchies exist only in the Time dimension and never in other dimensions\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst is viewing sales broken down by City and wants to see totals aggregated at the Country level instead. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Roll-up operation\",\n      \"It involves climbing up the Location hierarchy from City toward Country\",\n      \"This operation is also known as consolidation or aggregation\",\n      \"This is the opposite of roll-up, known as drill-down\",\n      \"This requires selecting a single dimension value to create a sub-cube\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst is viewing sales at the Quarter level and wants to see the more detailed Month-level breakdown within each quarter. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Drill-down operation\",\n      \"It steps down the Time hierarchy from Quarter to Month\",\n      \"Data becomes fragmented into smaller, more detailed parts\",\n      \"This is the same operation as roll-up since both change the Time dimension\",\n      \"This action aggregates data into a higher summary level\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst filters the sales cube to show data for only Q1, keeping all other dimensions (Product, Location) unrestricted. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Slice operation\",\n      \"It selects a single value for one dimension (Time = Q1)\",\n      \"The result is a rectangular subset of the original cube\",\n      \"This selects specific values across two or more dimensions simultaneously\",\n      \"This operation rotates the cube to present an alternate view\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An analyst filters the sales cube where (Product = 'Modems' or 'Wireless Mouse') AND (Time = '2000' or '2001') AND (Location = 'Euro' or 'Asia'). Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Dice operation\",\n      \"It selects specific values across two or more dimensions to form a new sub-cube\",\n      \"This differs from Slice, which restricts only a single dimension\",\n      \"This is identical to Slice since both filter the cube\",\n      \"This operation only ever applies to exactly one dimension at a time\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A report currently shows Products as rows and Regions as columns. The analyst rotates the view so that Regions become rows and Time periods become columns instead. Which statements correctly describe this action?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a Pivot operation\",\n      \"It rotates the data axes to provide an alternative presentation\",\n      \"It may involve swapping rows and columns or moving a dimension between axes\",\n      \"This changes the underlying data values stored in the cube\",\n      \"This is the same as a Roll-up, since both reorganize the view\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly distinguish Roll-up from Drill-down?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Roll-up aggregates data by climbing up a hierarchy\",\n      \"Drill-down navigates into more detailed data by stepping down a hierarchy\",\n      \"Roll-up and drill-down are functionally identical operations\",\n      \"Drill-down is the opposite process of roll-up\",\n      \"Both operations require selecting exactly one value from each dimension\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly distinguish Slice from Dice?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Slice restricts the cube using a single value on one dimension\",\n      \"Dice restricts the cube using values across two or more dimensions\",\n      \"Slice and Dice both always produce a single data point, never a sub-cube\",\n      \"Dice can be viewed as an extension of slicing across multiple dimensions\",\n      \"Slice always requires selecting exactly three dimensions simultaneously\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company implements ROLAP for its analytics platform, storing data directly in fact and dimension tables and using SQL queries for analysis. Which statements correctly describe this choice?\",\n    options: [\n      \"ROLAP can handle very large datasets effectively\",\n      \"ROLAP leverages existing relational database technology\",\n      \"ROLAP typically offers faster query performance than pre-built cubes\",\n      \"Query performance in ROLAP can be slower compared to pre-aggregated cube structures\",\n      \"ROLAP requires abandoning fact and dimension table structures entirely\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company implements MOLAP, storing sales data in a multidimensional cube structure with pre-calculated aggregations across Time, Product, and Location. Which statements correctly describe this choice?\",\n    options: [\n      \"MOLAP offers very fast analytical query performance\",\n      \"MOLAP is well suited for interactive analysis\",\n      \"MOLAP requires additional storage for the cube structure\",\n      \"MOLAP eliminates the need for any aggregation processing\",\n      \"Cube processing time is not a consideration in MOLAP implementations\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An organization stores transaction-level sales data in a relational database but keeps monthly sales summaries in a multidimensional cube. Which statements correctly describe this design?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is a HOLAP (Hybrid OLAP) approach\",\n      \"Detailed data is handled using the ROLAP-style relational storage\",\n      \"Summary data is handled using the MOLAP-style cube storage\",\n      \"This approach cannot use any OLAP operations like roll-up or drill-down\",\n      \"ROLAP, MOLAP, and HOLAP differ only in storage, not in core OLAP concepts\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company has an extremely large dataset that must remain queryable via existing relational database infrastructure, and can tolerate somewhat slower analytical queries. Which storage type reasoning applies best?\",\n    options: [\n      \"ROLAP is a reasonable fit given the large data volume\",\n      \"ROLAP uses SQL queries directly against fact and dimension tables\",\n      \"MOLAP would guarantee equal or better performance with zero storage overhead\",\n      \"ROLAP avoids the need for extensive pre-built cube storage\",\n      \"HOLAP is the only storage type capable of handling large datasets\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company needs extremely fast, interactive analytical queries for a moderately sized dataset and is willing to invest in extra storage and pre-processing time. Which storage type reasoning applies best?\",\n    options: [\n      \"MOLAP is a strong fit given the priority on query speed\",\n      \"MOLAP pre-calculates aggregations to speed up analysis\",\n      \"MOLAP requires no additional storage compared to ROLAP\",\n      \"Cube processing time is a trade-off worth considering with MOLAP\",\n      \"ROLAP would always outperform MOLAP for this use case\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A team is designing a new OLAP cube for sales analysis. Which elements must be defined as part of the cube design process?\",\n    options: [\n      \"The business process being analyzed\",\n      \"The measures (facts) to be captured, such as sales amount\",\n      \"The dimensions and their hierarchies (e.g., Time, Product, Location)\",\n      \"The specific BI tool's color theme and dashboard layout\",\n      \"The relationships between dimensions and facts\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which sequence of steps correctly reflects OLAP cube implementation as described in the lecture?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Ensure the data warehouse is ready before building the cube\",\n      \"Select the relevant fact and dimension tables\",\n      \"Define the cube structure (dimensions, measures, hierarchies) and process aggregations\",\n      \"Skip data warehouse readiness since OLAP cubes can be built directly from raw source systems\",\n      \"Analyse the processed cube using BI tools\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A retail sales table contains columns: Product, Region, Year, and Sales_Amount.
