Select all that apply.\", { italics: true }));\nchildren.push(hr());\n\nmcqs.forEach((q, idx) => {\n  children.push(...questionBlock(idx + 1, q.stem, q.options));\n});\n\nchildren.push(new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: \"\", break: 1 })], pageBreakBefore: true }));\n\n// SECTION 2: Answer key table\nchildren.push(h1(\"Section 2: Answer Key\"));\nconst keyRows = [\n  new TableRow({\n    children: [cell(\"Q#\", { width: 1200, shade: \"D9D9D9\", bold: true }), cell(\"Correct Options\", { width: USABLE_WIDTH - 1200, shade: \"D9D9D9\", bold: true })],\n  }),\n];\nanswerKey.forEach((ans, i) => {\n  keyRows.push(\n    new TableRow({\n      children: [cell(String(i + 1), { width: 1200 }), cell(ans, { width: USABLE_WIDTH - 1200 })],\n    })\n  );\n});\nchildren.push(\n  new Table({\n    width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    columnWidths: [1200, USABLE_WIDTH - 1200],\n    rows: keyRows,\n  })\n);\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Note: For Q18, Q19, and Q22 more than 3 options are defensible; examiners may accept the broader set or narrow to the 3 strongest.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: \"\", break: 1 })], pageBreakBefore: true }));\n\n// SECTION 3: Short Notes\nchildren.push(h1(\"Section 3: Short Notes (Quick Revision)\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"1. What is OLAP?\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) analyses large volumes of historical data stored in a data warehouse.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Enables: analysing data from different perspectives, identifying trends, comparing performance, generating summaries/reports, supporting decision-making.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"The DW stores integrated historical data; OLAP provides the analytical capability to explore it.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"2. OLTP vs OLAP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLTP \u2014 optimized for day-to-day transaction processing (fast inserts/updates, operational systems).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"OLAP \u2014 optimized for analysing historical, integrated data for trends and strategic decisions.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"3. Role of OLAP in Data Warehousing \u2014 Three Tiers\"));\nconst tierRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Tier\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2000}), cell(\"Role\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:4700}), cell(\"Example\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Bottom \u2014 Data Warehouse\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Stores integrated historical data; fact and dimension tables from ETL\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Sales fact table with Product, Customer, Time dimensions\", {width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Middle \u2014 OLAP Layer\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Transforms warehouse data into multidimensional cubes; enables fast queries\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot operations\", {width:3300})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Top \u2014 Analysis/Reporting\", {width:2000}), cell(\"Interfaces for exploring OLAP results\", {width:4700}), cell(\"Power BI, Tableau, Excel Pivot Tables\", {width:3300})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [2000,4700,3300], rows: tierRows }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"4. OLAP Cubes\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"A multidimensional structure organizing data from a DW to support fast, interactive analysis.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Analyses measures (facts) from different perspectives (dimensions).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Pre-calculates aggregation, joining, and grouping so queries run fast without scanning raw records.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Table \u2192 Matrix \u2192 Cube: a table is 2D at best; a matrix handles 2 dimensions; a cube handles 3+ dimensions; multiple related cubes can represent even more combinations.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"5. Dimensional Hierarchy\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"A dimension often has multiple levels of detail forming a hierarchy (e.g., Country \u2192 State \u2192 City; Year \u2192 Quarter \u2192 Month).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Hierarchies define how to move between detailed and summarized data \u2014 the basis for roll-up and drill-down.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"6. OLAP Operations\"));\nconst opRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Operation\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:1800}), cell(\"What it does\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:5000}), cell(\"Direction/Note\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Roll-up\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Climbs up a hierarchy to aggregate data (e.g., City \u2192 Country)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Aka consolidation/aggregation\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Drill-down\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Steps down a hierarchy for more detail (e.g., Quarter \u2192 Month)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Opposite of roll-up\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Slice\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Selects a single value on ONE dimension\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Produces a rectangular subset of the cube\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Dice\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Selects specific values across TWO OR MORE dimensions\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Produces a smaller sub-cube\", {width:3200})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Pivot\", {width:1800}), cell(\"Rotates data axes for an alternate view (swap rows/columns)\", {width:5000}), cell(\"Visualization only \u2014 doesn't change stored values\", {width:3200})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [1800,5000,3200], rows: opRows }));\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Exam tip: One dimension filtered \u2192 Slice. Two+ dimensions filtered \u2192 Dice. Aggregating upward \u2192 Roll-up. Going more detailed \u2192 Drill-down. Just changing the view's orientation \u2192 Pivot.\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"7. OLAP Storage Types\"));\nconst storageRows = [\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"Type\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:1600}), cell(\"Storage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:3400}), cell(\"Advantage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2500}), cell(\"Disadvantage\", {shade:\"D9D9D9\", bold:true, width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"ROLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Relational tables (fact + dimension); SQL-based analysis\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Handles very large datasets; uses existing RDBMS tech\", {width:2500}), cell(\"Slower query performance vs. pre-built cubes\", {width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"MOLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Multidimensional cube structure; pre-calculated aggregations\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Very fast queries; great for interactive analysis\", {width:2500}), cell(\"Needs extra storage; cube processing takes time\", {width:2500})] }),\n  new TableRow({ children: [cell(\"HOLAP\", {width:1600}), cell(\"Hybrid \u2014 detail in relational DB, summary in cube\", {width:3400}), cell(\"Balances scalability and speed\", {width:2500}), cell(\"More complex to design/manage\", {width:2500})] }),\n];\nchildren.push(new Table({ width: { size: USABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: [1600,3400,2500,2500], rows: storageRows }));\nchildren.push(p(\"\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Note: ROLAP, MOLAP, and HOLAP differ only in how data is stored \u2014 all three still use the same OLAP concepts (dimensions, measures, hierarchies, operations).\", { italics: true }));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"8. OLAP Cube Design\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Define: (1) business process to analyze, (2) measures/facts, (3) dimensions, (4) hierarchies, (5) relationships between dimensions and facts.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Goal: enable fast analytical queries for decision-making.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"9. OLAP Cube Implementation Steps\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"1) Ensure the data warehouse is ready.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"2) Select fact and dimension tables.\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"3) Define cube structure (dimensions, measures, hierarchies).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"4) Process the cube (calculate aggregations).\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"5) Analyse using BI tools.\"));\n\nchildren.push(h2(\"10. Quick Decision Framework\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Historical, multi-year trend/comparison question \u2192 OLAP, not OLTP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Aggregating up a hierarchy \u2192 Roll-up; going into detail \u2192 Drill-down\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"One dimension fixed \u2192 Slice; multiple dimensions fixed \u2192 Dice\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Changing view orientation only \u2192 Pivot\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Huge data, must stay relational, tolerate slower queries \u2192 ROLAP\"));\nchildren.push(bullet(\"Need blazing-fast interactive queries, can afford Honours in Information Technology - Specialization in Data Science\r\nIT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence\r\nLecture 01\r\nMr. Nadana Swasthi\r\nModule Learning Outcomes\r\nAt the end of the module, the student will be able to:\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 2\r\nLO1 Demonstrate data warehousing design principles various technologies\r\nand tools to create efficient and scalable data models.\r\nLO2 Apply ETL processes and integration techniques to extract transform and\r\nload data into a data warehouse.\r\nLO3 Evaluate and apply business intelligence tools and techniques for\r\nreporting visualization and data analysis.\r\nLO4 Design and create visually compelling data visualizations and interactive\r\ndashboards to present insights effectively.\r\nLO5 Apply and analyze data governance and security measures in data\r\nwarehousing environment to protect data integrity and privacy.\r\nSyllabus\r\nOutline &\r\nLesson Plan\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 3\r\nWeek Lecture\r\n1 Lecture 1 - Introduction\r\n2 Lecture 2 - Data Warehouse Design and Architecture\r\n3 Lecture 3 - Data Modeling for Data Warehousing\r\n4 Lecture 4 - Data Modeling for Data Warehousing\r\n5 Lecture 5 \u2013 ETL Process and Data Integration\r\n6 Lecture 6 \u2013 ETL Process and Data Integration\r\n7 Lecture 7 - Querying and SQL for DW\r\n8 Mid Week\r\n9 Lecture 8 - Data Analysis and OLAP\r\n10 Lecture 9 - Business Intelligence Concepts and Tools\r\n11 Lecture 10 - Reporting and Dashboard Development\r\n12 Lecture 11 - Reporting and Dashboard Development\r\n13 Lecture 12 - Storytelling with Data\r\n14 Lecture 13 - Data Governance and Security in DW\r\n15 Lecture 14 - Emerging Trends in DW\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 4\r\nRecommended text\r\n1. R. Kimball and M. Ross, The data warehouse toolkit : the definitive guide to\r\ndimensional modeling, 3rd ed. John Wiley Sons, Inc., 2013.\r\n2. R. Sherman, Business intelligence guidebook : from data integration to\r\nanalytics. Amsterdam: Elsevier, 2015, pp. 449\u2013492.\r\n3. Kieran Healy, Data visualization : a practical introduction. Princeton, N.J.:\r\nPrinceton University Press, 2019.\r\n4. C. N. Knaflic, Storytelling with data : a data visualization guide for business\r\nprofessionals. Hoboken, New Jersey: Wiley, 2015.\r\nMethod of Assessment\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 5\r\nMid Term Examination 20%\r\nLab Test 10%\r\nAssignment 20%\r\nFinal Examination 50%\r\nStudents must complete at least 80% of lab submissions to be eligible for the Mid\r\nTerm Examination.\r\nContent for Today\r\n1. Definition and importance of DWBI\r\n2. Benefits of implementing DWBI solutions\r\n3. Challenges and considerations in designing and deploying DWBI solutions\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 6\r\nIntroduction\r\nImagine you own a coffee shop.\r\nEvery day, your business generates data from orders, customers, employees,\r\nexpenses, and suppliers. At this stage, information is small and easy to manage,\r\nand you can quickly understand how your business is performing.\r\nAfter five years, the situation changes completely.\r\nNow you have millions of records spread across multiple branches, online ordering\r\nsystems, delivery platforms, loyalty programs, and supplier networks.\r\nThe volume and complexity of data grow beyond manual analysis or simple\r\nreporting tools.\r\nOn a random day you want to determine which branch is performing best?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 7\r\nData Warehouse (DW)\r\nA data warehouse is a centralized repository that stores integrated, cleaned, and\r\nhistorical data collected from multiple sources.\r\nIt is specifically designed to support analysis and decision-making, rather than\r\nday-to-day transaction processing.\r\n\u201cA data warehouse is a subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, and nonvolatile collection of data in support of management\u2019s decision-making process.\u201d\r\n- Bill Inmon, the Father of Data Warehousing\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 8\r\nSubject-Oriented\r\nA data warehouse is organized around major subjects such as customers,\r\nsuppliers, products, sales, and inventory.\r\nUnlike operational systems that are designed for individual business\r\ntransactions (e.g., placing an order, updating customer information), a data\r\nwarehouse is designed to support analysis and decision-making.\r\nIt focuses on understanding important business areas rather than processing daily\r\noperations.\r\nA subject-oriented design provides a structured view of business information by\r\norganizing related data around key subjects.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 9\r\nSubject-Oriented\r\nExample: A sales analysis subject may combine information about customers,\r\nproducts, stores, sales transactions.\r\nThis allows managers to answer questions such as:\r\n\u2022 Which products generate the highest revenue?\r\n\u2022 Which customer segments are most profitable?\r\n\u2022 How have sales changed over time?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 10\r\nIntegrated\r\nA data warehouse is built by integrating data from multiple heterogeneous data\r\nsources.\r\nData Sources: Relational databases, Online transaction processing (OLTP)\r\nsystems, Flat files (CSV, Excel), External systems / APIs.\r\nTraditionally, data warehouses mainly store structured data. However, modern\r\ndata warehouse platforms can also handle semi-structured data as well.\r\nData cleaning and data integration techniques ensure consistency in:\r\n\u2022 Naming conventions\r\n\u2022 Attribute measurements\r\nExample: If one system stores gender as \"M/F\" and another as \"Male/Female,\" the\r\nwarehouse integrates them into a consistent format.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 11\r\n\u2022 Encoding structures\r\nTime-Variant\r\nA data warehouse stores historical data over a long period. (typically, 5 - 10 years\r\nor more).\r\nHistorical data provides trends and patterns that are crucial for forecasting,\r\nstrategic planning, and decision-making.\r\nEvery key structure (tables, records, attributes) in the warehouse usually contains\r\na time dimension, either explicitly (timestamps, date fields) or implicitly\r\n(snapshot-based historical records).\r\nExample: Sales data can be analyzed by year, quarter, month, or week to identify\r\nseasonal patterns.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 12\r\nNon-Volatile\r\nA data warehouse is a separate data store, distinct from operational databases.\r\nOnce entered, data is generally not updated or deleted; instead, it is appended\r\nwith new historical data.\r\nBecause the data warehouse is mainly read-oriented, it does not require the same\r\nlevel of frequent transaction processing and concurrency control as operational\r\ndatabases.\r\nOnly two main operations are performed:\r\n1. Initial data loading (bulk data transfer from sources)\r\n2. Data access/retrieval (queries and analysis)\r\nThis ensures stable, reliable data for decision support.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 13\r\nActivity: Identify the Characteristics of a Data Warehouse\r\nA data warehouse has four important characteristics:\r\n\u2022 Subject-oriented\r\n\u2022 Integrated\r\n\u2022 Time-variant\r\n\u2022 Non-volatile\r\nRead each scenario and decide which characteristic it represents.\r\nFor each answer, write one sentence explaining why.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 14\r\nActivity: Identify the Characteristics of a Data Warehouse\r\nNo. Scenario Characteristic Reason\r\n1\r\nA company combines customer information\r\nfrom the CRM system, online ordering\r\nplatform, and loyalty application into one\r\nconsistent customer view.\r\n2\r\nA retail manager analyses sales performance\r\nby product category, customer segment, and\r\nbranch location.\r\n3\r\nThe company keeps sales records from the\r\nprevious 10 years to identify seasonal trends.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 15\r\nActivity: Identify the Characteristics of a Data Warehouse\r\nNo. Scenario Characteristic Reason\r\n4\r\nOnce daily sales data is loaded into the\r\nwarehouse, business users can only query\r\nand analyse the data.\r\n5\r\nOne system stores gender as \"M\", another\r\nas \"Male\", and another as \"1\". The\r\nwarehouse converts all values into a\r\ncommon format.\r\n6\r\nEvery month, new sales records are added\r\nwhile previous historical records are\r\npreserved.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 16\r\nActivity: Identify the Characteristics of a Data Warehouse\r\nWhich characteristic is most important when building a\r\nmodel to predict next year's sales? Why?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 17\r\nBusiness intelligence (BI)\r\nBusiness intelligence (BI) is the process of transforming data into actionable\r\ninsights that help a company make strategic and tactical decisions.\r\nBusiness intelligence outlines the strategies, processes, and tools businesses use to\r\nanalyse data and extract meaningful insights.\r\nBI covers everything from statistical analysis to data storytelling to ultimately feed\r\ndata-driven decisions, providing users with accurate intelligence about the state of\r\nthe business.\r\nIt transforms data into knowledge.\r\nBusiness Intelligence relies on data warehousing to extract the required data.\r\nThus, a data warehouse acts as a backend for Business Intelligence.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 18\r\nHistory of Data Warehousing\r\nPeriod Milestone\r\n1960s\u20131970s Early data analysis ideas \u2192 facts & dimensions\r\n1980s Decision Support Systems + early data marts\r\n1990 Data warehouse formally defined (Bill Inmon)\r\n2000s Business Intelligence tools expand\r\nToday Cloud data warehouses + AI + real-time analytics\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 19\r\nEvolution of Business Intelligence\r\nTransaction Processing\r\nSystems (TPS)\r\n1960s\r\nDecision Support\r\nSystems (DSS)\r\n1980s\r\nData Warehouses\r\n1990s\r\nBusiness Intelligence\r\n2000s\r\nCloud Data\r\nWarehouses + AI +\r\nReal-Time Analytics\r\nToday\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 20\r\nActivity: Where Does This Task Belong?\r\nThe following business activities happen in a coffee-shop company.\r\nClassify each activity into one of these categories:\r\nCategories\r\nA. Operational System (OLTP): Used for daily business transactions and realtime operations.\r\nB. Data Warehouse (Analytical Storage): Used for storing integrated historical\r\ndata and performing analysis.\r\nC. Business Intelligence / Data Science: Used for generating insights, reports,\r\ndashboards, predictions, and supporting decisions.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 21\r\nActivity: Where Does This Task Belong?\r\nTask No. Business Activity Your Classification\r\n1 Record a new coffee order.\r\n2 Update a customer\u2019s delivery address.\r\n3\r\nCalculate revenue by branch for the last five\r\nyears.\r\n4 Display monthly profit on a dashboard.\r\n5 Detect unusual sales patterns.\r\n6 Process a card payment.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 22\r\nHigh-Level Architecture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 23\r\nImportance of DW\r\nData is scattered across systems\r\n\u2022 In most organizations, data is not stored in a single place.\r\n\u2022 Different systems (sales, HR, finance, inventory) operate independently.\r\nInconsistent definitions across departments\r\n\u2022 Different departments store similar data in different formats or standards.\r\n\u2022 This makes integration and reporting difficult.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 24\r\nImportance of DW\r\nHard to access historical data\r\n\u2022 Operational systems are designed for current-day transactions, not long-term\r\nstorage or trend analysis.\r\n\u2022 Historical data is often archived, fragmented, or difficult to retrieve.\r\nOperational systems cannot handle analytics\r\n\u2022 Operational systems (e.g., POS, banking, HR systems) are optimized for fast\r\ntransactions such as insert, update, and delete operations.\r\n\u2022 Complex analytical queries can slow them down or disrupt daily operations.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 25\r\nBenefits of DW\r\n\u2022 Integrates data from multiple sources into a centralized repository.\r\n\u2022 Provides clean, consistent, and standardized data for accurate analysis.\r\n\u2022 Stores historical data to support trend analysis and long-term decision-making.\r\n\u2022 Eliminates data silos by combining data across different departments and\r\nsystems.\r\n\u2022 Improves data quality and reliability, enabling trustworthy reporting and\r\nanalytics.\r\n\u2022 Enables fast and efficient querying of large volumes of data without affecting\r\noperational systems.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 26\r\nImportance of BI\r\nRaw data alone is not useful for decisions\r\n\u2022 Organizations generate large volumes of data, but raw data in its original form\r\nis difficult to interpret and act upon.\r\nManagers need insights, not tables\r\n\u2022 Decision-makers do not want to analyse raw tables or complex datasets.\r\n\u2022 They need summarized, meaningful information such as trends, comparisons,\r\nand predictions.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 27\r\nImportance of BI\r\nOrganizations need performance monitoring\r\n\u2022 Businesses must continuously track performance to understand whether goals\r\nare being achieved.\r\n\u2022 This includes monitoring KPIs such as sales, profit, customer growth, and\r\noperational efficiency.\r\nBusiness Intelligence is needed because data must be turned into meaningful\r\ninsights for decision-making and performance tracking.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 28\r\nBenefits of BI\r\n\u2022 Transforms data into meaningful insights for informed decision-making.\r\n\u2022 Provides interactive dashboards, reports, and visualizations to support business\r\nanalysis.\r\n\u2022 Identifies trends, patterns, and anomalies to uncover valuable insights.\r\n\u2022 Monitors business performance using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).\r\n\u2022 Helps organizations identify opportunities and address problems quickly.\r\n\u2022 Supports strategic, tactical, and operational decision-making across all levels of\r\nan organization.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 29\r\nChallenges in DWBI\r\n1. Poor Data Quality\r\nData collected from different sources may contain duplicates, missing values,\r\ninconsistent formats, or incorrect information, leading to unreliable analysis.\r\nConsideration: Implement data cleansing, validation, and quality management\r\nprocesses.\r\n2. Data Integration Complexity\r\nCombining data from multiple systems (e.g., CRM, ERP, HR, Finance) can be\r\ndifficult due to differences in formats, structures, and update frequencies.\r\nConsideration: Use well-designed ETL/ELT processes and standardized data\r\nmodels.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 30\r\nChallenges in DWBI\r\n3. Performance and Scalability\r\nAs data volume and the number of users increase, analytical queries may become\r\nslower and system performance may degrade.\r\nConsideration: Optimize database design and choose scalable architectures.\r\n4. Security and Compliance\r\nData warehouses often store sensitive business and customer information that\r\nmust be protected from unauthorized access and comply with legal regulations.\r\nConsideration: Implement access controls, encryption, auditing, and compliance\r\npolicies.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 31\r\nChallenges in DWBI\r\n5. High Implementation and Maintenance Cost\r\nDeveloping and maintaining a data warehouse requires significant investment in\r\ninfrastructure, software, skilled personnel, and ongoing support.\r\nConsideration: Evaluate costs carefully and consider cloud-based solutions where\r\nappropriate.\r\n6. Data Governance\r\nWithout proper governance, organizations may experience inconsistent data\r\ndefinitions, poor data ownership, and reduced trust in analytical results.\r\nConsideration: Establish clear data standards, ownership, and governance\r\npolicies.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 32\r\nIn Next Lecture\r\nYou will learn about Data Warehouse Design and Architecture\r\n1. Components and architecture of a data warehouse\r\n2. Operational databases vs Data warehouses\r\n3. Data sources, data integration and data transformation\r\n4. Enterprise data warehouse and Data mart\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 33\r\nThank you\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 34"}], "files": [{"file_uuid": "21f46c3d-0544-4f18-b744-1f11f312b9ce", "file_name": ""}], "parent_message_uuid": "01a06fb0-a48f-73ae-9b34-301e53a42d14"}, {"uuid": "01a06fb1-dfc4-7328-bdfe-adc7ae501058", "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nEverything renders well. Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Time-Variant characteristic\",\n      \"Long-term historical retention supports identifying trends and seasonal patterns\",\n      \"This represents the Integrated characteristic instead\",\n      \"This aligns with using a time dimension across warehouse structures\",\n      \"This scenario indicates data is deleted after each year to save space\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'Once daily sales data is loaded into the warehouse, business users can only query and analyse the data.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Non-Volatile characteristic\",\n      \"Data is read-oriented after loading, without frequent updates or deletes\",\n      \"This represents the Subject-Oriented characteristic instead\",\n      \"This matches the idea that only loading and retrieval operations occur\",\n      \"This scenario suggests users can freely edit historical warehouse records\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'One system stores gender as \\\"M\\\", another as \\\"Male\\\", and another as \\\"1\\\". The warehouse converts all values into a common format.'     \"Cloud Data Warehouses, AI, and real-time analytics represent the earliest historical stage\",\n      \"This evolution reflects a general shift from transaction recording toward advanced analytics\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In a coffee-shop company, an employee 'records a new coffee order' and later 'processes a card payment' for that order. "language": "javascript", "code": "const {\n  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel, Table, TableRow, TableCell,\n  WidthType, ShadingType, BorderStyle, AlignmentType, LevelFormat\n} = require(\"docx\");\nconst fs = require(\"fs\");\n\nconst PAGE_WIDTH_DXA = 12240;\nconst PAGE_HEIGHT_DXA = 15840;\nconst MARGIN = 1080;\nconst USABLE_WIDTH = PAGE_WIDTH_DXA - MARGIN * 2;\n\nfunction h1(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 150 } });\n}\nfunction h2(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA (Lecture 01) ----------\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A coffee shop owner used to track daily sales easily on paper, but after five years of growth (multiple branches, online ordering, delivery platforms, loyalty programs), determining which branch performs best becomes very difficult. Which statements explain why a Data Warehouse is now needed?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Data volume and complexity have grown beyond manual analysis or simple reporting\",\n      \"A DW can integrate scattered data from multiple systems into one centralized view\",\n      \"Operational systems used for daily orders are ideal for this kind of multi-branch trend analysis\",\n      \"A DW supports historical, cross-branch analysis rather than single-transaction processing\",\n      \"The owner should keep using individual system reports instead of consolidating data\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A retail manager combines customer, product, store, and sales transaction data into one structured view to answer questions like 'which products generate the highest revenue?'. Which characteristic of a data warehouse does this best illustrate, and why?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Subject-Oriented, since data is organized around a key business area (sales analysis)\",\n      \"It focuses on understanding business areas rather than processing individual transactions\",\n      \"Non-Volatile, since no data is ever added after the initial load\",\n      \"This organization helps managers analyse profitability and revenue trends by subject\",\n      \"Time-Variant, since the primary focus here is historical timestamps\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"One source system stores gender as 'M/F' while another stores it as 'Male/Female'. The data warehouse converts both into a single consistent format before storage. Which statements correctly describe this?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This illustrates the Integrated characteristic of a data warehouse\",\n      \"Data cleaning and integration techniques ensure consistency in naming and encoding\",\n      \"This is an example of the Non-Volatile characteristic instead\",\n      \"Without this step, combining data from multiple heterogeneous sources would be inconsistent\",\n      \"This process is unrelated to combining data from multiple sources\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company retains 8 years of sales data so analysts can study seasonal patterns by year, quarter, and month. Which statements correctly relate to this scenario?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This illustrates the Time-Variant characteristic of a data warehouse\",\n      \"Historical data supports forecasting, strategic planning, and trend analysis\",\n      \"Warehouse structures typically include a time dimension, explicit or implicit\",\n      \"This scenario is instead an example of the Non-Volatile characteristic\",\n      \"Operational systems are typically better suited for this kind of long-term historical analysis\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Once daily sales data is loaded into the warehouse, business users can only query and analyse it \u2014 no updates or deletions occur afterward. Which statements correctly describe this behavior?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This illustrates the Non-Volatile characteristic\",\n      \"Only two main operations occur: initial loading and data access/retrieval\",\n      \"This differs from operational databases, which require frequent updates and concurrency control\",\n      \"This is an example of the Subject-Oriented characteristic instead\",\n      \"This design ensures stable, reliable data for decision support\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'A company combines customer information from the CRM system, online ordering platform, and loyalty application into one consistent customer view.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Integrated characteristic\",\n      \"Multiple heterogeneous sources are combined into a unified, consistent view\",\n      \"This represents the Time-Variant characteristic instead\",\n      \"This is similar in nature to reconciling inconsistent formats across systems\",\n      \"No data cleaning or consistency work would be required in this scenario\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'A retail manager analyses sales performance by product category, customer segment, and branch location.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Subject-Oriented characteristic\",\n      \"The analysis is organized around key business subjects (products, customers, branches)\",\n      \"This represents the Non-Volatile characteristic instead\",\n      \"This kind of analysis supports understanding of major business areas rather than daily transactions\",\n      \"This scenario primarily demonstrates combining data formats from different sources\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'The company keeps sales records from the previous 10 years to identify seasonal trends.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Time-Variant characteristic\",\n      \"Long-term historical retention supports identifying trends and seasonal patterns\",\n      \"This represents the Integrated characteristic instead\",\n      \"This aligns with using a time dimension across warehouse structures\",\n      \"This scenario indicates data is deleted after each year to save space\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'Once daily sales data is loaded into the warehouse, business users can only query and analyse the data.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Non-Volatile characteristic\",\n      \"Data is read-oriented after loading, without frequent updates or deletes\",\n      \"This represents the Subject-Oriented characteristic instead\",\n      \"This matches the idea that only loading and retrieval operations occur\",\n      \"This scenario suggests users can freely edit historical warehouse records\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'One system stores gender as \\\"M\\\", another as \\\"Male\\\", and another as \\\"1\\\". The warehouse converts all values into a common format.' Which characteristic and reasoning apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This represents the Integrated characteristic\",\n      \"Standardizing values from multiple sources into a consistent format is a core integration task\",\n      \"This represents the Non-Volatile characteristic instead\",\n      \"This reflects resolving encoding and naming convention differences across sources\",\n      \"This scenario has no connection to combining heterogeneous data sources\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Scenario: 'Every month, new sales records are added while previous historical records are preserved.' Which characteristic(s) and reasoning best apply?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This reflects the Non-Volatile characteristic, since old data is preserved rather than overwritten\",\n      \"This also reflects the Time-Variant characteristic, since historical records accumulate over time\",\n      \"This is best explained purely as the Subject-Oriented characteristic\",\n      \"New data is appended rather than replacing existing historical data\",\n      \"This indicates records are deleted once a new month begins\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A data science team wants to build a model to predict next year's sales using several years of past performance. Which reasoning best explains which DW characteristic matters most here?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Time-Variant is most critical, since forecasting relies on historical trends and patterns\",\n      \"Without sufficient historical depth, seasonal and trend patterns would be hard to detect\",\n      \"Non-Volatility is the most critical factor for enabling forecasting models\",\n      \"A time dimension (explicit or implicit) supports analysing performance across periods\",\n      \"Subject-Orientation alone would be sufficient without any historical data\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly describe Business Intelligence (BI) and its relationship to a data warehouse?\",\n    options: [\n      \"BI transforms data into actionable insights for strategic and "2026-09-05T04:01:28.121438Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-09-05T04:01:28.121559Z", "updated_at": "2026-09-05T04:01:28.121559Z", "attachments": [{"file_name": "", "file_size": 15147, "file_type": "txt", "extracted_content": "Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology\r\nB.Sc. Honours in Information Technology - Specialization in Data Science\r\nIT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence\r\nLecture 02\r\nMr. Nadana Swasthi\r\nContent\r\n1. Components and architecture of a data warehouse\r\n2. Operational databases vs Data warehouses\r\n3. Data sources, data integration and data transformation\r\n4. Enterprise data warehouse and Data mart\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 2\r\nFrom Lecture 1:\r\nOrganizations need a data warehouse because:\r\n\u2022 Data exists across multiple operational systems.\r\n\u2022 Analytical requirements differ from transaction processing.\r\n\u2022 Integrated and historical data is required for decision-making.\r\nToday we focus on,\r\nHow do we design a system that moves data from\r\noperational systems into an analytical environment?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 3\r\nOperational Database vs Data Warehouse\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 4\r\nOperational Database vs Data Warehouse\r\nOperational Database Data Warehouse\r\nSupports daily transactions Supports decision making\r\nCurrent data Historical data\r\nHighly normalized Often denormalized\r\nFrequent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE Mostly read-oriented\r\nOptimized for transactions Optimized for analytical queries\r\nMany small queries Fewer but more complex queries\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 5\r\nHow does raw organizational data become a trusted\r\nanalytical asset that can be used for BI and Data Science?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 6\r\nHigh Level Architecture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 7\r\nWhere Does Warehouse Data Come From?\r\nUniversity Analytics Platform\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 8\r\nBefore data can be stored in a warehouse, data from different sources must be\r\nintegrated into a consistent format.\r\nData Integration Problem\r\nData integration is the process of combining data from multiple sources into\r\na consistent and unified view for analysis.\r\nIt enables organizations to:\r\n\u2022 Break down data silos\r\n\u2022 Improve data consistency and quality\r\n\u2022 Support analytics and decision-making\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 9\r\nData Integration Problem\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 10\r\nCommon Data Integration Challenges\r\nPoor data quality\r\nMissing values, duplicates, inaccurate or inconsistent data.\r\nIncompatible data formats and structures\r\nDifferent schemas, databases, file formats and naming conventions.\r\nManaging large data volumes\r\nHandling increasing amounts of data efficiently and reliably.\r\nReal-time data requirements\r\nProviding timely data for applications requiring low-latency updates.\r\nSecurity and compliance concerns\r\nProtecting sensitive data during movement and integration.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 11\r\nETL Pipeline\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 12\r\nETL vs ELT\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 13\r\nComponents of a Data Warehouse\r\nA well-designed data warehouse provides a centralized platform for storing,\r\nintegrating, and analysing vast amount of data to support informed business\r\ndecision-making.\r\nA typical data warehouse consists of the following key components:\r\n1. Data Sources\r\n2. Data Integration & Ingestion (ETL/ELT)\r\n3. Staging Area\r\n4. Central Data Warehouse\r\n5. Data Marts\r\n6. Metadata\r\n7. Business Intelligence (BI) & Access Tools\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 14\r\nComponents of a DW - Data Sources\r\nData sources are the original internal and external systems that provide raw\r\ndata to the data warehouse.\r\nData sources include:\r\n\u2022 Internal operational systems: Sales, HR, finance, and transaction databases\r\nthat generate core business data.\r\n\u2022 External systems: Third-party providers, partner systems, web applications,\r\nand APIs.\r\nThese sources provide mainly raw structured data that is used for analytical\r\nprocessing in a data warehouse.\r\nSince source data is often scattered and inconsistent, it must be extracted, cleaned,\r\nand transformed before being loaded into the warehouse.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 15\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\nA large online retail company wants to build a Business Intelligence system.\r\nCurrently, data is stored in multiple operational systems:\r\n\u2022 Customer Management System\r\n\u2022 Online Shopping System\r\n\u2022 Payment System\r\n\u2022 Inventory Management System\r\n\u2022 Delivery Tracking System\r\n\u2022 Customer Review Platform\r\nDraw the first layer of the architecture and identify,\r\n1. What are the data sources?\r\n2. Are these operational databases or analytical systems?\r\n3. Why cannot management directly run analytics on these systems?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 16\r\nComponents of a DW - ETL\r\nETL is the process of moving data from multiple sources into a data\r\nwarehouse.\r\nIt consists of three steps:\r\n1. Extract: Collect data from source systems\r\n2. Transform: Clean, standardize, and integrate data\r\n3. Load: Store data into the data warehouse\r\nThe purpose of ETL is to ensure that data is clean, consistent, integrated, and\r\nready for analysis.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 17\r\nComponents of a DW\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 18\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\nYou are a Data Engineer working for an online retail company.\r\nThe company receives daily sales data from different operational systems. Before\r\nloading this data into the data warehouse, you must clean and transform it.\r\nYou receive the following raw data.\r\nSource 1: Sales System\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 19\r\nOrder_ID Customer_ID Product_ID Order_Date Amount\r\n1001 C101 P01 01/05/25 25000.00\r\n1002 103 001 2025-05-01 15000\r\n1003 C102 P02 May 2 2025 Rs. 12000\r\n1003 C102 P02 May 2 2025 12000\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\nSource 2: Customer System\r\n1. Identify Data Quality Problems\r\n2. Create rules that will convert raw data into warehouse-ready data.\r\n3. After transformation, what should the final Sales Fact table look like?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 20\r\nCustomer_ID Customer_Name City\r\nC101 John Smith Colombo\r\n101 JOHN SMITH Colombo\r\nC102 Nimal Perera Kandy\r\nC103 Amali Dias GALLE\r\nComponents of a DW - Staging Area\r\nA staging area is a temporary storage space where raw data from multiple\r\nsources is collected, cleaned, and transformed before loading into the data\r\nwarehouse.\r\nIt acts as a buffer zone in the ETL process, ensuring only validated and\r\nconsistent data enters the warehouse.\r\nWhy a Staging Area is Needed\r\n\u2022 Cleans data by removing errors, duplicates, and missing values\r\n\u2022 Improves performance by avoiding heavy processing in the data warehouse\r\n\u2022 Standardizes data from different systems into a common format\r\n\u2022 Keeps raw data copies for debugging and recovery\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 21\r\nComponents of a DW - Staging Area\r\nRole in ETL\r\n1. Extract: Raw data is copied into the\r\nstaging area\r\n2. Transform: Data is cleaned,\r\nformatted, and integrated\r\n3. Load: Processed data is moved into\r\nthe data warehouse\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 22\r\nComponents of a DW - Central Data Warehouse\r\nThe data warehouse database is the central repository where cleansed,\r\nintegrated, historical, and subject-oriented data is stored.\r\nA central data warehouse acts as a single source of truth, eliminating data\r\nsilos.\r\nIt is optimized for analytical queries, reporting, OLAP, and decision support, rather\r\nthan daily transaction processing.\r\nKey Characteristics\r\n\u2022 Integrated\r\n\u2022 Historical\r\n\u2022 Subject-oriented\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 23\r\n\u2022 Non-volatile\r\n\u2022 Read-optimized\r\n\u2022 Supports analytical queries\r\nComponents of a DW - Data Marts\r\nData marts are smaller, focused subsets of a data warehouse designed for\r\nspecific business functions or departments.\r\nThey provide department-level analytics with simplified and faster access to\r\nrelevant data.\r\nExamples: Sales data mart, finance data mart, marketing data mart, HR data\r\nmart\r\nPurpose\r\n\u2022 Faster reporting and query performance\r\n\u2022 Department-specific analysis\r\n\u2022 Simplified access to relevant data\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 24\r\nComponents of a DW - Data Marts\r\nKey Benefits\r\n\u2022 Faster queries due to smaller, focused\r\ndatasets\r\n\u2022 Simpler access for department-level\r\nreporting without complex systems\r\n\u2022 Better security by isolating sensitive\r\ndepartmental data\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 25\r\nComponents of a DW - Metadata\r\nMetadata is data about data.\r\nIt describes structure, meaning, and rules of data in the warehouse, helping users\r\nfind, understand, and manage data effectively.\r\nExamples: Table names, column definitions, data types, source systems,\r\ntransformation rules\r\nPurpose of Metadata\r\n\u2022 Helps users understand and locate data\r\n\u2022 Supports data governance and consistency\r\n\u2022 Enables data lineage tracking (where data comes from and how it changes)\r\n\u2022 Improves data discovery and usability\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 26\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 27\r\nComponents of a DW - Metadata\r\nComponents of a DW - BI & Access Tools\r\nBI tools form the presentation layer of a data warehouse, designed for business\r\nusers to convert stored data into meaningful insights.\r\nBI tools run on top of the data warehouse and turn transformed historical data into\r\ninteractive insights for business decision-making.\r\nLeading BI Tools\r\n\u2022 Microsoft Power BI: Cost-effective, user-friendly, strong Microsoft ecosystem\r\nintegration\r\n\u2022 Tableau: Advanced visual analytics, ideal for complex and large datasets\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 28\r\nComponents of a DW - BI & Access Tools\r\nMain Functions of BI Tools\r\n\u2022 Dashboards: KPI monitoring using refreshed warehouse data\r\n\u2022 Reports: Structured summaries of business performance\r\n\u2022 Data Visualization: Charts, graphs, heatmaps for pattern discovery\r\n\u2022 OLAP Analysis: Multi-dimensional analysis (slice, dice, drill-down)\r\n\u2022 Ad-hoc Querying: On-demand data exploration without heavy coding\r\n\u2022 Data Mining & Predictive Analytics: Forecast trends using statistical/ML\r\nmodels\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 29\r\nDW Architecture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 30\r\nData Warehouse (DW) 3-Tier Architecture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 31\r\nData Warehouse (DW) 3-Tier Architecture\r\n1. Bottom Tier (Data Layer)\r\nThis is the data storage layer\r\nIncludes:\r\nData Sources (operational systems,\r\nexternal data)\r\nETL processes (Extract,\r\nTransform, Load)\r\nData Warehouse + Data Marts\r\nIt collects raw data, cleans and\r\ntransforms it and store structured\r\nhistorical data\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 32\r\n2. Middle Tier (OLAP Layer)\r\nContains the OLAP server\r\nActs as a processing/logic layer\r\nConverts warehouse data into a fast\r\nanalytical format\r\nActs as a bridge between data storage\r\nand users.\r\nData Warehouse (DW) 3-Tier Architecture\r\n3. Top Tier (Presentation Layer)\r\nThis is the client interface where business users, data analysts, and stakeholders\r\ninteract with the data.\r\nIncludes tools like: Reporting tools, Dashboards, Data mining tools, Analysis tools.\r\nThis layer let users:\r\n\u2022 Query, visualize, and analyse data\r\n\u2022 Converts data into business insights\r\nThe 3-tier DW architecture separates systems into data storage (bottom), processing\r\n(middle), and user interaction (top) to make data analysis efficient, scalable, and\r\nuser-friendly.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 33\r\nA Modern DW Architecture\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 34\r\nData Warehouse vs Data Mart\r\nData Warehouse Data Mart\r\nUsed for organization-wide analysis\r\nand strategic decision-making.\r\nUsed for department-specific analysis\r\nand reporting.\r\nIntegrates data from multiple\r\ndepartments and data sources.\r\nFocuses on the data needs of a single\r\ndepartment or business function.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 35\r\nData Warehouse vs Data Mart\r\nData Warehouse Data Mart\r\nOrganization-wide repository Department- or subject-specific\r\nrepository\r\nStores integrated data from multiple\r\nsources\r\nStores a subset of data for a specific\r\nbusiness area\r\nLarge volume of historical data Smaller volume of focused data\r\nSupports organization-wide decisionmaking Supports departmental decision-making\r\nMore complex to design and maintain Easier and faster to implement\r\nServes multiple departments Serves a single department or business\r\nfunction\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 36\r\nDW vs Data Mart - Example\r\nA retail company plans to expand into a\r\nnew region.\r\nTo make an informed decision,\r\nmanagement needs data from:\r\n\u2022 Sales\r\n\u2022 Marketing\r\n\u2022 Customer loyalty\r\nSince data from the entire organization\r\nis required, an Enterprise Data\r\nWarehouse is the appropriate solution.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 37\r\nThe marketing department wants to\r\nanalyse:\r\n\u2022 Campaign performance\r\n\u2022 Customer demographics\r\n\u2022 Website traffic\r\n\u2022 Conversion rates\r\nSince only marketing-related data is\r\nrequired, a Marketing Data Mart is\r\nsufficient.\r\n\u2022 Inventory\r\n\u2022 Supply chain\r\n\u2022 Finance\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\nThe retail company has successfully built an Enterprise Data Warehouse\r\n(EDW). The warehouse contains integrated historical data from:\r\n\u2022 Customers\r\n\u2022 Sales transactions\r\n\u2022 Products\r\n\u2022 Inventory\r\n\u2022 Payments\r\n\u2022 Delivery records\r\n\u2022 Website interactions\r\nThe company now wants to provide faster and simpler analytics for different\r\nbusiness teams.\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 38\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\nBusiness Requirements\r\n1. Sales Department\r\nThe Sales Manager wants answers to:\r\n1. Which products generate the highest\r\nrevenue?\r\n2. Which regions have the best sales\r\nperformance?\r\n3. How are monthly sales changing?\r\n4. Which sales channels perform\r\nbetter?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 39\r\n2. Marketing Department\r\nThe Marketing Manager wants answers\r\nto:\r\n1. Who are our most valuable\r\ncustomers?\r\n2. Which campaigns attract more\r\ncustomers?\r\n3. What customer groups should\r\nreceive promotions?\r\n4. What are customer buying patterns?\r\nActivity: Design a Data Warehouse\r\n3. Inventory Management\r\nDepartment\r\nThe Inventory Manager wants answers\r\nto:\r\n1. Which products are running out of\r\nstock?\r\n2. Which products are slow-moving?\r\n3. How much inventory is needed for\r\nfuture demand?\r\n4. Which suppliers perform better?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 40\r\n1. Decide whether each department\r\nshould directly query the\r\nEnterprise Data Warehouse or\r\nuse a Data Mart.\r\n2. If you are using Data Marts, why\r\nnot allow every department to\r\nquery the complete Enterprise\r\nData Warehouse?\r\n3. Design the required Data Marts.\r\n4. Does a Data Mart create new\r\ndata?\r\nDW Solution for a Coffee Shop Chain\r\nYou are hired as a Data Warehouse Designer for a growing coffee shop chain.\r\nThe company has several branches across the country and wants to use data\r\nanalytics to improve business decisions.\r\nCurrently, data is stored in different operational systems. Management wants\r\nanswers to questions such as:\r\n1. Which drinks are the most popular?\r\n2. Which branches generate the highest revenue?\r\n3. What are the busiest times of the day?\r\n4. Which customers are most loyal?\r\n5. Which products should be promoted?\r\n6. How much inventory should each branch maintain?\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 41\r\nDesign a high-level Data Warehouse solution for the coffee shop chain.\r\nYour design should identify:\r\n1. Data Sources\r\nIdentify possible operational systems that can provide data for the data warehouse.\r\n2. ETL Activities\r\nIdentify possible Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) activities required before\r\nstoring data in the warehouse.\r\n3. Data Marts\r\nIdentify possible department/business-specific data marts that can be created\r\nfrom the data warehouse.\r\nFor each data mart, mention:\r\n\u2022 Purpose\r\n\u2022 Users\r\n\u2022 Type of analysis supported\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 42\r\nNext Lecture\r\n1. Importance of data modeling in data warehousing\r\n2. Dimensional modelling techniques\r\n3. Star schema design and Snowflake schema design\r\n4. Facts, dimensions, hierarchies and measures\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 43\r\nThank you\r\nIT 3101 - DWBI 44"}], "files": [{"file_uuid": "fd2b29c7-0e72-4a09-b18d-2c249e3b58b4", "file_name": ""}], PAGE_WIDTH_DXA = 12240;\nconst PAGE_HEIGHT_DXA = 15840;\nconst MARGIN = 1080;\nconst USABLE_WIDTH = PAGE_WIDTH_DXA - MARGIN * 2;\n\nfunction h1(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, spacing: { before: 300, after: 150 } });\n}\nfunction h2(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_2, spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 } });\n}\nfunction h3(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({ text, heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_3, spacing: { before: 200, after: 100 } });\n}\nfunction p(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold, italics: !!opts.italics })],\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  });\n}\nfunction bullet(text, level = 0) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text })],\n    numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level },\n    spacing: { after: 60 },\n  });\n}\nfunction optionLine(letter, text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    children: [\n      new TextRun({ text: `${letter}) `, bold: true }),\n      new TextRun({ text }),\n    ],\n    spacing: { after: 40 },\n    indent: { left: 360 },\n  });\n}\nfunction questionBlock(num, stem, options) {\n  const blocks = [];\n  blocks.push(\n    new Paragraph({\n      children: [new TextRun({ text: `Q${num}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: stem })],\n      spacing: { before: 220, after: 80 },\n    })\n  );\n  const letters = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"];\n  options.forEach((opt, i) => blocks.push(optionLine(letters[i], opt)));\n  return blocks;\n}\nfunction hr() {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    text: \"\",\n    border: { bottom: { color: \"999999\", space: 1, style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6 } },\n    spacing: { after: 160 },\n  });\n}\nfunction cell(text, opts = {}) {\n  return new TableCell({\n    width: { size: opts.width || 2000, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    shading: opts.shade ? { fill: opts.shade, type: ShadingType.CLEAR, color: \"auto\" } : undefined,\n    children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, bold: !!opts.bold })] })],\n  });\n}\n\n// ---------- MCQ DATA (Lecture 02) ----------\n// Correct-answer letters are deliberately varied across positions (not clustered).\nconst mcqs = [\n  {\n    stem: \"A company's sales database processes thousands of small transactions per second and is heavily normalized to avoid redundancy. Which statements correctly contrast this with a data warehouse?\",\n    options: [\n      \"The data warehouse would typically be denormalized rather than heavily normalized\",\n      \"Both systems are equally optimized for the same type of workload\",\n      \"The data warehouse favors fewer, more complex analytical queries\",\n      \"The operational database is optimized for daily transactions, not decision-making\",\n      \"The data warehouse relies primarily on frequent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the retail activity, management cannot directly run analytics on the Customer Management, Payment, and Inventory systems. Which reasons correctly justify this limitation?\",\n    options: [\n      \"These systems are analytical databases not meant for daily transactions\",\n      \"Running heavy analytical queries could disrupt daily transaction processing\",\n      \"These operational systems are optimized for transactions, not complex analysis\",\n      \"Data across these systems is already integrated and consistent for analysis\",\n      \"Each system holds only a fragment of the data needed for a full business view\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A company integrating CRM, ERP, and legacy systems discovers duplicate customer records, inconsistent schemas, and difficulty meeting a business unit's low-latency reporting need. Which data integration challenges are illustrated?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Real-time data requirements, since low-latency reporting is needed\",\n      \"Poor data quality, due to duplicate records\",\n      \"This scenario reflects no meaningful integration challenge\",\n      \"Incompatible data formats and structures, due to inconsistent schemas\",\n      \"Security and compliance concerns, since encryption keys were mismatched\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"An engineer builds a pipeline that collects raw sales data from source systems, cleans and standardizes it, then stores it into the warehouse. Which statements correctly describe this process?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the ETL process: Extract, Transform, Load\",\n      \"The Transform step focuses on cleaning, standardizing, and integrating data\",\n      \"The Load step stores the final data into the data warehouse\",\n      \"This process is only used for retrieving reports, not preparing data\",\n      \"The Extract step is responsible for cleaning and standardizing values\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Before loading sales data into a warehouse, an engineer routes it through a temporary buffer where duplicates are removed and formats are standardized. Which statements correctly describe this component?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is the Staging Area\",\n      \"It keeps raw data copies useful for debugging and recovery\",\n      \"It replaces the need for a central data warehouse entirely\",\n      \"It avoids heavy processing load directly inside the data warehouse\",\n      \"It is the final destination where business users run their reports\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly describe the Central Data Warehouse as a component of the overall architecture?\",\n    options: [\n      \"It acts as a single source of truth, eliminating data silos\",\n      \"It is primarily optimized for frequent transactional updates\",\n      \"It stores integrated, historical, and subject-oriented data\",\n      \"It is optimized for analytical queries, reporting, and OLAP\",\n      \"It is meant to replace the staging area's cleaning function entirely\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A marketing team is given a smaller, focused copy of warehouse data containing only campaign, customer, and website traffic information for faster reporting. Which statements correctly describe this setup?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is an example of a Data Mart\",\n      \"It supports faster queries due to a smaller, focused dataset\",\n      \"It stores a completely different dataset unrelated to the main warehouse\",\n      \"It provides simplified, department-specific access to relevant data\",\n      \"It always contains more historical data than the central warehouse itself\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A data governance team documents table names, column definitions, data types, and transformation rules used throughout the warehouse. Which statements correctly describe the purpose of this documentation?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This is Metadata \u2014 data about data\",\n      \"It supports data lineage tracking of where data comes from and how it changes\",\n      \"It replaces the need for a staging area in the ETL pipeline\",\n      \"It helps users understand, locate, and manage warehouse data\",\n      \"It is used exclusively for encrypting sensitive customer records\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A manager uses a dashboard to monitor KPIs, drills down into regional sales using OLAP, and runs an ad-hoc query without writing code. Which statements correctly describe these activities?\",\n    options: [\n      \"These are functions typically provided by BI & Access Tools\",\n      \"Drilling down into regional sales is an example of OLAP analysis within a BI tool\",\n      \"Ad-hoc querying allows on-demand exploration without heavy coding\",\n      \"These functions are performed directly on the operational transaction database\",\n      \"Dashboards use warehouse data refreshed for KPI monitoring\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the 3-tier DW architecture, which statements correctly describe the Bottom Tier (Data Layer)?\",\n    options: [\n      \"It includes data sources, ETL processes, and the data warehouse/data marts\",\n      \"It is where business users directly build dashboards and visualizations\",\n      \"It collects, cleans, transforms, and stores structured historical data\",\n      \"It contains the OLAP server that converts data into a fast analytical format\",\n      \"It represents the raw and processed data storage foundation of the architecture\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the 3-tier DW architecture, which statements correctly describe the Middle Tier (OLAP Layer)?\",\n    options: [\n      \"It contains the OLAP server acting as a processing/logic layer\",\n      \"It is the layer where raw operational data is first extracted\",\n      \"It acts as a bridge between data storage and the presentation layer\",\n      \"It converts warehouse data into a fast analytical format\",\n      \"It is where reporting tools and dashboards are directly installed for end users\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the 3-tier DW architecture, which statements correctly describe the Top Tier (Presentation Layer)?\",\n    options: [\n      \"It is where business users and analysts interact with the data\",\n      \"It includes reporting tools, dashboards, and data mining/analysis tools\",\n      \"It performs the initial extraction of raw data from source systems\",\n      \"It lets users query, visualize, and analyse data to generate insights\",\n      \"It stores the structured historical data used for analytical queries\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Which statements correctly distinguish a Data Warehouse from a Data Mart?\",\n    options: [\n      \"A data warehouse supports organization-wide, strategic decision-making\",\n      \"A data mart is generally easier and faster to implement than a full warehouse\",\n      \"A data mart typically integrates data from every department across the company\",\n      \"A data warehouse integrates data from multiple departments and sources\",\n      \"A data mart usually serves a single department or business function\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"A retail company is expanding into a new region and needs combined data from Sales, Marketing, Customer Loyalty, Inventory, Supply Chain, and Finance to make the decision. Which reasoning best justifies the chosen solution?\",\n    options: [\n      \"An Enterprise Data Warehouse is appropriate since organization-wide data is required\",\n      \"A single departmental Data Mart would be sufficient for this decision\",\n      \"The decision spans multiple business functions, not just one department\",\n      \"This scenario needs integrated data from across the whole organization\",\n      \"A Data Mart could fully replace the Data Warehouse in this situation\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The marketing department wants to analyse campaign performance, customer demographics, website traffic, and conversion rates only. Which reasoning best justifies the appropriate solution?\",\n    options: [\n      \"A Marketing Data Mart is sufficient since only marketing-related data is needed\",\n      \"An Enterprise Data Warehouse query is strictly required for this narrow need\",\n      \"This need is department-specific rather than organization-wide\",\n      \"A Data Mart offers simplified, faster access to the relevant subset of data\",\n      \"This scenario requires building an entirely separate data warehouse from scratch\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"In the retail EDW activity, the Sales, Marketing, and Inventory departments each have distinct reporting needs (revenue by product/region, campaign/customer analysis, stock/supplier performance). Which approach and reasoning are most appropriate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Each department should generally use its own dedicated Data Mart\",\n      \"Every department should instead query the full Enterprise Data Warehouse directly for all needs\",\n      \"Data Marts provide faster, simpler, department-focused access to relevant subsets\",\n      \"Using Data Marts helps isolate sensitive departmental data for better security\",\n      \"Using Data Marts would require duplicating the entire EDW for every department\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The retail company asks: 'why not allow every department to query the complete Enterprise Data Warehouse directly instead of using Data Marts?' Which reasons justify preferring Data Marts?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Querying the full EDW directly could be slower due to its size and complexity\",\n      \"Data Marts simplify access to only the data relevant to each department\",\n      \"Data Marts help isolate and better secure sensitive departmental data\",\n      \"The full EDW always contains completely different data than any Data Mart\",\n      \"Direct EDW queries would guarantee better performance than any Data Mart\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Regarding the question 'Does a Data Mart create new data?' which statements are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"No, a Data Mart is a subset of existing warehouse data, not a new data source\",\n      \"A Data Mart generates entirely new business data of its own\",\n      \"A Data Mart reorganizes and simplifies existing data for a specific audience\",\n      \"The underlying data still originates from the central Enterprise Data Warehouse\",\n      \"Creating a Data Mart eliminates the need for the Enterprise Data Warehouse\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Raw Sales System records show: Order 1001 with Customer_ID 'C101'; Order 1002 with Customer_ID '103' (no prefix); Order 1003 appearing twice with slightly different amount formats ('Rs. 12000' vs '12000'). Which data quality problems are present?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Inconsistent Customer_ID formatting (with and without the 'C' prefix)\",\n      \"All records are fully clean and ready for direct warehouse loading\",\n      \"A likely duplicate record for Order 1003\",\n      \"Inconsistent formatting of the Amount field (currency symbol vs plain number)\",\n      \"The Order_Date column contains no inconsistencies at all\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The Sales System's Order_Date values appear as '01/05/25', '2025-05-01', and 'May 2 2025' across different records. Which statements correctly describe this issue and its handling?\",\n    options: [\n      \"This reflects inconsistent date formats across source records\",\n      \"Dates should be standardized into a single consistent format before loading\",\n      \"This inconsistency has no impact on downstream time-based analysis\",\n      \"Such inconsistencies are typically resolved during the Transform step of ETL\",\n      \"This issue should be left unresolved and loaded as-is into the warehouse\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"The Customer System shows: 'C101, John Smith, Colombo' and separately '101, JOHN SMITH, Colombo', plus 'C103, Amali Dias, GALLE'. Which data quality issues are present?\",\n    options: [\n      \"A likely duplicate customer record represented inconsistently (C101 vs 101)\",\n      \"Inconsistent capitalization in the Customer_Name field\",\n      \"All city names are already in a fully standardized format\",\n      \"Inconsistent capitalization in the City field (e.g., 'GALLE')\",\n      \"There are no naming convention issues in this dataset\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"When designing transformation rules to convert this raw sales/customer data into warehouse-ready data, which rules would be appropriate?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Standardize Customer_ID format consistently across all records\",\n      \"Leave duplicate records unresolved so historical detail is preserved as-is\",\n      \"Convert all date values into a single standard date format\",\n      \"Standardize text casing (e.g., proper case or uppercase) for names and cities\",\n      \"Store the Amount field with mixed currency symbols and plain numbers as received\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"After transformation, the final Sales Fact table is being designed for the warehouse. Which characteristics would be appropriate for this fact table?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Standardized, clean Customer_ID and Product_ID references\",\n      \"Retaining the original inconsistent date text formats unchanged\",\n      \"A consistently formatted numeric Amount field without mixed currency symbols\",\n      \"Deduplicated records so the same order isn't counted twice\",\n      \"No relationship at all to any customer or product dimension\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"Designing a Data Warehouse for a coffee shop chain, the team identifies POS systems, an online ordering app, a loyalty program system, and a supplier/inventory system as inputs. Which statements about this design step are correct?\",\n    options: [\n      \"These operational systems serve as the Data Sources feeding the warehouse\",\n      \"These systems alone are sufficient to directly answer 'which branches generate the highest revenue' without any integration\",\n      \"Data from these systems is likely scattered and needs extraction and integration\",\n      \"Some of this data may include both internal systems and external/loyalty platforms\",\n      \"These systems already store fully integrated, historical, analysis-ready data\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    stem: \"For the coffee shop chain, the team plans ETL activities such as combining sales records from POS and the online app, and cleaning inconsistent product names before loading. Which statements correctly reflect appropriate ETL activities and resulting Data Marts?\",\n    options: [\n      \"Extracting and cleaning inconsistent product names is part of the Transform step\",\n      \"Combining POS and online app sales data supports building an integrated Sales Data Mart\",\n      \"No transformation is needed since POS and app data are already identical in format\",\n      \"An Inventory Data Mart could support answering how much stock each branch should maintain\",\n      \"ETL activities are unnecessary once data marts have been designed\",\n    ],\n  },\n];\n\nconst answerKey = [\n  \"a, c, d\", \"b, c, e\", \"a, b, d\", \"a, b, c\", \"a, b, d\",\n  \"a, c, d\", \"a, b, d\", \"a, b, d\", \"a, b, c, e\", \"a, c, e\",\n  \"a, c, d\", \"a, b, d\", \"a, b, e\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, c, d\",\n  \"a, c, d\", \"a, b, c\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, b, d\",\n  \"a, b, d\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, c, d\", \"a, b, d\",\n];\n\n// ---------- BUILD DOCUMENT ----------\nconst children = [];\n\nchildren.push(\n  new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text: \"IT3101 \u2013 Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence\", bold: true, size: 40 })],\n    heading: HeadingLevel.TITLE,\n    alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER,\n    spacing: { after: 100 },\n  }),\n  new Paragraph({\n    children: [new TextRun({ text: \"Lecture 02 Exam Prep: DW Components, Architecture, Integration & Data Marts\", italics: true, size: 26 })],\n    alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER,\n    spacing: { after: 400 },\n  })\n);\n\n// SECTION 1\nchildren.push(h1(\"Section 1: MCQs (25 Questions \u2014 Multiple Correct Answers)\"));\nchildren.push(p(\"Instructions: Each question has 2\u20134 correct options.
